Can also be specified in the URL</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>pop_timeout</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>1</code></td>\n<td>BRPOP timeout in seconds before retrying</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h4>Data Flow</h4>\n<pre><code>Producer                  Redis                    Worker (queue-subscriber)\n   │                        │                              │\n   │── LPUSH queue ────────&gt;│                              │\n   │                        │&lt;──────── BRPOP queue ────────│\n   │                        │                              │── run_workflow()\n   │                        │&lt;── SET {name}:{wf}:{rid} ───│\n   │                        │&lt;── PUBLISH {name}:{wf}:{rid} │\n   │&lt;── GET {name}:{wf}:{rid}│                             │\n   │&lt;── SUBSCRIBE {name}:*  │                              │\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Task Message Format (Producer → Queue)</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;user-task-123&quot;,\n  &quot;run_id&quot;: &quot;01JXYZ...&quot;,\n  &quot;input&quot;: { &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Hello&quot; }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li><code>task_id</code>: Logical task identifier (remains the same across retries)</li>\n<li><code>run_id</code>: Execution instance identifier (unique per publish)</li>\n<li><code>input</code>: Workflow input data</li>\n</ul>\n<h4>Result Message Format (Worker → Redis)</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;user-task-123&quot;,\n  &quot;run_id&quot;: &quot;01JXYZ...&quot;,\n  &quot;status&quot;: &quot;completed&quot;,\n  &quot;output&quot;: { &quot;message&quot;: &quot;Hello!&quot; },\n  &quot;worker_id&quot;: &quot;01JXY...&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Result status values: <code>completed</code>, <code>failed</code>, <code>interrupted</code></p>\n<p>When <code>interrupted</code>, the result includes an <code>interrupt</code> field:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;status&quot;: &quot;interrupted&quot;,\n  &quot;interrupt&quot;: {\n    &quot;job_id&quot;: &quot;review-step&quot;,\n    &quot;phase&quot;: &quot;before&quot;,\n    &quot;message&quot;: &quot;Please review before proceeding.&quot;,\n    &quot;metadata&quot;: {}\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Redis Key/Channel Reference</h4>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key/Channel</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>{name}:{workflow_id}</code></td>\n<td>List</td>\n<td>Task queue (LPUSH/BRPOP)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>{name}:{workflow_id}:{run_id}</code></td>\n<td>String</td>\n<td>Result storage (with TTL)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>{name}:{workflow_id}:{run_id}</code></td>\n<td>Pub/Sub</td>\n<td>Result notification channel</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h4>Examples</h4>\n<p><strong>Single workflow worker:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: queue-subscriber\n  driver: redis\n  url: redis://localhost:6379\n  workflow: my-workflow\n  max_concurrent_count: 3\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Multi-workflow worker:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: queue-subscriber\n  driver: redis\n  url: redis://localhost:6379\n  workflows:\n    - text-summary\n    - translation\n  max_concurrent_count: 5\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Worker with custom queue and result settings:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: queue-subscriber\n  driver: redis\n  host: redis.internal\n  port: 6379\n  password: ${env.REDIS_PASSWORD}\n  database: 2\n  name: myapp:tasks\n  result_ttl: 7200\n  worker_id: gpu-worker-01\n  workflows:\n    - image-generation\n  max_concurrent_count: 2\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>TLS connection using URL:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: queue-subscriber\n  driver: redis\n  url: rediss://:${env.REDIS_PASSWORD}@redis.internal:6380/2\n  workflows:\n    - image-generation\n  max_concurrent_count: 2\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>TLS connection using host/port:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: queue-subscriber\n  driver: redis\n  host: redis.internal\n  port: 6380\n  secure: true\n  password: ${env.REDIS_PASSWORD}\n  database: 2\n  workflows:\n    - image-generation\n  max_concurrent_count: 2\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Common Configuration Options</h2>\n<h3>Core Settings</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>name</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Optional name to identify the controller</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>type</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Controller type: <code>http-server</code>, <code>mcp-server</code>, or <code>queue-subscriber</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>host</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>0.0.0.0</code></td>\n<td>Host address to bind the server to</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>port</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>8080</code></td>\n<td>Port number for the server</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>base_path</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Base path prefix for all routes/endpoints</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>HTTP Server Specific</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>origins</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;*&quot;</code></td>\n<td>CORS allowed origins (comma-separated string)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Concurrency &amp; Threading</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_concurrent_count</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>1</code></td>\n<td>Maximum number of tasks that can execute concurrently</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>threaded</code></td>\n<td>boolean</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Whether to run tasks in separate threads</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Runtime Configuration</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>runtime</code></td>\n<td>object/string</td>\n<td><code>native</code></td>\n<td>Runtime environment settings</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Runtime Options:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>native</code> - Run directly on the host system</li>\n<li><code>docker</code> - Run in Docker containers</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Examples:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># Simple string format\nruntime: native\n\n# Object format with additional configuration\nruntime:\n  type: docker\n  # Additional docker-specific options can be added here\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Web UI Configuration</h2>\n<p>The <code>webui</code> section configures an optional web interface for interacting with workflows.</p>\n<h3>Common Web UI Settings</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>driver</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>gradio</code></td>\n<td>Web UI rendering mode</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>host</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>0.0.0.0</code></td>\n<td>Host address for the Web UI server</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>port</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>8081</code></td>\n<td>Port number for the Web UI</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Web UI Drivers</h3>\n<h4>Gradio (<code>gradio</code>)</h4>\n<p>Creates an interactive web interface using Gradio.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">webui:\n  driver: gradio\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8081\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Static (<code>static</code>)</h4>\n<p>Serves static HTML/CSS/JS files.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">webui:\n  driver: static\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8081\n  static_dir: webui    # Directory containing static files\n</code></pre>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>static_dir</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>webui</code></td>\n<td>Directory containing static HTML/CSS/JS files</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h4>Dynamic (<code>dynamic</code>)</h4>\n<p>Runs a custom web server command.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">webui:\n  driver: dynamic\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8081\n  command: npm start              # Command to start the web server\n  server_dir: webui/server        # Directory with server source code\n  static_dir: webui/static        # Directory with static files\n</code></pre>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>command</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Command to start the web UI server</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>server_dir</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>webui/server</code></td>\n<td>Directory containing server source code and entry point</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>static_dir</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>webui/static</code></td>\n<td>Directory containing static HTML/CSS/JS files</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Queue Dispatch Configuration</h2>\n<p>The <code>queue</code> section configures optional queue-based workflow dispatch. When configured, <code>run_workflow()</code> delegates execution to remote workers via a message queue instead of running workflows locally. This enables distributed deployment where an HTTP/MCP entry point dispatches work to separate queue-subscriber workers.</p>\n<pre><code>Client → [HTTP Server] → Redis LPUSH → [Worker A or B] → Redis PUBLISH → [HTTP Server] → Client\n         (entry point)                   (queue-subscriber)                 (result)\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Common Queue Dispatch Settings</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>driver</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Queue backend driver. Currently supported: <code>redis</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>name</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>model-compose:tasks</code></td>\n<td>Base name for task queues. Queue key: <code>{name}:{workflow_id}</code>. Result key: <code>{name}:{workflow_id}:{run_id}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>timeout</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>0</code></td>\n<td>Maximum time in seconds to wait for a result from the queue. <code>0</code> means no limit</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Redis Driver Settings</h3>\n<p>Connection can be configured using either <code>url</code> or <code>host</code>/<code>port</code>/<code>secure</code> fields. If both <code>url</code> and <code>host</code> are provided, validation will fail.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>url</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Redis connection URL (e.g., <code>redis://localhost:6379</code>, <code>rediss://localhost:6379</code> for TLS). Mutually exclusive with <code>host</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>host</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>localhost</code></td>\n<td>Redis server hostname or IP address. Mutually exclusive with <code>url</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>port</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>6379</code></td>\n<td>Redis server port number (1-65535)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>secure</code></td>\n<td>boolean</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Use TLS/SSL for connections (equivalent to <code>rediss://</code> protocol)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>database</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>0</code></td>\n<td>Redis database number (0-15)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>password</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Redis password. Can also be specified in the URL</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Examples</h3>\n<p><strong>Basic queue dispatch with URL:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  adapter:\n    type: http-server\n    port: 8080\n  queue:\n    driver: redis\n    url: redis://localhost:6379\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Queue dispatch with host/port:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  adapter:\n    type: http-server\n    port: 8080\n  queue:\n    driver: redis\n    host: redis.internal\n    port: 6379\n    password: ${env.REDIS_PASSWORD}\n    database: 2\n    name: myapp:tasks\n    timeout: 600\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>TLS connection:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  adapter:\n    type: http-server\n    port: 8080\n  queue:\n    driver: redis\n    url: rediss://:${env.REDIS_PASSWORD}@redis.internal:6380/2\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Data Flow</h3>\n<pre><code>HTTP/MCP Adapter           ControllerService           Redis              Worker (queue-subscriber)\n    │                            │                       │                        │\n    │── run_workflow() ────────&gt; │                       │                        │\n    │                            │── LPUSH queue ──────&gt; │                        │\n    │                            │── SUBSCRIBE result ─&gt; │                        │\n    │                            │                       │&lt;──── BRPOP queue ──────│\n    │                            │                       │                        │── run_workflow()\n    │                            │                       │&lt;── SET+PUBLISH result ─│\n    │                            │&lt;── result message ────│                        │\n    │&lt;── TaskState ──────────────│                       │                        │\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note</strong>: The <code>queue</code> configuration shares the same message format and Redis key conventions as <code>queue-subscriber</code>. The entry point pushes tasks to <code>{name}:{workflow_id}</code> and subscribes to <code>{name}:{workflow_id}:{run_id}</code> for results. Workers (queue-subscriber) consume from the same queues and publish results to the same keys.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Complete Examples</h2>\n<h3>HTTP Server with Gradio UI</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  name: my-api-server\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /api\n  origins: http://localhost:3000,https://myapp.com\n  max_concurrent_count: 5\n  threaded: true\n  webui:\n    driver: gradio\n    port: 8081\n</code></pre>\n<h3>MCP Server with Static UI</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: mcp-server\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /mcp\n  runtime: docker\n  webui:\n    driver: static\n    port: 8081\n    static_dir: custom-webui\n</code></pre>\n<h3>HTTP Server with Custom Dynamic UI</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  max_concurrent_count: 10\n  webui:\n    driver: dynamic\n    port: 8081\n    command: node server.js\n    server_dir: frontend/server\n    static_dir: frontend/dist\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Queue Subscriber with Redis</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: queue-subscriber\n  driver: redis\n  url: redis://localhost:6379\n  workflows:\n    - image-generation\n    - text-summary\n  max_concurrent_count: 4\n  result_ttl: 3600\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Distributed Deployment (Entry Point + Workers)</h3>\n<p><strong>Entry point server</strong> (<code>model-compose.yml</code> on server A):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  adapter:\n    type: http-server\n    port: 8080\n  queue:\n    driver: redis\n    url: redis://redis.internal:6379\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Worker server</strong> (<code>model-compose.yml</code> on server B &amp; C):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  adapter:\n    type: queue-subscriber\n    driver: redis\n    url: redis://redis.internal:6379\n    max_concurrent_count: 4\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Usage Notes</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Port Conflicts</strong>: Ensure the controller port and webui port are different to avoid conflicts.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>CORS Configuration</strong>: For HTTP servers, configure <code>origins</code> appropriately for your client applications.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Concurrency</strong>: Higher <code>max_concurrent_count</code> values allow more simultaneous workflow executions but consume more resources.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Base Paths</strong>: Use <code>base_path</code> to namespace your API routes, especially useful when running behind a reverse proxy.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Runtime Selection</strong>: Choose <code>docker</code> runtime for better isolation, <code>native</code> for better performance and simpler deployment.</p>\n</li>\n</ol>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Controller Configuration Reference"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "reference/compose/gateway",
      "html": "<h1>Gateway Configuration Reference</h1>\n<p>Gateways provide tunneling services that expose local ports to external networks. They enable external access to your model-compose services by creating secure tunnels through firewalls and NAT configurations.</p>\n<h2>Basic Structure</h2>\n<h3>Single Gateway</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel | ssh-tunnel\n  runtime: native | docker\n  port: 8090                    # Single port\n  # OR\n  port:                         # Multiple ports\n    - 8090\n    - 8091\n    - 8092\n  # ... type-specific configuration\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Multiple Gateways</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateways:\n  - type: http-tunnel\n    driver: ngrok\n    port: 8080\n    # ... configuration for first gateway\n    \n  - type: ssh-tunnel\n    port: 8090\n    connection:\n      # ... SSH connection configuration\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Gateway Types</h2>\n<h3>HTTP Tunnel (<code>http-tunnel</code>)</h3>\n<p>Creates HTTP tunnels using third-party services like ngrok or Cloudflare tunnels to expose local services to the internet.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: ngrok | cloudflare\n  port: 8080              # Local port to tunnel\n  runtime: native\n</code></pre>\n<h3>SSH Tunnel (<code>ssh-tunnel</code>)</h3>\n<p>Creates SSH tunnels to expose local services through a remote SSH server.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: ssh-tunnel\n  port: 8080              # Local port to tunnel\n  connection:\n    host: remote-server.com\n    port: 22\n    auth:\n      type: keyfile | password\n      username: user\n      # ... auth configuration\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Common Configuration Options</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>type</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Gateway type: <code>http-tunnel</code> or <code>ssh-tunnel</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>runtime</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>native</code></td>\n<td>Runtime environment: <code>native</code> or <code>docker</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>port</code></td>\n<td>integer or array</td>\n<td><code>8090</code></td>\n<td>Local port(s) to tunnel through the gateway. Can be a single port number or an array of ports</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>HTTP Tunnel Configuration</h2>\n<h3>Ngrok Driver</h3>\n<p>Uses ngrok service to create HTTP tunnels.</p>\n<p><strong>Single port:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: ngrok\n  port: 8080\n  runtime: native\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Multiple ports:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: ngrok\n  port:\n    - 8080\n    - 8090\n    - 3000\n  runtime: native\n</code></pre>\n<p>Each port gets its own unique public URL (e.g., <code>https://abc123.ngrok.io</code>, <code>https://def456.ngrok.io</code>, <code>https://ghi789.ngrok.io</code>).</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>driver</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Must be <code>ngrok</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>port</code></td>\n<td>integer or array</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Local port(s) to expose. Can be single port or array of ports</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>ngrok CLI must be installed and configured</li>\n<li>ngrok account and authtoken (for persistent tunnels)</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Accessing Public URLs:</strong>\nUse <code>${gateway:PORT.public_url}</code> to access the public URL for each port in your configuration.</p>\n<h3>Cloudflare Driver</h3>\n<p>Uses Cloudflare tunnels to expose local services.</p>\n<p><strong>Single port:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: cloudflare\n  port: 8080\n  runtime: native\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Multiple ports:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: cloudflare\n  port:\n    - 8080\n    - 8090\n    - 3000\n  runtime: native\n</code></pre>\n<p>Each port gets its own unique public URL (e.g., <code>https://abc-def.trycloudflare.com</code>, <code>https://ghi-jkl.trycloudflare.com</code>).</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>driver</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Must be <code>cloudflare</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>port</code></td>\n<td>integer or array</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Local port(s) to expose. Can be single port or array of ports</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Cloudflare tunnel CLI (cloudflared) must be installed</li>\n<li>Cloudflare account with tunnel configured</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Accessing Public URLs:</strong>\nUse <code>${gateway:PORT.public_url}</code> to access the public URL for each port in your configuration.</p>\n<h2>SSH Tunnel Configuration</h2>\n<p>Creates secure SSH tunnels through remote servers.</p>\n<p><strong>Single port:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: ssh-tunnel\n  port:\n    - &quot;9834:8080&quot;              # Remote port 9834 -&gt; Local port 8080\n  connection:\n    host: tunnel-server.example.com\n    port: 22\n    auth:\n      type: keyfile\n      username: tunnel-user\n      keyfile: &quot;/path/to/private/key&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Multiple ports:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: ssh-tunnel\n  port:\n    - &quot;9834:8080&quot;              # Remote port 9834 -&gt; Local port 8080\n    - &quot;9835:8090&quot;              # Remote port 9835 -&gt; Local port 8090\n    - &quot;9836:3000&quot;              # Remote port 9836 -&gt; Local port 3000\n  connection:\n    host: tunnel-server.example.com\n    port: 22\n    auth:\n      type: keyfile\n      username: tunnel-user\n      keyfile: &quot;/path/to/private/key&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Port Formats:</strong></p>\n<p>The <code>port</code> field supports multiple flexible formats:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Integer</strong>: <code>8080</code> → Forwards remote port 8080 to localhost:8080</li>\n<li><strong>Port:Port</strong>: <code>&quot;9834:8080&quot;</code> → Forwards remote port 9834 to localhost:8080</li>\n<li><strong>Port:Host</strong>: <code>&quot;8080:192.168.1.107&quot;</code> → Forwards remote port 8080 to 192.168.1.107:8080</li>\n<li><strong>Port:Host:Port</strong>: <code>&quot;9834:192.168.1.107:3000&quot;</code> → Forwards remote port 9834 to 192.168.1.107:3000</li>\n</ol>\n<p>Multiple port mappings can be specified as an array.</p>\n<p><strong>Accessing Public Addresses:</strong>\nUse <code>${gateway:LOCAL_PORT.public_address}</code> to access the public address (returns <code>remote-host:remote-port</code>).</p>\n<h3>Connection Settings</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>connection</code></td>\n<td>object</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>SSH connection configuration</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>connection.host</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Host address of the SSH server</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>connection.port</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>22</code></td>\n<td>SSH server port</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>connection.auth</code></td>\n<td>object</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>SSH authentication configuration</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Authentication Configuration</h3>\n<h4>Keyfile Authentication</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">auth:\n  type: keyfile\n  username: ssh-user\n  keyfile: &quot;/home/user/.ssh/id_rsa&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>type</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Must be <code>keyfile</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>username</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>SSH username</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>keyfile</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Path to private key file</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h4>Password Authentication</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">auth:\n  type: password\n  username: ssh-user\n  password: secure-password\n</code></pre>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>type</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Must be <code>password</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>username</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>SSH username</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>password</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>SSH password</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Configuration Examples</h2>\n<h3>Simple Ngrok Tunnel (Single Port)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: ngrok\n  port: 8080\n</code></pre>\n<p>Exposes local port 8080 through ngrok tunnel with a random public URL.</p>\n<h3>Ngrok Tunnel with Multiple Ports</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: ngrok\n  port:\n    - 8080    # Main API\n    - 8081    # Admin panel\n    - 3000    # Frontend app\n</code></pre>\n<p>Exposes three local ports through separate ngrok tunnels. Access URLs via:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>${gateway:8080.public_url}</code> for the main API</li>\n<li><code>${gateway:8081.public_url}</code> for the admin panel</li>\n<li><code>${gateway:3000.public_url}</code> for the frontend app</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Cloudflare Tunnel (Single Port)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: cloudflare\n  port: 8080\n  runtime: native\n</code></pre>\n<p>Creates a Cloudflare tunnel for local port 8080.</p>\n<h3>Cloudflare Tunnel with Multiple Ports</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: cloudflare\n  port:\n    - 8090    # Callback listener\n    - 8091    # Status endpoint\n    - 3000    # Web interface\n  runtime: native\n</code></pre>\n<p>Each port gets its own Cloudflare tunnel URL.</p>\n<h3>SSH Tunnel with Key Authentication (Single Port)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: ssh-tunnel\n  port:\n    - &quot;9834:8080&quot;    # Remote 9834 -&gt; Local 8080\n  runtime: native\n  connection:\n    host: bastion.example.com\n    port: 22\n    auth:\n      type: keyfile\n      username: deploy\n      keyfile: ~/.ssh/tunnel_key\n</code></pre>\n<p>Creates an SSH tunnel through bastion.example.com using SSH key authentication.</p>\n<h3>SSH Tunnel with Multiple Ports</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: ssh-tunnel\n  port:\n    - &quot;9834:8080&quot;    # Remote 9834 -&gt; Local 8080\n    - &quot;9835:8090&quot;    # Remote 9835 -&gt; Local 8090\n    - &quot;9836:3000&quot;    # Remote 9836 -&gt; Local 3000\n  connection:\n    host: bastion.example.com\n    port: 22\n    auth:\n      type: keyfile\n      username: deploy\n      keyfile: ~/.ssh/tunnel_key\n</code></pre>\n<p>Exposes multiple local ports through different remote ports on the SSH server.</p>\n<h3>SSH Tunnel with Password Authentication</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: ssh-tunnel\n  port:\n    - &quot;9834:8080&quot;\n  connection:\n    host: vpn-server.company.com\n    port: 2222\n    auth:\n      type: password\n      username: tunnel-user\n      password: ${env.TUNNEL_PASSWORD}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Creates an SSH tunnel using password authentication with password stored in environment variable.</p>\n<h3>SSH Tunnel with Custom Local Host</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: ssh-tunnel\n  port:\n    - &quot;8080:192.168.1.107&quot;          # Remote 8080 -&gt; 192.168.1.107:8080\n    - &quot;9834:192.168.1.107:3000&quot;     # Remote 9834 -&gt; 192.168.1.107:3000\n    - &quot;9835:example.local:8090&quot;     # Remote 9835 -&gt; example.local:8090\n  connection:\n    host: tunnel-server.example.com\n    port: 22\n    auth:\n      type: keyfile\n      username: tunnel-user\n      keyfile: ~/.ssh/tunnel_key\n</code></pre>\n<p>Forwards remote ports to specific hosts in the local network, useful for exposing services running on other machines in your local network.</p>\n<h3>Multiple Gateways</h3>\n<p>You can configure multiple gateways to expose different services:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateways:\n  - type: http-tunnel\n    driver: ngrok\n    port: 8080    # Expose main API\n    \n  - type: http-tunnel\n    driver: ngrok\n    port: 8081    # Expose web UI\n    \n  - type: ssh-tunnel\n    port: 8090    # Expose admin interface through SSH\n    connection:\n      host: secure-bastion.example.com\n      auth:\n        type: keyfile\n        username: admin\n        keyfile: /secure/admin-key\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Use Cases</h2>\n<h3>Development and Testing</h3>\n<p>Expose local development servers for:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Webhook testing from external services</li>\n<li>Mobile app testing against local APIs</li>\n<li>Sharing work-in-progress with team members</li>\n<li>Integration testing with external systems</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Production Deployment</h3>\n<p>Enable external access in environments where:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Direct port exposure is not possible due to NAT/firewall</li>\n<li>SSL termination is handled by the tunnel service</li>\n<li>Load balancing and DDoS protection are provided by tunnel service</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Hybrid Cloud Architectures</h3>\n<p>Connect on-premises services to cloud systems:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Expose internal APIs to cloud-based consumers</li>\n<li>Create secure channels for data synchronization</li>\n<li>Enable cloud-to-on-premises webhook delivery</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Security Considerations</h2>\n<h3>HTTP Tunnels</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Public URLs</strong>: HTTP tunnels create publicly accessible URLs</li>\n<li><strong>Authentication</strong>: Implement proper authentication in your services</li>\n<li><strong>Rate Limiting</strong>: Configure rate limiting to prevent abuse</li>\n<li><strong>Monitoring</strong>: Monitor tunnel usage and access patterns</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>SSH Tunnels</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Key Management</strong>: Securely store and manage SSH private keys</li>\n<li><strong>User Permissions</strong>: Use dedicated SSH users with minimal privileges</li>\n<li><strong>Network Security</strong>: Ensure SSH servers are properly hardened</li>\n<li><strong>Access Logging</strong>: Enable SSH access logging for security auditing</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Performance Considerations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Latency</strong>: Tunnels add network latency compared to direct connections</li>\n<li><strong>Bandwidth</strong>: Monitor bandwidth usage, especially for high-traffic services</li>\n<li><strong>Reliability</strong>: HTTP tunnels may have uptime limitations based on provider</li>\n<li><strong>Concurrent Connections</strong>: Consider connection limits imposed by tunnel services</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Troubleshooting</h2>\n<h3>HTTP Tunnel Issues</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Verify tunnel service CLI is installed and authenticated</li>\n<li>Check service status and quota limits</li>\n<li>Ensure local port is accessible and not blocked by firewall</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>SSH Tunnel Issues</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Verify SSH connectivity to remote server</li>\n<li>Check SSH key permissions (should be 600 or 400)</li>\n<li>Confirm SSH server allows tunnel/port forwarding</li>\n<li>Validate authentication credentials and user permissions</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Integration with Controllers</h2>\n<p>Gateways work seamlessly with controllers to expose services:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n\ngateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: ngrok\n  port: 8080  # Same port as controller\n</code></pre>\n<p>This configuration exposes the HTTP controller through an ngrok tunnel, making it accessible from the internet.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Gateway Configuration Reference"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "reference/compose/language-codes",
      "html": "<h1>Language Codes</h1>\n<p>model-compose uses standardized ISO 639-1 / BCP 47 language codes across components that support language selection, such as text-to-speech and speech-to-text.</p>\n<h2>Supported Codes</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Code</th>\n<th>Language</th>\n<th>Notes</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>en</code></td>\n<td>English</td>\n<td></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>zh-CN</code></td>\n<td>Chinese</td>\n<td>Simplified Chinese</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ja</code></td>\n<td>Japanese</td>\n<td></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ko</code></td>\n<td>Korean</td>\n<td></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>de</code></td>\n<td>German</td>\n<td></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>fr</code></td>\n<td>French</td>\n<td></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ru</code></td>\n<td>Russian</td>\n<td></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>pt</code></td>\n<td>Portuguese</td>\n<td></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>es</code></td>\n<td>Spanish</td>\n<td></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>it</code></td>\n<td>Italian</td>\n<td></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Usage</h2>\n<h3>Text-to-Speech</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">component:\n  type: model\n  task: text-to-speech\n  driver: custom\n  family: qwen\n  model: Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice\n  action:\n    method: generate\n    text: ${input.text as text}\n    language: ko\n    voice: ${input.voice | vivian}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Dynamic Language Selection</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">language: ${input.language as select/en,ko,ja,zh-CN}\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Notes</h2>\n<ul>\n<li>When <code>language</code> is omitted, the model will attempt automatic language detection.</li>\n<li>The available languages depend on the specific model being used. Qwen TTS models support all codes listed above.</li>\n<li>model-compose automatically translates these standardized codes to model-specific formats internally.</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Language Codes"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "reference/compose/listener",
      "html": "<h1>Listener Configuration Reference</h1>\n<p>Listeners are services that wait for external callbacks and webhook notifications. They enable asynchronous workflows where external systems can notify your model-compose application when certain events occur or tasks are completed.</p>\n<h2>Basic Structure</h2>\n<h3>Single Listener</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-callback\n  runtime: native | docker\n  max_concurrent_count: 0\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8090\n  base_path: /callbacks\n  callbacks:\n    - path: /webhook\n      method: POST\n      # ... callback configuration\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Multiple Listeners</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listeners:\n  - type: http-callback\n    port: 8090\n    callbacks:\n      - path: /payment-webhook\n        method: POST\n        # ... payment callback configuration\n        \n  - type: http-callback\n    port: 8091\n    callbacks:\n      - path: /notification-webhook\n        method: POST\n        # ... notification callback configuration\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Listener Types</h2>\n<h3>HTTP Callback (<code>http-callback</code>)</h3>\n<p>Creates an HTTP server that receives webhook callbacks from external services.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-callback\n  host: 0.0.0.0           # Host address to bind the HTTP server to\n  port: 8090                # Port number for the callback server\n  base_path: /callbacks   # Base path prefix for callback endpoints\n  callbacks:                # List of callback endpoint configurations\n    - path: /webhook\n      method: POST\n      # ... additional callback options\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Common Configuration Options</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>type</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Listener type: <code>http-callback</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>runtime</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>native</code></td>\n<td>Runtime environment: <code>native</code> or <code>docker</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_concurrent_count</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>0</code></td>\n<td>Maximum concurrent callback requests (0 = unlimited)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>HTTP Callback Configuration</h2>\n<h3>Server Settings</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>host</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;0.0.0.0&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Host address to bind the HTTP server to</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>port</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>8090</code></td>\n<td>Port number on which the HTTP server will listen</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>base_path</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Base path prefix for all callback endpoints</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Callback Endpoint Configuration</h3>\n<p>Each callback endpoint in the <code>callbacks</code> array can be configured with the following options:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>path</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>URL path for this callback endpoint</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>method</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;POST&quot;</code></td>\n<td>HTTP method: <code>GET</code>, <code>POST</code>, <code>PUT</code>, <code>DELETE</code>, <code>PATCH</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>bulk</code></td>\n<td>boolean</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Whether this callback handles multiple items in a single request</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>item</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Field path to extract individual items from bulk payload</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>identify_by</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Field path used to match callback responses to pending requests</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>status</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Field path to check for completion status in callback payload</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>success_when</code></td>\n<td>array</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Status values that indicate successful completion</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>fail_when</code></td>\n<td>array</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Status values that indicate failed completion</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>result</code></td>\n<td>any</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Field path or transformation to extract final result from payload</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Configuration Examples</h2>\n<h3>Simple Webhook Listener</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-callback\n  port: 8090\n  callbacks:\n    - path: /webhook\n      method: POST\n</code></pre>\n<p>This creates a simple webhook endpoint at <code>http://localhost:8090/webhook</code> that accepts POST requests.</p>\n<h3>Advanced Status-Based Callback</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-callback\n  port: 8090\n  base_path: &quot;/api/callbacks&quot;\n  max_concurrent_count: 10\n  callbacks:\n    - path: /job-status\n      method: POST\n      identify_by: job_id\n      status: status\n      success_when: [&quot;completed&quot;, &quot;finished&quot;]\n      fail_when: [&quot;failed&quot;, &quot;error&quot;, &quot;cancelled&quot;]\n      result: result.data\n</code></pre>\n<p>This configuration:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Creates endpoint at <code>/api/callbacks/job-status</code></li>\n<li>Limits to 10 concurrent callback requests</li>\n<li>Uses <code>job_id</code> field to match callbacks to pending requests</li>\n<li>Considers job complete when status is &quot;completed&quot; or &quot;finished&quot;</li>\n<li>Considers job failed when status is &quot;failed&quot;, &quot;error&quot;, or &quot;cancelled&quot;</li>\n<li>Extracts final result from <code>result.data</code> field</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Bulk Processing Callback</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-callback\n  port: 8090\n  callbacks:\n    - path: /batch-results\n      method: POST\n      bulk: true\n      item: results[]\n      identify_by: request_id\n      status: processing_status\n      success_when: success\n      fail_when: [&quot;failed&quot;, &quot;timeout&quot;]\n      result: output\n</code></pre>\n<p>This configuration:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Processes multiple results in a single callback request</li>\n<li>Extracts individual items from the <code>results</code> array</li>\n<li>Uses <code>request_id</code> to match each result to its original request</li>\n<li>Checks <code>processing_status</code> field for completion status</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Multiple Callback Endpoints</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-callback\n  port: 8090\n  runtime: docker\n  callbacks:\n    - path: /payment-webhook\n      method: POST\n      identify_by: transaction_id\n      status: payment_status\n      success_when: completed\n      fail_when: [&quot;failed&quot;, &quot;cancelled&quot;]\n      result: payment_details\n    \n    - path: /notification-callback\n      method: POST\n      identify_by: message_id\n      status: delivery_status\n      success_when: delivered\n      fail_when: failed\n      result: delivery_info\n</code></pre>\n<p>This configuration creates two different callback endpoints on the same listener service.</p>\n<h3>Simplified Single Callback Syntax</h3>\n<p>For listeners with only one callback endpoint, you can use a simplified syntax:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-callback\n  port: 8090\n  path: /webhook\n  method: POST\n  identify_by: id\n  status: &quot;status&quot;\n  success_when: done\n  result: data\n</code></pre>\n<p>This is equivalent to:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-callback\n  port: 8090\n  callbacks:\n    - path: /webhook\n      method: POST\n      identify_by: id\n      status: status\n      success_when: done\n      result: data\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Usage Patterns</h2>\n<h3>Asynchronous Job Processing</h3>\n<p>Listeners are commonly used for asynchronous job processing where:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Your workflow submits a job to an external service</li>\n<li>The external service immediately returns a job ID</li>\n<li>The external service processes the job asynchronously</li>\n<li>When complete, the external service sends a webhook to your listener</li>\n<li>Your workflow continues with the job results</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Event-Driven Workflows</h3>\n<p>Listeners enable event-driven architectures where external events trigger workflow execution:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Configure listener with appropriate callback endpoints</li>\n<li>Register webhook URLs with external services</li>\n<li>External events trigger callbacks to your listener</li>\n<li>Listener processes the callback and continues workflow execution</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Runtime Considerations</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Concurrency</strong>: Set <code>max_concurrent_count</code> based on your expected callback load</li>\n<li><strong>Port Management</strong>: Ensure listener ports don't conflict with controller or other services</li>\n<li><strong>Security</strong>: Consider implementing authentication/authorization for webhook endpoints</li>\n<li><strong>Network</strong>: Listeners need to be accessible from external services sending callbacks</li>\n<li><strong>Timeouts</strong>: Configure appropriate timeouts for long-running callback processing</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Integration with Workflows</h2>\n<p>Listeners work seamlessly with workflows to enable asynchronous processing patterns. The listener automatically matches incoming callbacks to pending workflow executions based on the <code>identify_by</code> field configuration.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Listener Configuration Reference"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "reference/compose/logger",
      "html": "<h1>Logger Configuration Reference</h1>\n<p>Loggers control how model-compose records and outputs log messages during workflow execution. They provide visibility into workflow progress, debugging information, and error tracking.</p>\n<h2>Basic Structure</h2>\n<h3>Single Logger</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">logger:\n  type: console | file\n  level: debug | info | warning | error | critical\n  # ... type-specific configuration\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Multiple Loggers</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">loggers:\n  - type: console\n    level: info\n    \n  - type: file\n    level: debug\n    path: ./logs/debug.log\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Logger Types</h2>\n<h3>Console Logger (<code>console</code>)</h3>\n<p>Outputs log messages to the console/terminal where model-compose is running.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">logger:\n  type: console\n  level: info\n</code></pre>\n<h3>File Logger (<code>file</code>)</h3>\n<p>Writes log messages to a specified file on disk.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">logger:\n  type: file\n  level: info\n  path: ./logs/run.log\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Common Configuration Options</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>type</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Logger type: <code>console</code> or <code>file</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>level</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>info</code></td>\n<td>Minimum logging level to capture</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Logging Levels</h2>\n<p>Logging levels determine which messages are captured and output. Each level includes all higher priority levels:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Level</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n<th>Includes</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>debug</code></td>\n<td>Detailed diagnostic information</td>\n<td>All messages</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>info</code></td>\n<td>General information about workflow progress</td>\n<td>info, warning, error, critical</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>warning</code></td>\n<td>Warning messages about potential issues</td>\n<td>warning, error, critical</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>error</code></td>\n<td>Error messages for failures</td>\n<td>error, critical</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>critical</code></td>\n<td>Critical errors that may cause system failure</td>\n<td>critical only</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>File Logger Configuration</h2>\n<h3>Path Configuration</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>path</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;./logs/run.log&quot;</code></td>\n<td>File path where logs will be written</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Path Options:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Relative paths</strong>: Resolved relative to the model-compose.yml directory</li>\n<li><strong>Absolute paths</strong>: Full system paths</li>\n<li><strong>Environment variables</strong>: Use <code>${env.LOG_PATH}</code> for dynamic paths</li>\n<li><strong>Directory creation</strong>: Parent directories are created automatically if they don't exist</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Configuration Examples</h2>\n<h3>Console Logger</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">logger:\n  type: console\n  level: info\n</code></pre>\n<p>Basic console logging that outputs INFO level and above messages to the terminal.</p>\n<h3>Console Debug Logger</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">logger:\n  type: console\n  level: debug\n</code></pre>\n<p>Detailed console logging including DEBUG messages for troubleshooting.</p>\n<h3>File Logger with Default Path</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">logger:\n  type: file\n  level: info\n</code></pre>\n<p>Writes logs to the default file location at <code>./logs/run.log</code>.</p>\n<h3>File Logger with Custom Path</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">logger:\n  type: file\n  level: debug\n  path: /var/log/model-compose/app.log\n</code></pre>\n<p>Writes detailed logs to a custom absolute path.</p>\n<h3>File Logger with Environment Variable</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">logger:\n  type: file\n  level: info\n  path: ${env.LOG_FILE_PATH}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Uses an environment variable to specify the log file path dynamically.</p>\n<h3>Error-Only File Logger</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">logger:\n  type: file\n  level: error\n  path: ./logs/errors.log\n</code></pre>\n<p>Only captures ERROR and CRITICAL messages for error tracking.</p>\n<h2>Log Message Format</h2>\n<p>Model-compose log messages follow a structured format:</p>\n<pre><code>YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,mmm LEVEL: [task-ID] Message content\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Format Components:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Timestamp</strong>: Date and time with millisecond precision</li>\n<li><strong>Level</strong>: Log level (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL)</li>\n<li><strong>Task ID</strong>: Unique identifier for the workflow execution</li>\n<li><strong>Message</strong>: Descriptive log message</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Example Log Messages:</strong></p>\n<pre><code>2025-07-30 08:20:25,922 INFO: [task-01K1C7SEJ0G010ZZ1M398DDCXA] Workflow '__workflow__' started.\n2025-07-30 08:20:25,924 DEBUG: [task-01K1C7SEJ0G010ZZ1M398DDCXA] Action 'run-01K1C7SEJ41AFFMPJG6Z8FTJ5C' started for job 'gpt-image-1'\n2025-07-30 08:21:16,492 DEBUG: [task-01K1C7SEJ0G010ZZ1M398DDCXA] Action 'run-01K1C7SEJ41AFFMPJG6Z8FTJ5C' completed in 50.57 seconds.\n2025-07-30 08:21:16,493 INFO: [task-01K1C7SEJ0G010ZZ1M398DDCXA] Workflow '__workflow__' completed in 50.57 seconds.\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Multiple Logger Configuration</h2>\n<p>You can configure multiple loggers to output to different destinations:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">loggers:\n  - type: console\n    level: info\n    \n  - type: file\n    level: debug\n    path: ./logs/debug.log\n    \n  - type: file\n    level: error\n    path: ./logs/errors.log\n</code></pre>\n<p>This configuration:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Shows INFO+ messages on console for real-time monitoring</li>\n<li>Captures DEBUG+ messages to a detailed log file</li>\n<li>Separates ERROR+ messages to a dedicated error log</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Best Practices</h2>\n<h3>Development Environment</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">logger:\n  type: console\n  level: debug\n</code></pre>\n<p>Use console logging with DEBUG level during development for immediate feedback.</p>\n<h3>Production Environment</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">loggers:\n  - type: console\n    level: info\n    \n  - type: file\n    level: info\n    path: /var/log/model-compose/app.log\n    \n  - type: file\n    level: error\n    path: /var/log/model-compose/errors.log\n</code></pre>\n<p>Combine console and file logging in production with separate error tracking.</p>\n<h3>High-Volume Environments</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">logger:\n  type: file\n  level: warning\n  path: ${env.LOG_PATH}/model-compose.log\n</code></pre>\n<p>Use WARNING+ level in high-volume environments to reduce log noise while capturing issues.</p>\n<h2>Log Management</h2>\n<h3>File Rotation</h3>\n<p>Model-compose doesn't provide built-in log rotation. Use system tools for log management:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Linux</strong>: <code>logrotate</code> utility</li>\n<li><strong>Docker</strong>: Configure logging drivers with rotation</li>\n<li><strong>Kubernetes</strong>: Use log aggregation solutions</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Log Analysis</h3>\n<p>Common log analysis patterns:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Filter by task ID\ngrep &quot;task-01K1C7SEJ0G010ZZ1M398DDCXA&quot; logs/run.log\n\n# Show only errors\ngrep &quot;ERROR\\|CRITICAL&quot; logs/run.log\n\n# Workflow completion times\ngrep &quot;completed in&quot; logs/run.log\n\n# Action performance analysis\ngrep &quot;Action.*completed&quot; logs/run.log | sort -k9 -n\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Integration with Monitoring</h2>\n<h3>Structured Logging</h3>\n<p>For integration with log aggregation systems, consider parsing the structured format:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Task ID</strong>: Extract for tracing workflow executions</li>\n<li><strong>Timestamps</strong>: Parse for performance analysis</li>\n<li><strong>Levels</strong>: Filter by severity for alerting</li>\n<li><strong>Execution Times</strong>: Monitor for performance regressions</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Alerting</h3>\n<p>Set up alerts based on log patterns:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Critical errors: <code>CRITICAL</code> level messages</li>\n<li>Workflow failures: Error patterns in workflow completion</li>\n<li>Performance issues: Execution times exceeding thresholds</li>\n<li>System issues: Connection failures, timeouts</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Troubleshooting</h2>\n<h3>Common Issues</h3>\n<p><strong>Log file not created:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Check directory permissions</li>\n<li>Verify parent directory exists</li>\n<li>Ensure sufficient disk space</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Missing log messages:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Verify log level configuration</li>\n<li>Check if logger is properly configured</li>\n<li>Ensure workflow is actually executing</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Permission errors:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Check write permissions for log directory</li>\n<li>Consider using relative paths in containerized environments</li>\n<li>Verify user context has appropriate file system access</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Debug Configuration</h3>\n<p>To troubleshoot logging issues, temporarily use:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">logger:\n  type: console\n  level: debug\n</code></pre>\n<p>This ensures you can see all log messages and verify logger functionality.</p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Logger Configuration Reference"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "reference/compose/system",
      "html": "<h1>System Configuration Reference</h1>\n<p>Systems provide declarative management of infrastructure services required by your components. They are automatically started before components during <code>model-compose up</code> and stopped after components during <code>model-compose down</code>.</p>\n<h2>Basic Structure</h2>\n<h3>Single System</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">system:\n  type: docker-compose\n  file: docker-compose.yml\n  wait: true\n  wait_timeout: 60s\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Multiple Systems</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">systems:\n  - id: database\n    type: docker-compose\n    file: docker-compose.db.yml\n    wait: true\n\n  - id: browser-infra\n    type: docker-compose\n    file: docker-compose.browser.yml\n    wait: true\n    wait_timeout: 120s\n</code></pre>\n<h2>System Types</h2>\n<h3>Docker Compose (<code>docker-compose</code>)</h3>\n<p>Manages services defined in Docker Compose files. Runs <code>docker compose up -d</code> on start and <code>docker compose down</code> on stop.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">system:\n  type: docker-compose\n  file: docker-compose.yml\n  project_name: my-project\n  build: true\n  wait: true\n  wait_timeout: 60s\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Common Configuration Options</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>id</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>__system__</code></td>\n<td>Unique identifier for the system</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>type</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>System type: <code>docker-compose</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Docker Compose Configuration</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>file</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Path to a single docker-compose file (shorthand for <code>files</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>files</code></td>\n<td>array</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Paths to docker-compose files. Multiple files are merged in order</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>project_name</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Docker Compose project name (<code>-p</code> flag)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>profiles</code></td>\n<td>array</td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Docker Compose profiles to activate (<code>--profile</code> flag)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>env_file</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Path to environment file for docker-compose (<code>--env-file</code> flag)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>build</code></td>\n<td>boolean</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Whether to build images before starting (<code>--build</code> flag)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>wait</code></td>\n<td>boolean</td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Whether to wait for services to be healthy before proceeding (<code>--wait</code> flag)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>wait_timeout</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>60s</code></td>\n<td>Timeout for waiting for services to be ready. Supports duration format (e.g., <code>30s</code>, <code>2m</code>, <code>1m30s</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note</strong>: You can use either <code>file</code> (single file) or <code>files</code> (multiple files). If neither is specified, Docker Compose uses its default file discovery (<code>docker-compose.yml</code>).</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Configuration Examples</h2>\n<h3>Simple Docker Compose</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">system:\n  type: docker-compose\n  file: docker-compose.yml\n</code></pre>\n<p>Starts services defined in <code>docker-compose.yml</code> and waits for them to be healthy.</p>\n<h3>Multiple Compose Files</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">system:\n  type: docker-compose\n  files:\n    - docker-compose.yml\n    - docker-compose.override.yml\n  project_name: my-app\n</code></pre>\n<p>Merges multiple compose files, equivalent to <code>docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.override.yml -p my-app up -d</code>.</p>\n<h3>Build and Start</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">system:\n  type: docker-compose\n  file: docker-compose.yml\n  build: true\n  wait: true\n  wait_timeout: 120s\n</code></pre>\n<p>Builds images before starting, useful when compose files reference custom Dockerfiles.</p>\n<h3>With Profiles</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">system:\n  type: docker-compose\n  file: docker-compose.yml\n  profiles:\n    - development\n    - debug\n</code></pre>\n<p>Activates specific Docker Compose profiles.</p>\n<h3>With Environment File</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">system:\n  type: docker-compose\n  file: docker-compose.yml\n  env_file: .env.production\n</code></pre>\n<p>Uses a specific environment file for variable substitution in the compose file.</p>\n<h3>Multiple Systems</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">systems:\n  - id: database\n    type: docker-compose\n    file: docker-compose.db.yml\n    wait: true\n    wait_timeout: 30s\n\n  - id: browser\n    type: docker-compose\n    file: docker-compose.browser.yml\n    wait: true\n    wait_timeout: 60s\n</code></pre>\n<p>Manages multiple independent infrastructure stacks. All systems are started before components and stopped after components.</p>\n<h3>Complete Example with Components</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">systems:\n  - id: browser-infra\n    type: docker-compose\n    file: docker-compose.yml\n    wait: true\n    wait_timeout: 60s\n\ncomponents:\n  - id: browser\n    type: web-browser\n    host: localhost\n    port: 9222\n\nworkflows:\n  - id: scrape\n    jobs:\n      - id: navigate\n        component: browser\n        action: navigate\n        input:\n          url: ${input.url}\n</code></pre>\n<p>The system starts the Docker Compose services (e.g., Chromium browser) before the web-browser component connects to it.</p>\n<h2>Lifecycle</h2>\n<p>Systems follow this lifecycle order relative to other configuration sections:</p>\n<p><strong>Startup (<code>model-compose up</code>):</strong></p>\n<pre><code>1. Systems start (docker compose up -d)\n2. Gateways start\n3. Listeners start\n4. Components start\n5. Controller starts accepting requests\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Shutdown (<code>model-compose down</code>):</strong></p>\n<pre><code>1. Controller stops accepting requests\n2. Components stop\n3. Listeners stop\n4. Gateways stop\n5. Systems stop (docker compose down)\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Prerequisites</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Docker</strong>: The <code>docker</code> CLI must be installed and available in PATH</li>\n<li><strong>Docker Compose</strong>: The <code>docker compose</code> subcommand must be available (Docker Desktop or standalone plugin)</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Troubleshooting</h2>\n<h3>Docker Not Found</h3>\n<pre><code>RuntimeError: 'docker' command not found. Please install Docker to use docker-compose systems.\n</code></pre>\n<p>Install Docker Desktop or Docker Engine with the Compose plugin.</p>\n<h3>Wait Timeout</h3>\n<p>If services take longer than <code>wait_timeout</code> to become healthy, increase the timeout value or check your Docker Compose health check configurations.</p>\n<h3>Compose File Not Found</h3>\n<p>Ensure the <code>file</code> or <code>files</code> paths are relative to the directory containing <code>model-compose.yml</code>.</p>\n<h2>Next Steps</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"/model-compose/reference/compose/component\">Component Configuration</a> - Define components that use system-managed infrastructure</li>\n<li><a href=\"/model-compose/reference/compose/gateway\">Gateway Configuration</a> - Expose services through tunnels</li>\n<li><a href=\"/model-compose/reference/compose/workflow\">Workflow Configuration</a> - Orchestrate jobs using components</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "System Configuration Reference"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "reference/compose/tracer",
      "html": "<h1>Tracer Configuration Reference</h1>\n<p>Tracers send structured tracing data from workflow and job executions to external observability tools. They provide visibility into execution flow, performance metrics, and debugging information through dedicated tracing backends like Langfuse.</p>\n<h2>Basic Structure</h2>\n<h3>Single Tracer</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">tracer:\n  driver: langfuse\n  public_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}\n  secret_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Multiple Tracers</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">tracers:\n  - driver: langfuse\n    public_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}\n    secret_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\n\n  - driver: langfuse\n    public_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY_2}\n    secret_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY_2}\n    url: http://localhost:3000\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Tracer Drivers</h2>\n<h3>Langfuse (<code>langfuse</code>)</h3>\n<p>Sends traces to <a href=\"https://langfuse.com\">Langfuse</a>, an open-source LLM observability platform.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">tracer:\n  driver: langfuse\n  public_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}\n  secret_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Requirements:</strong> <code>langfuse&gt;=4.0</code> (installed automatically on first use)</p>\n<h2>Common Configuration Options</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>driver</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Tracer backend driver (currently: <code>langfuse</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>capture</code></td>\n<td>object</td>\n<td><code>{input: true, output: true}</code></td>\n<td>Controls what data is included in traces</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>timeout</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>30</code></td>\n<td>Timeout in seconds for API requests to the tracing backend</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Capture Settings</h2>\n<p>The <code>capture</code> section controls what data is included in trace payloads.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>capture.input</code></td>\n<td>boolean</td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Include input data in traces</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>capture.output</code></td>\n<td>boolean</td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Include output data in traces</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>capture.redact_keys</code></td>\n<td>list[string]</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Keys to redact from payloads (case-insensitive, recursive)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>capture.max_payload_bytes</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td>none</td>\n<td>Maximum payload size in bytes; payloads exceeding this are replaced with <code>[truncated]</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Redaction</h3>\n<p>Keys listed in <code>redact_keys</code> are replaced with <code>[redacted]</code> recursively throughout the entire payload, regardless of nesting depth. Matching is case-insensitive.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">tracer:\n  driver: langfuse\n  public_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}\n  secret_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\n  capture:\n    redact_keys:\n      - Authorization\n      - secret_key\n      - api_key\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Payload Size Limit</h3>\n<p>When <code>max_payload_bytes</code> is set, payloads that exceed the limit (in UTF-8 bytes) are replaced with <code>[truncated]</code>.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">tracer:\n  driver: langfuse\n  public_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}\n  secret_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\n  capture:\n    max_payload_bytes: 1048576    # 1MB\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Langfuse Configuration</h2>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>driver</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Must be <code>langfuse</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>public_key</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Langfuse public key</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>secret_key</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Langfuse secret key</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>url</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>none</td>\n<td>Langfuse server URL (e.g., <code>https://cloud.langfuse.com</code>, <code>http://localhost:3000</code>). Cannot be used with <code>host</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>host</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>cloud.langfuse.com</code></td>\n<td>Langfuse server hostname or IP address. Cannot be used with <code>url</code>.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>port</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>443</code></td>\n<td>Langfuse server port number (1–65535).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>secure</code></td>\n<td>boolean</td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Use HTTPS for connections.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> Use either <code>url</code> or <code>host</code>/<code>port</code>/<code>secure</code>, not both. When neither is specified, defaults to <code>https://cloud.langfuse.com</code>.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h2>Tracing Data Model</h2>\n<p>Tracers capture a two-level hierarchy: <strong>Trace</strong> (workflow execution) and <strong>Span</strong> (job execution).</p>\n<pre><code>Trace (workflow execution)\n├── Span (job execution)\n├── Span (job execution)\n└── ...\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Trace (Workflow)</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Value</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>name</code></td>\n<td>Workflow ID</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>id</code></td>\n<td>Task ID (deterministic, seeded from task_id)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>session_id</code></td>\n<td>Session ID (if provided at workflow execution)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>input</code></td>\n<td>Workflow input (when <code>capture.input: true</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>output</code></td>\n<td>Workflow output (when <code>capture.output: true</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>status</code></td>\n<td><code>SUCCESS</code> or <code>ERROR</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>metadata</code></td>\n<td><code>{workflow_id, metadata}</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Span (Job)</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Value</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>name</code></td>\n<td>Job ID</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>input</code></td>\n<td>Rendered job input (when <code>capture.input: true</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>output</code></td>\n<td>Job output (when <code>capture.output: true</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>status</code></td>\n<td><code>SUCCESS</code> or <code>ERROR</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Configuration Examples</h2>\n<h3>Basic Langfuse Tracer</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">tracer:\n  driver: langfuse\n  public_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}\n  secret_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Sends all workflow and job traces to Langfuse Cloud with full input/output capture.</p>\n<h3>Self-Hosted Langfuse (URL)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">tracer:\n  driver: langfuse\n  public_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}\n  secret_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\n  url: http://localhost:3000\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Self-Hosted Langfuse (Host/Port)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">tracer:\n  driver: langfuse\n  public_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}\n  secret_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\n  host: localhost\n  port: 3000\n  secure: false\n</code></pre>\n<p>Connects to a self-hosted Langfuse instance.</p>\n<h3>Output-Only Tracing</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">tracer:\n  driver: langfuse\n  public_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}\n  secret_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\n  capture:\n    input: false\n    output: true\n</code></pre>\n<p>Only captures output data, excluding potentially sensitive input payloads.</p>\n<h3>Tracing with Redaction</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">tracer:\n  driver: langfuse\n  public_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}\n  secret_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\n  capture:\n    redact_keys:\n      - Authorization\n      - api_key\n      - secret_key\n      - password\n    max_payload_bytes: 1048576\n</code></pre>\n<p>Redacts sensitive keys and limits payload size to 1MB.</p>\n<h3>Minimal Tracing (No Payloads)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">tracer:\n  driver: langfuse\n  public_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}\n  secret_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\n  capture:\n    input: false\n    output: false\n</code></pre>\n<p>Captures only trace structure (workflow/job names, timing, status) without any payload data.</p>\n<h2>Session Grouping</h2>\n<p>Tracers support <code>session_id</code> for grouping multiple workflow executions into a single session. When provided, traces are grouped in the Langfuse UI by session.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># CLI\nmodel-compose run chat --session-id my-session -i '{&quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;hello&quot;}'\n\n# HTTP API\n# POST /workflows/runs\n# {&quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;chat&quot;, &quot;input&quot;: {...}, &quot;session_id&quot;: &quot;my-session&quot;}\n</code></pre>\n<p>In Langfuse, traces with the same <code>session_id</code> appear grouped together, making it easy to track multi-turn conversations or related workflow executions.</p>\n<h2>Complete Example</h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n\ntracer:\n  driver: langfuse\n  public_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}\n  secret_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\n  url: http://localhost:3000\n  capture:\n    input: true\n    output: true\n    redact_keys:\n      - Authorization\n      - api_key\n\nlogger:\n  type: console\n  level: info\n\ncomponents:\n  - id: gpt-4o\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n    action:\n      path: /chat/completions\n      method: POST\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n      body:\n        model: gpt-4o\n        messages:\n          - role: user\n            content: ${input.prompt}\n      output: ${response.choices[0].message.content}\n\nworkflows:\n  - id: chat\n    jobs:\n      - id: generate\n        component: gpt-4o\n        input:\n          prompt: ${input.prompt}\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Behavior</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Non-blocking</strong>: Tracer event methods are synchronous and return immediately. Events are queued internally and sent asynchronously by a background worker.</li>\n<li><strong>Fault-tolerant</strong>: Tracer failures never impact workflow execution. Errors are logged as warnings and the affected event is dropped.</li>\n<li><strong>No-op when unconfigured</strong>: If no tracers are configured, tracing calls are no-ops with zero performance impact.</li>\n<li><strong>Optional dependency</strong>: The <code>langfuse</code> package is an optional dependency, installed automatically when a Langfuse tracer is configured.</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Best Practices</h2>\n<h3>Development Environment</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">tracer:\n  driver: langfuse\n  public_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}\n  secret_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\n  url: http://localhost:3000\n</code></pre>\n<p>Use a self-hosted Langfuse instance for full visibility during development.</p>\n<h3>Production Environment</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">tracer:\n  driver: langfuse\n  public_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}\n  secret_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\n  capture:\n    redact_keys:\n      - Authorization\n      - api_key\n      - password\n      - secret_key\n    max_payload_bytes: 1048576\n</code></pre>\n<p>Enable redaction for sensitive keys and set payload size limits in production.</p>\n<h3>High-Volume Environments</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">tracer:\n  driver: langfuse\n  public_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY}\n  secret_key: ${env.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY}\n  capture:\n    input: false\n    output: false\n</code></pre>\n<p>Disable payload capture to minimize overhead while still tracking execution structure and timing.</p>\n<h2>Troubleshooting</h2>\n<h3>Common Issues</h3>\n<p><strong>Traces not appearing in Langfuse:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Verify <code>public_key</code> and <code>secret_key</code> are correct</li>\n<li>Check <code>url</code> (or <code>host</code>/<code>port</code>/<code>secure</code>) points to the correct Langfuse instance</li>\n<li>Ensure the Langfuse server is accessible from the model-compose host</li>\n<li>Check logs for tracer warning messages</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Missing input/output data:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Verify <code>capture.input</code> and <code>capture.output</code> are <code>true</code></li>\n<li>Check if <code>max_payload_bytes</code> is set too low (data may be truncated)</li>\n<li>Verify <code>redact_keys</code> isn't matching keys you want to see</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Langfuse package not found:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>The <code>langfuse&gt;=4.0</code> package is installed automatically on first use</li>\n<li>If auto-install fails, install manually: <code>pip install &quot;langfuse&gt;=4.0&quot;</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Connection timeouts:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Increase the <code>timeout</code> value (default: 30 seconds)</li>\n<li>Check network connectivity to the Langfuse server</li>\n<li>Verify firewall rules allow outbound connections</li>\n</ul>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Tracer Configuration Reference"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "reference/compose/workflow",
      "html": "<h1>Workflow Configuration Reference</h1>\n<p>Workflows define the execution logic and data flow for your model-compose applications. They orchestrate components, handle data transformation, and manage complex business logic through a sequence of jobs.</p>\n<h2>Basic Structure</h2>\n<h3>Single Workflow</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflow:\n  id: main\n  title: My Workflow\n  description: Description of what this workflow does\n  jobs:\n    - id: step1\n      component: my-component\n      input: ${input}\n    - id: step2\n      component: another-component\n      input: ${step1.output}\n  output: ${step2.output}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Multiple Workflows</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: workflow-1\n    title: First Workflow\n    default: true\n    jobs:\n      - id: job1\n        component: component-a\n        \n  - id: workflow-2\n    title: Second Workflow\n    jobs:\n      - id: job1\n        component: component-b\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Workflow Configuration</h2>\n<h3>Core Properties</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>id</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;__default__&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Unique identifier for the workflow</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>name</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Name of the workflow</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>title</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Display title for the workflow</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>description</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Description of what the workflow does</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>jobs</code></td>\n<td>array</td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>List of jobs that define execution steps</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>default</code></td>\n<td>boolean</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Whether this workflow should be used as default</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h2>Job Types</h2>\n<p>Workflows support different job types for various execution patterns:</p>\n<h3>Component Job (<code>component</code>)</h3>\n<p>Execute a component action -
