      "slug": "user-guide/01-getting-started",
      "html": "<h1>Chapter 1: Getting Started</h1>\n<h2>1.1 Introduction and Overview</h2>\n<p><strong>model-compose</strong> is a declarative AI workflow orchestrator that lets you define and run AI model pipelines using simple YAML configuration files. Inspired by <code>docker-compose</code>, it brings the same philosophy of declarative configuration to the world of AI model orchestration.</p>\n<h3>What is model-compose?</h3>\n<p>model-compose allows you to:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Compose AI workflows declaratively</strong>: Define complete multi-step AI pipelines in YAML—no custom code required</li>\n<li><strong>Connect anything</strong>: Integrate external AI services (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) or run local AI models seamlessly</li>\n<li><strong>Build complex pipelines</strong>: Chain multiple models and APIs together with clean data flow between steps</li>\n<li><strong>Flexible execution</strong>: Run workflows from CLI, expose as HTTP APIs, or use the Model Context Protocol (MCP)</li>\n<li><strong>Deploy easily</strong>: Run locally or deploy via Docker with minimal configuration</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Key Use Cases</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>API Orchestration</strong>: Chain multiple AI service calls (e.g., text generation → translation → speech synthesis)</li>\n<li><strong>Local Model Inference</strong>: Run HuggingFace models for tasks like chat completion, image analysis, or embeddings</li>\n<li><strong>RAG Systems</strong>: Build retrieval-augmented generation pipelines with vector stores</li>\n<li><strong>Multi-modal Workflows</strong>: Combine text, image, and audio processing in a single pipeline</li>\n<li><strong>Automated Workflows</strong>: Script and automate AI tasks without writing custom integration code</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>How It Works</h3>\n<p>model-compose consists of three core elements:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>YAML Configuration Files</strong> (<code>model-compose.yml</code>): Declaratively define components, workflows, and execution environments.</li>\n<li><strong>Component System</strong>: Provides reusable units of work such as API calls, local model execution, and data processing.</li>\n<li><strong>Execution Environment</strong>: Run workflows via CLI commands or through HTTP/MCP servers.</li>\n</ol>\n<p>For example, a simple workflow that calls the OpenAI API can be defined as:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: chatgpt\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n    action:\n      path: /chat/completions\n\nworkflows:\n  - id: generate-text\n    jobs:\n      - component: chatgpt\n</code></pre>\n<p>With this configuration alone, you can run it from the CLI, expose it as an HTTP API, or deploy it as a Docker container.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>1.2 Installation</h2>\n<h3>Requirements</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Python 3.9 or higher</strong></li>\n<li>pip package manager</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Install via pip</h3>\n<p>The simplest way to install model-compose is via pip:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">pip install model-compose\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Install from Source</h3>\n<p>For the latest development version or to contribute to the project:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">git clone https://github.com/hanyeol/model-compose.git\ncd model-compose\npip install -e .\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Verify Installation</h3>\n<p>Check that model-compose is installed correctly:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose --version\n</code></pre>\n<p>You should see the version number printed.</p>\n<h3>Using Virtual Environments (Recommended)</h3>\n<p>It's recommended to use a virtual environment to avoid dependency conflicts:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Create a virtual environment\npython -m venv venv\n\n# Activate it\n# On macOS/Linux:\nsource venv/bin/activate\n# On Windows:\nvenv\\Scripts\\activate\n\n# Install model-compose\npip install model-compose\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>1.3 Running Your First Workflow</h2>\n<p>Let's walk through creating and running your first model-compose workflow. We'll build a simple workflow that calls the OpenAI API to generate text.</p>\n<h3>1.3.1 Simple Example (OpenAI API Call)</h3>\n<h4>Step 1: Create a Project Directory</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">mkdir my-first-workflow\ncd my-first-workflow\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Step 2: Set Up Your API Key</h4>\n<p>Create a <code>.env</code> file to store your OpenAI API key securely:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># .env\nOPENAI_API_KEY=your-api-key\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note</strong>: Never commit <code>.env</code> files to version control. Add <code>.env</code> to your <code>.gitignore</code>.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h4>Step 3: Create Your Workflow Configuration</h4>\n<p>Create a <code>model-compose.yml</code> file:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># model-compose.yml\ncontroller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /api\n  webui:\n    port: 8081\n\ncomponents:\n  - id: chatgpt\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n    action:\n      path: /chat/completions\n      method: POST\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n        Content-Type: application/json\n      body:\n        model: gpt-4o\n        messages:\n          - role: user\n            content: ${input.prompt}\n      output:\n        response: ${response.choices[0].message.content}\n\nworkflows:\n  - id: generate-text\n    default: true\n    jobs:\n      - id: call-gpt\n        component: chatgpt\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Understanding the Configuration</h4>\n<p>Let's break down what each section does:</p>\n<p><strong>Controller</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /api\n  webui:\n    port: 8081\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li>Defines how workflows are exposed (as HTTP server)</li>\n<li>Sets the API port (8080) and Web UI port (8081)</li>\n<li>Base path for API endpoints (<code>/api</code>)</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Components</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: chatgpt\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n    action:\n      path: /chat/completions\n      method: POST\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n      body:\n        model: gpt-4o\n        messages:\n          - role: user\n            content: ${input.prompt}\n      output:\n        response: ${response.choices[0].message.content}\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li>Defines a reusable component called <code>chatgpt</code></li>\n<li>Configures an HTTP client to call OpenAI's API</li>\n<li>Uses <code>${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}</code> to inject the API key from environment variables</li>\n<li>Passes <code>${input.prompt}</code> to the request body</li>\n<li>Extracts the response into an <code>output.response</code> variable</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Workflows</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: generate-text\n    default: true\n    jobs:\n      - id: call-gpt\n        component: chatgpt\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li>Defines a workflow named <code>generate-text</code></li>\n<li>Marks it as <code>default</code> (runs when no workflow name specified)</li>\n<li>Contains a single job that executes the <code>chatgpt</code> component</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h3>1.3.2 Running a Workflow (run command)</h3>\n<p>The <code>run</code> command executes a workflow once directly from the CLI—perfect for testing and scripting.</p>\n<h4>Basic Usage</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose run generate-text --input '{&quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Write a short poem about coding&quot;}'\n</code></pre>\n<p>This will:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Load the <code>model-compose.yml</code> configuration</li>\n<li>Execute the <code>generate-text</code> workflow</li>\n<li>Pass the input to the workflow</li>\n<li>Print the output to the console</li>\n</ol>\n<h4>Expected Output</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;response&quot;: &quot;Code flows like water,\\nBugs emerge in moonlit nights,\\nDebug till sunrise.&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Passing Different Inputs</h4>\n<p>You can pass any JSON input that your workflow expects:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose run generate-text --input '{&quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Explain quantum computing in one sentence&quot;}'\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Using Environment Variables</h4>\n<p>If you need to override environment variables:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose run generate-text \\\n  --input '{&quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Hello!&quot;}' \\\n  --env OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-different-key\n</code></pre>\n<p>Or use a different env file:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose run generate-text \\\n  --input '{&quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Hello!&quot;}' \\\n  --env-file .env.production\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Running Non-Default Workflows</h4>\n<p>If you have multiple workflows and want to run a specific one:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose run my-other-workflow --input '{&quot;key&quot;: &quot;value&quot;}'\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h3>1.3.3 Starting the Controller and Using Web UI</h3>\n<p>The <code>up</code> command starts a persistent server that hosts your workflows as HTTP endpoints and optionally provides a Web UI.</p>\n<h4>Start the Controller</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose up\n</code></pre>\n<p>You should see output like:</p>\n<pre><code>Starting model-compose controller...\n✓ Loaded configuration from model-compose.yml\n✓ HTTP server running on http://localhost:8080\n✓ Web UI available at http://localhost:8081\n✓ Loaded 1 workflow: generate-text (default)\n</code></pre>\n<p>The controller is now running and ready to accept requests.</p>\n<h4>Using the Web UI</h4>\n<p>Open your browser and navigate to:</p>\n<pre><code>http://localhost:8081\n</code></pre>\n<p>The Web UI provides an interactive interface where you can:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Select workflows</strong> from a dropdown</li>\n<li><strong>Enter inputs</strong> in a form</li>\n<li><strong>Run workflows</strong> with a button click</li>\n<li><strong>View outputs</strong> in real-time</li>\n<li><strong>See execution logs</strong> for debugging</li>\n</ul>\n<p><img src=\"/model-compose/assets/user-guide/images/01-001.png\" alt=\"Web UI Screenshot\" /></p>\n<p><strong>To run your workflow:</strong></p>\n<ol>\n<li>Enter your prompt in the input field (e.g., &quot;Write a short poem about AI&quot;)</li>\n<li>Click &quot;Run Workflow&quot;</li>\n<li>View the generated response in the output panel</li>\n</ol>\n<h4>Using the HTTP API</h4>\n<p>You can also trigger workflows programmatically via HTTP:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/workflows/runs \\\n  -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; \\\n  -d '{\n    &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;generate-text&quot;,\n    &quot;input&quot;: {\n      &quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;What is machine learning?&quot;\n    },\n    &quot;output_only&quot;: true\n  }'\n</code></pre>\n<p>Response:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;response&quot;: &quot;Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence...&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Running in Detached Mode</h4>\n<p>To run the controller in the background:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose up -d\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Stopping the Controller</h4>\n<p>To gracefully shut down the controller:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose down\n</code></pre>\n<p>This will:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Stop the HTTP server</li>\n<li>Stop the Web UI</li>\n<li>Clean up resources</li>\n<li>Save state if needed</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>1.4 Basic Concepts</h2>\n<p>Now that you've run your first workflow, let's clarify the key concepts in model-compose.</p>\n<h3>Controller</h3>\n<p>The <strong>controller</strong> is the runtime environment that hosts and executes your workflows. It can operate in two modes:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>HTTP Server</strong>: Exposes workflows as REST API endpoints with optional Web UI</li>\n<li><strong>MCP Server</strong>: Exposes workflows via the Model Context Protocol (JSON-RPC)</li>\n</ul>\n<p>The controller is configured in the <code>controller</code> section of <code>model-compose.yml</code>.</p>\n<h3>Components</h3>\n<p><strong>Components</strong> are reusable building blocks that perform specific tasks. Think of them as functions you can call from workflows.</p>\n<p>Common component types:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>http-client</code>: Make HTTP API calls to external services</li>\n<li><code>model</code>: Run local AI models (HuggingFace transformers)</li>\n<li><code>shell</code>: Execute shell commands</li>\n<li><code>text-splitter</code>: Split text into chunks</li>\n<li><code>workflow</code>: Call another workflow as a component</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Each component has:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>An <strong>id</strong>: unique identifier to reference it in workflows</li>\n<li>A <strong>type</strong>: what kind of component it is</li>\n<li><strong>Configuration</strong>: specific settings for that component type</li>\n<li><strong>Input/output mappings</strong>: how data flows in and out</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Workflows</h3>\n<p>A <strong>workflow</strong> is a named sequence of jobs that defines a complete AI pipeline. Workflows can:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Execute multiple steps in order</li>\n<li>Pass data between steps using variable bindings</li>\n<li>Have multiple branches or parallel execution (advanced)</li>\n<li>Be triggered via CLI, HTTP API, or Web UI</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Key workflow properties:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>id</code>: Unique name for the workflow</li>\n<li><code>default</code>: Whether this workflow runs by default (optional)</li>\n<li><code>jobs</code>: List of jobs to execute</li>\n<li><code>title</code> and <code>description</code>: Human-readable metadata for Web UI</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Jobs</h3>\n<p><strong>Jobs</strong> are individual steps within a workflow. Each job:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>References a component to execute</li>\n<li>Can accept inputs from previous jobs</li>\n<li>Can produce outputs for subsequent jobs</li>\n<li>Executes in sequence (by default)</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: generate-text\n    component: chatgpt\n    input:\n      prompt: ${input.query}\n\n  - id: translate\n    component: translator\n    input:\n      text: ${generate-text.output.response}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Variable Binding</h3>\n<p><strong>Variable binding</strong> is how data flows through your workflow using the <code>${...}</code> syntax.</p>\n<p>Common variable sources:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>${env.VAR_NAME}</code>: Environment variables</li>\n<li><code>${input.field}</code>: Workflow input</li>\n<li><code>${response.field}</code>: HTTP response from current component</li>\n<li><code>${jobs.job-id.output.field}</code>: Output from a specific job (job-id)</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Example data flow:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">component:\n  action:\n    body:\n      prompt: ${input.user_prompt}  # From workflow input\n      api_key: ${env.API_KEY}       # From environment\n    output:\n      result: ${response.data}      # Extract from API response\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Putting It All Together</h3>\n<p>Here's how everything connects:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Define components</strong> - reusable actions (API calls, models, etc.)</li>\n<li><strong>Create workflows</strong> - sequences of jobs using those components</li>\n<li><strong>Configure controller</strong> - how to expose and run workflows</li>\n<li><strong>Run</strong> - execute via CLI (<code>run</code>) or start a server (<code>up</code>)</li>\n<li><strong>Data flows</strong> - through variable bindings between jobs</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>Next Steps</h2>\n<p>Try it out:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Change the OpenAI model (try <code>gpt-3.5-turbo</code> or <code>gpt-4</code>)</li>\n<li>Experiment with different prompts and inputs</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<p><strong>Next Chapter</strong>: <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/02-core-concepts\">2. Core Concepts</a></p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Chapter 1: Getting Started"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "user-guide/02-core-concepts",
      "html": "<h1>Chapter 2: Core Concepts</h1>\n<p>This chapter provides an in-depth look at model-compose's core concepts and the structure of the <code>model-compose.yml</code> configuration file.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>2.1 model-compose.yml Structure</h2>\n<p><code>model-compose.yml</code> is the central configuration file for model-compose. This file declaratively defines all aspects of your AI workflows.</p>\n<h3>Basic Structure</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  # Defines how workflows are hosted and executed\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n\ncomponents:\n  # Defines executable modules\n  - id: my-component\n    type: http-client\n\nworkflows:\n  # Defines workflow pipelines\n  - id: my-workflow\n    jobs:\n      - component: my-component\n\nlisteners:\n  # Defines event listeners (optional)\n\ngateways:\n  # Defines HTTP tunneling services (optional)\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Main Sections</h3>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>controller</strong> (required): Workflow execution environment configuration</li>\n<li><strong>components</strong> (optional): Executable module definitions</li>\n<li><strong>workflows</strong> (optional): Workflow pipeline definitions</li>\n<li><strong>listeners</strong> (optional): Event listener definitions</li>\n<li><strong>gateways</strong> (optional): Tunneling service definitions</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Configuration File Priority</h3>\n<p>You can use multiple configuration files, with later files overriding earlier ones:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose -f base.yml -f override.yml up\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>2.2 Controller</h2>\n<p>The <strong>controller</strong> is the runtime environment that hosts and executes workflows.</p>\n<h3>Controller Types</h3>\n<h4>HTTP Server</h4>\n<p>Exposes workflows as REST API endpoints.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /api\n  webui:\n    driver: gradio  # or static\n    port: 8081\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Main Settings:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>port</code>: HTTP server port (default: 8080)</li>\n<li><code>base_path</code>: Base path for API endpoints (default: /api)</li>\n<li><code>webui</code>: Optional Web UI configuration\n<ul>\n<li><code>driver</code>: <code>gradio</code> or <code>static</code></li>\n<li><code>port</code>: Web UI port</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>API Endpoints:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>POST /api/workflows/runs</code> - Execute workflow</li>\n</ul>\n<h4>MCP Server</h4>\n<p>Exposes workflows through Model Context Protocol.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: mcp-server\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /mcp\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Main Settings:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>port</code>: MCP server port (default: 8080)</li>\n<li><code>base_path</code>: Base path for MCP endpoints</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Transport Method:</strong></p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note</strong>: Currently only SSE (Server-Sent Events) transport is supported.</p>\n<p>SSE is an HTTP-based protocol that provides unidirectional real-time data streaming from server to client. This means:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>MCP clients must connect to the server via HTTP connections</li>\n<li>stdio transport (standard input/output) is not yet supported</li>\n<li>When using with MCP clients like Claude Desktop, the <code>@modelcontextprotocol/server-stdio</code> adapter is required</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Practical Example</strong>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">// Claude Desktop configuration (claude_desktop_config.json)\n{\n  &quot;mcpServers&quot;: {\n    &quot;my-workflow&quot;: {\n      &quot;command&quot;: &quot;npx&quot;,\n      &quot;args&quot;: [&quot;-y&quot;, &quot;@modelcontextprotocol/server-stdio&quot;, &quot;http://localhost:8080/mcp&quot;]\n    }\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Runtime Configuration</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  runtime:\n    type: native  # or docker\n  max_concurrent_count: 10  # Concurrent execution limit\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Runtime Types:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>native</code>: Execute directly in current environment</li>\n<li><code>docker</code>: Execute in Docker container</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>2.3 Components</h2>\n<p><strong>Components</strong> are reusable building blocks that define one or more actions. Each component groups actions for a specific service or functionality.</p>\n<h3>Single Action Component</h3>\n<p>The simplest form, where a component defines only one action using <code>action:</code> (singular):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: chatgpt\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n    action:\n      path: /chat/completions\n      method: POST\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n        Content-Type: application/json\n      body:\n        model: gpt-4o\n        messages:\n          - role: user\n            content: ${input.prompt}\n      output:\n        response: ${response.choices[0].message.content}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Multiple Actions Component</h3>\n<p>You can define multiple actions in a single component:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: slack-api\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://slack.com/api\n    headers:\n      Authorization: Bearer ${env.SLACK_TOKEN}\n    actions:\n      - id: send-message\n        path: /chat.postMessage\n        method: POST\n        body:\n          channel: ${input.channel}\n          text: ${input.text}\n        output: ${response}\n\n      - id: list-channels\n        path: /conversations.list\n        method: GET\n        output: ${response.channels}\n</code></pre>\n<p>In workflows, use <code>component.action</code> format to execute a specific action:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflow:\n  jobs:\n    - id: send\n      component: slack-api\n      action: send-message\n      input:\n        channel: &quot;#general&quot;\n        text: &quot;Hello!&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Main Component Types</h3>\n<h4>1. HTTP Client</h4>\n<p>Calls external APIs.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">- id: api-call\n  type: http-client\n  action:\n    endpoint: https://api.example.com/v1/endpoint\n    method: POST\n    headers:\n      Authorization: Bearer ${env.API_KEY}\n    body:\n      data: ${input.data}\n    output:\n      result: ${response.result}\n</code></pre>\n<h4>2. Model</h4>\n<p>Runs local AI models.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">- id: local-llm\n  type: model\n  source: huggingface\n  model_id: meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct\n  task: chat-completion\n  device: cuda\n  input:\n    messages: ${input.messages}\n  output:\n    response: ${output.content}\n</code></pre>\n<h4>3. Shell</h4>\n<p>Executes shell commands.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">- id: run-script\n  type: shell\n  command: python process.py\n  args:\n    - ${input.file_path}\n  output:\n    result: ${stdout}\n</code></pre>\n<h4>4. Workflow</h4>\n<p>Calls another workflow as a component.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">- id: sub-workflow\n  type: workflow\n  workflow_id: preprocessing\n  input: ${input}\n  output: ${output}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Input/Output Mapping</h3>\n<p>Components receive input and generate output:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">- id: translator\n  type: http-client\n  action:\n    endpoint: https://api.translate.com/v1/translate\n    body:\n      text: ${input.text}      # From input\n      target: ${input.language} # From input\n    output:\n      translated: ${response.translation}  # Extract to output\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>2.4 Workflows</h2>\n<p><strong>Workflows</strong> are named sequences of jobs that define complete AI pipelines.</p>\n<h3>Basic Workflow</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: generate-text\n    title: Text Generation\n    description: Generate text using GPT-4o\n    default: true\n    jobs:\n      - id: generate\n        component: chatgpt\n        input:\n          prompt: ${input.prompt}\n        output:\n          result: ${output.response}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Workflow Properties</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>id</code> (required): Unique workflow identifier</li>\n<li><code>title</code>: Human-readable title</li>\n<li><code>description</code>: Workflow description</li>\n<li><code>default</code>: Set as default workflow (true/false)</li>\n<li><code>jobs</code>: List of jobs to execute</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Simplified Workflow</h3>\n<p>For single workflows, use <code>workflow</code> (singular object) instead of <code>workflows</code> (plural array):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># Explicit form (workflows)\nworkflows:\n  - id: chat\n    title: Chat with GPT\n    jobs:\n      - component: chatgpt\n\n# Simplified form (workflow)\nworkflow:\n  title: Chat with GPT\n  component: chatgpt  # Single component workflow\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>2.5 Jobs</h2>\n<p><strong>Jobs</strong> are individual steps within a workflow.</p>\n<h3>Job Definition</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: step1\n    component: chatgpt\n    input:\n      prompt: ${input.query}\n    output:\n      answer: ${output.response}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Job Properties</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>id</code>: Unique job identifier (used to reference by other jobs)</li>\n<li><code>component</code>: Component ID to execute</li>\n<li><code>input</code>: Input mapping to pass to component</li>\n<li><code>output</code>: Map component output to workflow output</li>\n<li><code>depends_on</code>: Define dependencies (jobs that must complete before this one)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Data Passing Between Jobs</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: generate-quote\n    component: quote-generator\n    input:\n      topic: ${input.topic}\n    output:\n      quote: ${output.text}\n\n  - id: convert-to-speech\n    component: text-to-speech\n    input:\n      text: ${jobs.generate-quote.output.quote}  # Use previous job's output\n    output:\n      audio: ${output as audio/mp3;base64}\n    depends_on: [ generate-quote ]  # Explicit dependency\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Job Execution Order</h3>\n<p>By default, jobs execute sequentially:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: step1      # Executes 1st\n    component: comp1\n\n  - id: step2      # Executes 2nd (after step1)\n    component: comp2\n    depends_on: [ step1 ]\n\n  - id: step3      # Executes 3rd (after step2)\n    component: comp3\n    depends_on: [ step2 ]\n</code></pre>\n<p>Parallel execution is possible (when no dependencies):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: parallel1\n    component: comp1\n\n  - id: parallel2  # Can run in parallel with parallel1\n    component: comp2\n\n  - id: final      # Runs after both parallel1 and parallel2 complete\n    component: comp3\n    depends_on: [ parallel1, parallel2 ]\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>2.6 Data Flow and Variable Binding</h2>\n<p><strong>Variable binding</strong> uses the <code>${...}</code> syntax to connect data between workflow steps. You can reference environment variables, user input, component outputs, and previous job results, with support for type conversion, default values, and format specification. This enables you to build complex data pipelines declaratively without writing code.</p>\n<h3>Variable Sources</h3>\n<h4>1. Environment Variables</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${env.VARIABLE_NAME}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">headers:\n  Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n</code></pre>\n<h4>2. Workflow Input</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${input.field}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">body:\n  prompt: ${input.user_question}\n  temperature: ${input.temperature | 0.7}  # Default 0.7\n</code></pre>\n<h4>3. Component Response</h4>\n<p><strong>Important</strong>: Response variables differ by component type.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${response.field}   # HTTP-based components (http-client, http-server, vector-store, etc.)\n${result.field}     # Local execution components (model, datasets, text-splitter, key-value-store, file-store, etc.)\n${stdout}           # Shell commands (shell)\n${output}           # Workflow invocation (workflow)\n</code></pre>\n<p>Examples:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># HTTP client\noutput:\n  message: ${response.choices[0].message.content}\n  tokens: ${response.usage.total_tokens}\n\n# Local model\noutput:\n  generated_text: ${result}\n\n# Shell command\noutput:\n  command_output: ${stdout}\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p>💡 <strong>Detailed Variable Reference</strong>: See <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/14-variable-binding#1422-component-response-variables\">14.2.2 Component Response Variables</a> for a complete list of variable sources for all component types.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h4>4. Previous Job Output</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${jobs.job-id.output.field}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">input:\n  text: ${jobs.generate-text.output.content}\n  language: ${jobs.detect-language.output.lang}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Variable Transformations</h3>\n<h4>Type Casting</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${input.value as number}     # Convert to number\n${input.value as text}       # Convert to text\n${input.value as boolean}    # Convert to boolean\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Base64 Encoding</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${output as base64}                      # Encode to Base64\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Base64 Decoding</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${output as audio/mp3;base64}           # Decode Base64 to audio\n${output as image/png;base64}           # Decode Base64 to image\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Default Values</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${input.temperature | 0.7}               # Use 0.7 if input.temperature is missing\n${env.PORT | 8080}                       # Use 8080 if PORT env var is missing\n${input.model | gpt-4o}                  # Specify default model\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Complete Data Flow Example</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n\ncomponents:\n  - id: generate-quote\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n        Content-Type: application/json\n      body:\n        model: gpt-4o\n        messages:\n          - role: user\n            content: ${input.topic}\n      output:\n        quote: ${response.choices[0].message.content}\n\n  - id: text-to-speech\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/${input.voice_id}?output_format=mp3_44100_128\n      headers:\n        xi-api-key: ${env.ELEVENLABS_API_KEY}\n        Content-Type: application/json\n      body:\n        text: ${input.text}\n        model_id: eleven_multilingual_v2\n      output: ${response as base64}\n\nworkflow:\n  title: Quote to Voice\n  jobs:\n    - id: create-quote\n      component: generate-quote\n      input:\n        topic: ${input.topic}\n      output:\n        text: ${output.quote}\n\n    - id: create-voice\n      component: text-to-speech\n      input:\n        text: ${jobs.create-quote.output.text}\n        voice_id: ${input.voice_id | JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb}\n      output:\n        quote: ${jobs.create-quote.output.text}\n        audio: ${output}\n      depends_on: [create-quote]\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Data Flow:</strong></p>\n<ol>\n<li>User provides <code>topic</code> and <code>voice_id</code> input</li>\n<li><code>create-quote</code> job:\n<ul>\n<li>Pass <code>${input.topic}</code> to GPT-4o</li>\n<li>Extract quote to <code>${output.quote}</code></li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li><code>create-voice</code> job:\n<ul>\n<li>Get quote from previous job via <code>${jobs.create-quote.output.text}</code></li>\n<li>Get voice ID from <code>${input.voice_id}</code> (or use default)</li>\n<li>Pass to TTS API to generate MP3 audio</li>\n<li>Encode audio to Base64 and return</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>2.7 Components vs Jobs</h2>\n<p>In model-compose, <strong>Components</strong> and <strong>Jobs</strong> serve different purposes. Understanding this distinction is key to designing effective workflows.</p>\n<h3>Component</h3>\n<p>A <strong>component</strong> is a <strong>reusable functional definition</strong>.</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Definition</strong>: Declared in the <code>components</code> section</li>\n<li><strong>Role</strong>: Defines how to access a specific service or functionality (e.g., API calls, model execution)</li>\n<li><strong>Reusability</strong>: Can be reused across multiple workflows and jobs</li>\n<li><strong>Execution</strong>: Components themselves don't execute; they are executed through jobs</li>\n<li><strong>Distributed Deployment</strong>: Components can be deployed to remote servers to build distributed environments</li>\n</ul>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: gpt4o\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n    action:\n      path: /chat/completions\n      method: POST\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n      body:\n        model: gpt-4o\n        messages:\n          - role: user\n            content: ${input.prompt}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Job</h3>\n<p>A <strong>job</strong> is an <strong>actual execution instance of a component within a workflow</strong>.</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Definition</strong>: Declared in the <code>workflow.jobs</code> section</li>\n<li><strong>Role</strong>: Executes a component, passes input data, and collects output</li>\n<li><strong>Execution Order</strong>: Defines execution sequence with other jobs via <code>depends_on</code></li>\n<li><strong>Data Flow</strong>: Passes results from previous jobs as input to subsequent jobs</li>\n</ul>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflow:\n  jobs:\n    - id: generate-text\n      component: gpt4o\n      input:\n        prompt: &quot;Write a haiku&quot;\n      output: ${output}\n\n    - id: analyze-sentiment\n      component: gpt4o\n      input:\n        prompt: &quot;Analyze sentiment: ${jobs.generate-text.output}&quot;\n      depends_on: [generate-text]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Key Differences Summary</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Aspect</th>\n<th>Component</th>\n<th>Job</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Definition Location</strong></td>\n<td><code>components</code> section</td>\n<td><code>workflow.jobs</code> section</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Role</strong></td>\n<td>Functional definition (template)</td>\n<td>Execution instance</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Reusability</strong></td>\n<td>Reusable across workflows</td>\n<td>Bound to specific workflow</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Execution</strong></td>\n<td>Cannot execute directly</td>\n<td>Executes when workflow runs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Data</strong></td>\n<td>Defines input/output schema</td>\n<td>Handles actual data passing</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Dependencies</strong></td>\n<td>None</td>\n<td>Uses <code>depends_on</code> for job ordering</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Practical Example</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># Component definition: How to call OpenAI API\ncomponents:\n  - id: openai-chat\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n    action:\n      path: /chat/completions\n      method: POST\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n      body:\n        model: gpt-4o\n        messages:\n          - role: user\n            content: ${input.prompt}\n      output:\n        text: ${response.choices[0].message.content}\n\n# Workflow: Reuse the same component in multiple jobs\nworkflows:\n  - id: content-pipeline\n    jobs:\n      # Job 1: Generate title\n      - id: generate-title\n        component: openai-chat\n        input:\n          prompt: &quot;Create a catchy title for a blog about AI&quot;\n        output: ${output}\n\n      # Job 2: Generate body (uses title)\n      - id: generate-body\n        component: openai-chat\n        input:\n          prompt: &quot;Write a blog post with this title: ${jobs.generate-title.output.text}&quot;\n        depends_on: [generate-title]\n        output: ${output}\n\n      # Job 3: Generate summary (uses body)\n      - id: generate-summary\n        component: openai-chat\n        input:\n          prompt: &quot;Summarize this text: ${jobs.generate-body.output.text}&quot;\n        depends_on: [generate-body]\n        output: ${output}\n</code></pre>\n<p>In this example:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Component</strong> <code>openai-chat</code>: Defines OpenAI API calling method once</li>\n<li><strong>Jobs</strong> (<code>generate-title</code>, <code>generate-body</code>, <code>generate-summary</code>): Execute the same component three times with different prompts and data</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>Next Steps</h2>\n<p>Try it out:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Build workflows with multiple jobs</li>\n<li>Experiment with various variable binding patterns</li>\n<li>Explore component reusability patterns</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<p><strong>Next Chapter</strong>: <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/03-cli-usage\">3. CLI Usage</a></p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Chapter 2: Core Concepts"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "user-guide/03-cli-usage",
      "html": "<h1>Chapter 3: CLI Usage</h1>\n<p>This chapter provides detailed coverage of all model-compose CLI commands and options.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>3.1 Basic Commands</h2>\n<p>model-compose provides five core commands:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>up</code> - Start and run services</li>\n<li><code>down</code> - Stop and clean up services</li>\n<li><code>start</code> - Start services</li>\n<li><code>stop</code> - Stop services</li>\n<li><code>run</code> - Execute workflow once</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Command Structure</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose [global-options] &lt;command&gt; [command-options] [arguments]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Global Options</h3>\n<p>Available for all commands:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose --file &lt;config-file&gt; &lt;command&gt;\nmodel-compose -f &lt;config-file&gt; &lt;command&gt;\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Options:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>--file</code>, <code>-f</code>: Specify configuration file (repeatable, merges multiple files)</li>\n<li><code>--version</code>: Display version information</li>\n<li><code>--help</code>: Display help</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Examples:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Single configuration file\nmodel-compose -f config.yml up\n\n# Merge multiple configuration files\nmodel-compose -f base.yml -f override.yml up\n\n# Check version\nmodel-compose --version\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>3.2 up Command</h2>\n<p>Starts and runs services. Sets up a new environment and starts all necessary services.</p>\n<h3>Usage</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose up [options]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Options</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>-d</code>, <code>--detach</code>: Run in detached mode (background)</li>\n<li><code>--env-file &lt;file&gt;</code>: Specify environment variable file (repeatable)</li>\n<li><code>-e</code>, <code>--env &lt;KEY=VALUE&gt;</code>: Set environment variable directly (repeatable)</li>\n<li><code>-v</code>, <code>--verbose</code>: Enable verbose output</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Examples</h3>\n<p><strong>Basic execution:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose up\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Run in background:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose up -d\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Use environment file:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose up --env-file .env --env-file .env.production\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Set environment variables directly:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose up -e OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-xxx -e PORT=9000\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Verbose logging:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose up --verbose\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Combine multiple options:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose -f config.yml up -d --env-file .env -v\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Operations</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Load and validate configuration files</li>\n<li>Load and merge environment variables</li>\n<li>Set up and start components</li>\n<li>Set up listeners and gateways</li>\n<li>Start controller</li>\n<li>Start Web UI (if configured)</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>3.3 down Command</h2>\n<p>Stops running services and cleans up all resources.</p>\n<h3>Usage</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose down [options]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Options</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>--env-file &lt;file&gt;</code>: Specify environment variable file (repeatable)</li>\n<li><code>-e</code>, <code>--env &lt;KEY=VALUE&gt;</code>: Set environment variable directly (repeatable)</li>\n<li><code>-v</code>, <code>--verbose</code>: Enable verbose output</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Examples</h3>\n<p><strong>Basic shutdown:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose down\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>With environment variables:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose down --env-file .env\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Verbose logging:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose down --verbose\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Operations</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Load configuration files</li>\n<li>Identify running services</li>\n<li>Stop controller</li>\n<li>Clean up components</li>\n<li>Clean up listeners and gateways</li>\n<li>Release resources</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>3.4 start Command</h2>\n<p>Starts already configured services. Unlike <code>up</code>, only performs startup without new configuration.</p>\n<h3>Usage</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose start [options]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Options</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>--env-file &lt;file&gt;</code>: Specify environment variable file (repeatable)</li>\n<li><code>-e</code>, <code>--env &lt;KEY=VALUE&gt;</code>: Set environment variable directly (repeatable)</li>\n<li><code>-v</code>, <code>--verbose</code>: Enable verbose output</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Examples</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose start\nmodel-compose start --verbose\nmodel-compose start --env-file .env\n</code></pre>\n<h3>up vs start</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Command</th>\n<th>Purpose</th>\n<th>Operation</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>up</code></td>\n<td>Initial setup and start</td>\n<td>Create configuration + start services</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>start</code></td>\n<td>Start existing services</td>\n<td>Start services only</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>3.5 stop Command</h2>\n<p>Stops running services. Configuration is preserved and can be restarted with <code>start</code>.</p>\n<h3>Usage</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose stop [options]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Options</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>--env-file &lt;file&gt;</code>: Specify environment variable file (repeatable)</li>\n<li><code>-e</code>, <code>--env &lt;KEY=VALUE&gt;</code>: Set environment variable directly (repeatable)</li>\n<li><code>-v</code>, <code>--verbose</code>: Enable verbose output</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Examples</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose stop\nmodel-compose stop --verbose\n</code></pre>\n<h3>stop vs down</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Command</th>\n<th>Purpose</th>\n<th>Operation</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stop</code></td>\n<td>Pause</td>\n<td>Stop services (keep configuration)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>down</code></td>\n<td>Complete shutdown</td>\n<td>Stop services + clean up resources</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>3.6 run Command</h2>\n<p>Executes a workflow once. Ideal for testing workflows from CLI or using in scripts.</p>\n<h3>Usage</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose run [workflow-id] [options]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Arguments</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>workflow-id</code>: ID of workflow to execute (optional, defaults to default workflow)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Options</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>-i</code>, <code>--input &lt;JSON&gt;</code>: Workflow input data (JSON format)</li>\n<li><code>--env-file &lt;file&gt;</code>: Specify environment variable file (repeatable)</li>\n<li><code>-e</code>, <code>--env &lt;KEY=VALUE&gt;</code>: Set environment variable directly (repeatable)</li>\n<li><code>-o</code>, <code>--output &lt;file&gt;</code>: Save output to file</li>\n<li><code>--auto-resume</code>: Automatically resume interrupts without prompting</li>\n<li><code>-v</code>, <code>--verbose</code>: Enable verbose output</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Examples</h3>\n<p><strong>Run default workflow:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose run\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Run specific workflow:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose run generate-text\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>With input data:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose run generate-text --input '{&quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Hello&quot;}'\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Formatted JSON input:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose run generate-text --input '{\n  &quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Explain AI&quot;,\n  &quot;temperature&quot;: 0.7\n}'\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Save output to file:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose run generate-text \\\n  --input '{&quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Hello&quot;}' \\\n  --output result.json\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Specify environment variables:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose run generate-text \\\n  --input '{&quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Test&quot;}' \\\n  --env OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-xxx\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Combine multiple options:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose -f config.yml run my-workflow \\\n  --input '{&quot;data&quot;: &quot;test&quot;}' \\\n  --env-file .env \\\n  --output output.json \\\n  --verbose\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Interrupt Handling</h3>\n<p>When a workflow contains jobs with <code>interrupt</code> configuration, the <code>run</code> command pauses execution and prompts for user input:</p>\n<pre><code>--- Interrupted (job: run-command, phase: before) ---\n\nAbout to execute: ls -la\n{&quot;command&quot;: &quot;ls -la&quot;}\n\n✋ Action required — press Enter to continue, or type an answer (JSON or text):\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Behavior:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Press Enter without input to continue with the original data</li>\n<li>Enter JSON to replace the job's input (before phase) or output (after phase)</li>\n<li>Enter plain text to pass as a string value</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Non-interactive mode:</strong></p>\n<p>If no TTY is available (e.g., in CI/CD pipelines), use <code>--auto-resume</code> to skip all interrupt prompts and continue with original data:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose run my-workflow --input '{&quot;data&quot;: &quot;test&quot;}' --auto-resume\n</code></pre>\n<p>Without <code>--auto-resume</code> and no TTY, the command exits with code 1.</p>\n<h3>Output Format</h3>\n<p>Workflow execution results are output in JSON format:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;response&quot;: &quot;Workflow execution result...&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>On error:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;error&quot;: &quot;Error message...&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>3.7 Environment Variable Management</h2>\n<p>model-compose supports various methods for managing environment variables.</p>\n<h3>Method 1: .env File</h3>\n<p>Define environment variables in a <code>.env</code> file:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># .env\nOPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-key-here\nELEVENLABS_API_KEY=your-elevenlabs-key\nPORT=8080\n</code></pre>\n<p>Usage:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose up --env-file .env\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Method 2: Multiple .env Files</h3>\n<p>Use separate files for different environments:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># .env.base\nPORT=8080\nLOG_LEVEL=info\n\n# .env.production\nOPENAI_API_KEY=sk-prod-key\n</code></pre>\n<p>Usage (later files take precedence):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose up --env-file .env.base --env-file .env.production\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Method 3: Command Line Direct Specification</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose up -e OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-xxx -e PORT=9000\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Method 4: System Environment Variables</h3>\n<p>Reference system environment variables directly in configuration:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-xxx\nmodel-compose up\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Priority Order</h3>\n<p>Environment variables are applied in the following order (highest priority first):</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Command line <code>-e</code> option</strong> - Highest priority</li>\n<li><strong>Current shell environment variables</strong> - Medium priority</li>\n<li><strong><code>--env-file</code> files</strong> (later files override earlier ones) - Lowest priority</li>\n</ol>\n<p>This means:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Shell environment variables override <code>.env</code> file values</li>\n<li>Command line <code>-e</code> arguments override everything</li>\n<li>This allows flexible configuration across different deployment scenarios</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Security Recommendations</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Add <code>.env</code> files to <code>.gitignore</code></li>\n<li>Manage production keys in separate files</li>\n<li>Don't enter sensitive information directly in command line</li>\n<li>Use system environment variables in CI/CD</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>3.8 Configuration File Specification</h2>\n<h3>Single Configuration File</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose -f model-compose.yml up\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Merge Multiple Configuration Files</h3>\n<p>Later files take precedence over earlier files:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose -f base.yml -f override.yml up\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Example:</strong></p>\n<p><code>base.yml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n\ncomponents:\n  - id: chatgpt\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n</code></pre>\n<p><code>override.yml</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  port: 9000  # Overrides base.yml port\n\ncomponents:\n  - id: custom-component\n    type: http-client\n</code></pre>\n<p>Result: Port is 9000, both components are included</p>\n<h3>Default Configuration File</h3>\n<p>If no configuration file is specified, searches current directory in this order:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><code>model-compose.yml</code></li>\n<li><code>model-compose.yaml</code></li>\n</ol>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Automatically uses model-compose.yml\nmodel-compose up\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Environment-Specific Configuration</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Development environment\nmodel-compose -f base.yml -f dev.yml up\n\n# Staging environment\nmodel-compose -f base.yml -f staging.yml up\n\n# Production environment\nmodel-compose -f base.yml -f production.yml up\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>3.9 Debugging Options</h2>\n<h3>Verbose Mode</h3>\n<p>All commands support the <code>-v</code> or <code>--verbose</code> flag to enable detailed logging:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose up --verbose\nmodel-compose run my-workflow --input '{}' --verbose\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Information displayed in verbose mode:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Configuration file loading process</li>\n<li>Environment variable merging process</li>\n<li>Component initialization logs</li>\n<li>HTTP request/response details</li>\n<li>Workflow execution step-by-step logs</li>\n<li>Error stack traces</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Error Messages</h3>\n<p>model-compose provides clear error messages:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">❌ Invalid JSON provided for --input\n❌ Configuration file not found: config.yml\n❌ Environment variable OPENAI_API_KEY is required\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Common Troubleshooting</h3>\n<p><strong>Issue: Configuration file not found</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Solution: Check file path\nmodel-compose -f ./configs/model-compose.yml up\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Issue: Missing environment variable</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Solution: Specify environment variable\nmodel-compose up --env-file .env\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Issue: JSON parsing error</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Incorrect\nmodel-compose run --input '{prompt: &quot;test&quot;}'  # ❌\n\n# Correct\nmodel-compose run --input '{&quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;test&quot;}'  # ✅\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>3.10 Practical Examples</h2>\n<h3>Development Workflow</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># 1. Prepare development configuration\n# dev.yml\n\n# 2. Start services\nmodel-compose -f base.yml -f dev.yml up\n\n# 3. Test workflow\nmodel-compose run test-workflow --input '{&quot;test&quot;: true}' --verbose\n\n# 4. Restart after changes\nmodel-compose stop\nmodel-compose start\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Production Deployment</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># 1. Set production environment variables\nexport OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-prod-xxx\nexport ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=prod-xxx\n\n# 2. Start with production configuration\nmodel-compose -f base.yml -f production.yml up -d\n\n# 3. Check status (view logs)\ndocker logs &lt;container-id&gt;  # For Docker runtime\n</code></pre>\n<h3>CI/CD Pipeline</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">#!/bin/bash\n# deploy.sh\n\n# Load environment variables\nsource .env.production\n\n# Deploy service\nmodel-compose -f base.yml -f production.yml up -d\n\n# Health check\ncurl http://localhost:8080/health\n\n# Run tests\nmodel-compose run smoke-test --input '{}' --verbose\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Scripting</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">#!/bin/bash\n# batch-process.sh\n\n# Run workflow for multiple inputs\nfor file in inputs/*.json; do\n  echo &quot;Processing $file...&quot;\n  model-compose run process-data \\\n    --input &quot;$(cat $file)&quot; \\\n    --output &quot;outputs/$(basename $file)&quot; \\\n    --verbose\ndone\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>3.11 Command Quick Reference</h2>\n<h3>Basic Commands</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Command</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n<th>Main Options</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>up</code></td>\n<td>Start and run services</td>\n<td><code>-d</code>, <code>--env-file</code>, <code>-v</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>down</code></td>\n<td>Stop and clean up services</td>\n<td><code>--env-file</code>, <code>-v</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>start</code></td>\n<td>Start services</td>\n<td><code>--env-file</code>, <code>-v</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stop</code></td>\n<td>Stop services</td>\n<td><code>--env-file</code>, <code>-v</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>run</code></td>\n<td>Execute workflow</td>\n<td><code>-i</code>, <code>-o</code>, <code>--auto-resume</code>, <code>--env-file</code>, <code>-v</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Global Options</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Option</th>\n<th>Short</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>--file</code></td>\n<td><code>-f</code></td>\n<td>Specify configuration file</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>--version</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Display version</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>--help</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Display help</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Common Options</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Option</th>\n<th>Short</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>--env-file</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Environment variable file</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>--env</code></td>\n<td><code>-e</code></td>\n<td>Set environment variable directly</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>--verbose</code></td>\n<td><code>-v</code></td>\n<td>Verbose output</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>run Command Specific Options</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Option</th>\n<th>Short</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>--input</code></td>\n<td><code>-i</code></td>\n<td>Input JSON data</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>--output</code></td>\n<td><code>-o</code></td>\n<td>Output file path</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>--auto-resume</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Skip interrupt prompts automatically</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>Next Steps</h2>\n<p>Try it out:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Experiment with various command combinations</li>\n<li>Organize environment-specific configuration files</li>\n<li>Use model-compose in scripts</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<p><strong>Next Chapter</strong>: <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/04-component-configuration\">4. Component Configuration</a></p>\n",

        "title": "Chapter 3: CLI Usage"
      }

      "slug": "user-guide/04-component-configuration",
      "html": "<h1>Chapter 4: Component Configuration</h1>\n<p>This chapter covers various component types, definition methods, input/output mapping, and reusability patterns in model-compose.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>4.1 Component Types</h2>\n<p>model-compose provides various component types for performing different tasks.</p>\n<h3>Available Component Types</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Purpose</th>\n<th>Main Use Cases</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>agent</code></td>\n<td>Autonomous AI agent</td>\n<td>ReAct loop with tool use via workflows</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>http-client</code></td>\n<td>External API calls</td>\n<td>REST API integration for OpenAI, ElevenLabs, etc.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>http-server</code></td>\n<td>Provide HTTP service</td>\n<td>Implement custom HTTP API endpoints</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mcp-server</code></td>\n<td>Provide MCP service</td>\n<td>Implement Model Context Protocol server</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mcp-client</code></td>\n<td>MCP client</td>\n<td>Communicate with MCP servers</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>model</code></td>\n<td>Run local AI models</td>\n<td>Local model inference for text generation, image analysis, etc.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>model-memory</code></td>\n<td>Model conversation memory</td>\n<td>Session-based chat history with windowing and summarization</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>model-tokenizer</code></td>\n<td>Model tokenization</td>\n<td>Token encoding, decoding, counting using model tokenizers</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>model-trainer</code></td>\n<td>Train models</td>\n<td>Fine-tuning, LoRA training</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>datasets</code></td>\n<td>Load datasets</td>\n<td>Load and process training/evaluation datasets</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>vector-store</code></td>\n<td>Vector DB integration</td>\n<td>RAG systems with Chroma, Milvus, etc.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>graph-store</code></td>\n<td>Graph DB integration</td>\n<td>Knowledge graphs, social networks with Neo4j, ArangoDB</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>search-engine</code></td>\n<td>Full-text search</td>\n<td>BM25-ranked keyword search with SQLite FTS5</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>key-value-store</code></td>\n<td>Key-value storage</td>\n<td>Caching, session management with Redis</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>file-store</code></td>\n<td>File/object storage</td>\n<td>Local filesystem, AWS S3, GCP Storage, Azure Blob with streaming I/O</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>workflow</code></td>\n<td>Call workflows</td>\n<td>Execute other workflows as subroutines</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>shell</code></td>\n<td>Execute shell commands</td>\n<td>Run scripts, system commands</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>text-splitter</code></td>\n<td>Split text</td>\n<td>Split documents into chunks</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>image-processor</code></td>\n<td>Process images</td>\n<td>Image transformation, resizing, etc.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>video-scene-detector</code></td>\n<td>Detect video scenes</td>\n<td>Scene change detection with PySceneDetect, FFmpeg, TransNetV2</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>video-frame-extractor</code></td>\n<td>Extract video frames</td>\n<td>Decode video into PIL frames with sampling and time range support</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>web-scraper</code></td>\n<td>Scrape web pages</td>\n<td>Extract data from websites using CSS/XPath</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>web-browser</code></td>\n<td>Browser automation</td>\n<td>Full browser control via Chrome DevTools Protocol</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Component Selection Guide</h3>\n<p><strong>External API Integration</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>OpenAI, Anthropic, etc. → <code>http-client</code></li>\n<li>Custom REST API → <code>http-client</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Local AI Models</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Local inference → <code>model</code></li>\n<li>vLLM, Ollama, etc. backend usage → <code>http-server</code></li>\n<li>Training → <code>model-trainer</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Data Processing</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Conversation memory → <code>model-memory</code></li>\n<li>Vector storage → <code>vector-store</code></li>\n<li>Graph storage → <code>graph-store</code></li>\n<li>Full-text search → <code>search-engine</code></li>\n<li>Key-value storage → <code>key-value-store</code></li>\n<li>File/object storage → <code>file-store</code></li>\n<li>Text splitting → <code>text-splitter</code></li>\n<li>Image processing → <code>image-processor</code></li>\n<li>Video scene detection → <code>video-scene-detector</code></li>\n<li>Video frame extraction → <code>video-frame-extractor</code></li>\n<li>Web scraping → <code>web-scraper</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Browser Automation</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Full browser control (CDP) → <code>web-browser</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>AI Agents</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Autonomous tool-using agents → <code>agent</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Workflow Composition</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Sub-workflows → <code>workflow</code></li>\n<li>System tasks → <code>shell</code></li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>4.2 Defining Components</h2>\n<h3>Basic Structure</h3>\n<p>All components follow this basic structure:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: unique-component-id\n    type: component-type\n    # Type-specific settings...\n    output:\n      # Output mapping...\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Required Properties</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>id</code>: Unique component identifier</li>\n<li><code>type</code>: Component type</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Optional Properties</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>output</code>: Output data mapping</li>\n<li><code>actions</code>: Multiple action definitions (multi-action component)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Single Action vs Multi-Action Components</h3>\n<p>Components can be defined as single action or multi-action.</p>\n<h4>Single Action Component</h4>\n<p>A component that performs only one task, with action-specific fields wrapped under <code>action:</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: send-email\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.email.com/send\n      method: POST\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.EMAIL_API_KEY}\n      body:\n        to: ${input.to}\n        subject: ${input.subject}\n        body: ${input.body}\n      output: ${response}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Usage:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflow:\n  jobs:\n    - component: send-email\n      input:\n        to: &quot;user@example.com&quot;\n        subject: &quot;Welcome&quot;\n        body: &quot;Hello!&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Multi-Action Component</h4>\n<p>Define multiple tasks within a single component:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: email-service\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.email.com\n    headers:\n      Authorization: Bearer ${env.EMAIL_API_KEY}\n      Content-Type: application/json\n    actions:\n      - id: send\n        path: /send\n        method: POST\n        body:\n          to: ${input.to}\n          subject: ${input.subject}\n          body: ${input.body}\n        output: ${response}\n\n      - id: get-status\n        path: /status/${input.message_id}\n        method: GET\n        output: ${response.status}\n\n      - id: list-templates\n        path: /templates\n        method: GET\n        output: ${response.templates}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Usage:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflow:\n  jobs:\n    - id: send\n      component: email-service\n      action: send\n      input:\n        to: &quot;user@example.com&quot;\n        subject: &quot;Welcome&quot;\n        body: &quot;Hello!&quot;\n      output:\n        message_id: ${output.id}\n\n    - id: check\n      component: email-service\n      action: get-status\n      input:\n        message_id: ${jobs.send.output.message_id}\n</code></pre>\n<h4>When to Use Multi-Action?</h4>\n<p><strong>Multi-action is suitable when:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Using multiple endpoints of the same API service</li>\n<li>Sharing common authentication/headers</li>\n<li>Logically grouping related tasks</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Single action is suitable when:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Simple and independent tasks</li>\n<li>Limited reuse for specific tasks</li>\n<li>Rapid prototyping</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>4.3 Input/Output Mapping</h2>\n<h3>Input Mapping</h3>\n<p>How to pass data to components:</p>\n<h4>Method 1: Direct Mapping</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: translator\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.translate.com/v1/translate\n      body:\n        text: ${input.text}\n        target_lang: ${input.language}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Usage in workflow:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflow:\n  jobs:\n    - component: translator\n      input:\n        text: &quot;Hello&quot;\n        language: &quot;ko&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Method 2: Pass Entire Input</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: processor\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.example.com/process\n      body: ${input}  # Pass entire input as-is\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Output Mapping</h3>\n<p>How to extract component results:</p>\n<h4>Basic Output</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: chatgpt\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions\n      body:\n        model: gpt-4o\n        messages: ${input.messages}\n      output:\n        content: ${response.choices[0].message.content}\n        tokens: ${response.usage.total_tokens}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Usage in workflow:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflow:\n  jobs:\n    - component: chatgpt\n      output:\n        answer: ${output.content}  # Component output's content field\n        usage: ${output.tokens}     # Component output's tokens field\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Full Response Output</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: api-call\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.example.com/data\n      output: ${response}  # Full response\n</code></pre>\n<h4>With Type Conversion</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: image-gen\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.images.com/generate\n      output: ${response.image as image/png;base64}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Input/Output Flow Example</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: step1\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api1.com/process\n      body:\n        data: ${input.raw_data}\n      output:\n        processed: ${response.result}\n\n  - id: step2\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api2.com/analyze\n      body:\n        data: ${input.processed_data}\n      output:\n        analysis: ${response.insights}\n\nworkflow:\n  jobs:\n    - id: process\n      component: step1\n      input:\n        raw_data: ${input.data}\n      output:\n        result: ${output.processed}\n\n    - id: analyze\n      component: step2\n      input:\n        processed_data: ${jobs.process.output.result}\n      output:\n        final: ${output.analysis}\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>4.4 Reusability Patterns</h2>\n<h3>Pattern 1: Separate Components by Model</h3>\n<p>Assign clear responsibilities by separating components by model or service:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  # OpenAI GPT-4o dedicated\n  - id: gpt4o\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n        Content-Type: application/json\n      body:\n        model: gpt-4o\n        messages: ${input.messages}\n        temperature: ${input.temperature | 0.7}\n      output:\n        content: ${response.choices[0].message.content}\n        tokens: ${response.usage.total_tokens}\n\n  # Anthropic Claude dedicated\n  - id: claude\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages\n      headers:\n        x-api-key: ${env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}\n        anthropic-version: &quot;2023-06-01&quot;\n        Content-Type: application/json\n      body:\n        model: claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022\n        messages: ${input.messages}\n        max_tokens: ${input.max_tokens | 1024}\n      output:\n        content: ${response.content[0].text}\n\n  # TTS dedicated\n  - id: elevenlabs-tts\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/${input.voice_id}\n      headers:\n        xi-api-key: ${env.ELEVENLABS_API_KEY}\n        Content-Type: application/json\n      body:\n        text: ${input.text}\n        model_id: eleven_multilingual_v2\n      output: ${response as base64}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Pattern 2: Multi-Action Component</h3>\n<p>Define multiple actions for one service:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: slack\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://slack.com/api\n    headers:\n      Authorization: Bearer ${env.SLACK_TOKEN}\n    actions:\n      - id: send-message\n        path: /chat.postMessage\n        method: POST\n        body:\n          channel: ${input.channel}\n          text: ${input.text}\n        output: ${response}\n\n      - id: list-channels\n        path: /conversations.list\n        method: GET\n        output: ${response.channels}\n\n      - id: get-user\n        path: /users.info\n        method: GET\n        params:\n          user: ${input.user_id}\n        output: ${response.user}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Usage:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflow:\n  jobs:\n    - id: send\n      component: slack\n      action: send-message\n      input:\n        channel: &quot;#general&quot;\n        text: &quot;Hello!&quot;\n\n    - id: list\n      component: slack\n      action: list-channels\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Pattern 3: Component Chaining</h3>\n<p>Compose complex logic by combining small components:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: fetch-data\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.data.com/fetch\n      output: ${response.data}\n\n  - id: process-data\n    type: shell\n    command: [python, process.py, ${input.data}]\n    output:\n      result: ${stdout}\n\n  - id: save-result\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.storage.com/save\n      method: POST\n      body:\n        data: ${input.data}\n      output: ${response}\n\nworkflow:\n  jobs:\n    - id: fetch\n      component: fetch-data\n      output:\n        raw: ${output}\n\n    - id: process\n      component: process-data\n      input:\n        data: ${jobs.fetch.output.raw}\n      output:\n        processed: ${output.result}\n\n    - id: save\n      component: save-result\n      input:\n        data: ${jobs.process.output.processed}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Structure diagram:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-mermaid\">graph LR\n    fetch[&quot;Job: fetch&quot;]\n    process[&quot;Job: process&quot;]\n    save[&quot;Job: save&quot;]\n\n    fetch --&gt;|raw data| process\n    process --&gt;|processed data| save\n\n    fetch -.-&gt; comp1[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;fetch-data]]\n    process -.-&gt; comp2[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;process-data]]\n    save -.-&gt; comp3[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;save-result]]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Pattern 4: Environment-Specific Components</h3>\n<p>Use different endpoints based on environment:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># base.yml\ncomponents:\n  - id: api-client\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: ${env.API_ENDPOINT}/process\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.API_KEY}\n      body: ${input}\n      output: ${response}\n</code></pre>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Development environment\nexport API_ENDPOINT=https://dev-api.example.com\nexport API_KEY=dev-key\nmodel-compose up\n\n# Production environment\nexport API_ENDPOINT=https://api.example.com\nexport API_KEY=prod-key\nmodel-compose up\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Pattern 5: Workflow Modularization</h3>\n<p>Reuse workflows as components:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: preprocess\n    type: workflow\n    workflow: preprocessing\n\nworkflows:\n  - id: preprocessing\n    jobs:\n      - id: clean\n        component: data-cleaner\n      - id: normalize\n        component: normalizer\n\n  - id: main\n    jobs:\n      - id: preprocess\n        component: preprocess\n        input: ${input.raw_data}\n\n      - id: analyze\n        component: analyzer\n        input: ${jobs.preprocess.output}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Structure diagram:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-mermaid\">graph LR\n    subgraph main[&quot;Workflow: main&quot;]\n        direction TB\n        job1[&quot;Job: preprocess&quot;]\n        job2[&quot;Job: analyze&quot;]\n    end\n\n    subgraph wf2[&quot;Workflow: preprocessing&quot;]\n        direction TB\n        job3[&quot;Job: clean&quot;]\n        job4[&quot;Job: normalize&quot;]\n    end\n\n    comp1[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;preprocess]]\n\n    job1 -.-&gt;|①| comp1\n    comp1 -.-&gt;|②| wf2\n    job3 --&gt;|③| job4\n    wf2 -.-&gt;|④| job1\n    job1 --&gt;|⑤| job2\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>4.5 Runtime Configuration</h2>\n<p>Components can execute in different runtime environments depending on your needs. The runtime determines where and how components run.</p>\n<h3>Available Runtimes</h3>\n<p>model-compose supports three runtime types:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Runtime</th>\n<th>Isolation</th>\n<th>Speed</th>\n<th>Overhead</th>\n<th>Best For</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>embedded</code></td>\n<td>None</td>\n<td>Fast</td>\n<td>Minimal</td>\n<td>Lightweight tasks, default choice</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>process</code></td>\n<td>Process-level</td>\n<td>Medium</td>\n<td>Medium</td>\n<td>Heavy models, GPU isolation</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>docker</code></td>\n<td>Container-level</td>\n<td>Slow</td>\n<td>High</td>\n<td>Production deployments</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Embedded Runtime (Default)</h3>\n<p>Runs components in the same process as the controller.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: text-generator\n    type: model\n    runtime: embedded  # or omit (embedded is default)\n    task: text-generation\n    model: gpt2\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>When to use:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Simple API calls</li>\n<li>Lightweight models</li>\n<li>Fast response required</li>\n<li>Development and testing</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Process Runtime</h3>\n<p>Runs components in separate Python processes with isolated memory.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: heavy-model\n    type: model\n    runtime: process\n    task: text-generation\n    model: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>When to use:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Large models (70B+ parameters)</li>\n<li>Multiple GPU utilization</li>\n<li>Blocking operations</li>\n<li>Crash isolation needed</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Advanced configuration:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: model-gpu-0\n    type: model\n    runtime:\n      type: process\n      env:\n        CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES: &quot;0&quot;\n      start_timeout: 120\n      stop_timeout: 30\n    task: image-generation\n    model: stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Multi-GPU example:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: model-gpu-0\n    type: model\n    runtime:\n      type: process\n      env:\n        CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES: &quot;0&quot;\n    model: gpt2-large\n\n  - id: model-gpu-1\n    type: model\n    runtime:\n      type: process\n      env:\n        CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES: &quot;1&quot;\n    model: stabilityai/stable-diffusion-v1-5\n\nworkflows:\n  - id: multi-gpu-workflow\n    jobs:\n      - id: text\n        component: model-gpu-0\n        action: generate\n      - id: image\n        component: model-gpu-1\n        action: generate\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Docker Runtime</h3>\n<p>Runs components in isolated Docker containers.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: isolated-model\n    type: model\n    runtime: docker\n    task: text-generation\n    model: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>When to use:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Production deployments</li>\n<li>Security-critical workloads</li>\n<li>Reproducible environments</li>\n<li>Multi-tenant scenarios</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Runtime Selection Guide</h3>\n<p><strong>Embedded</strong> → Start here for most use cases\n<strong>Process</strong> → Upgrade when you need isolation or heavy workloads\n<strong>Docker</strong> → Use for production and security requirements</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>4.6 Component Best Practices</h2>\n<h3>1. Clear Naming</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># Good\n- id: openai-gpt4o-chat\n- id: elevenlabs-tts-multilingual\n- id: slack-send-message\n\n# Bad\n- id: comp1\n- id: api\n- id: process\n</code></pre>\n<h3>2. Document Input/Output</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: translator\n    type: http-client\n    # Input: { text: string, target_lang: string }\n    # Output: { translated: string, detected_lang: string }\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.translate.com/v1/translate\n      body:\n        text: ${input.text}\n        target: ${input.target_lang}\n      output:\n        translated: ${response.translation}\n        detected_lang: ${response.source_language}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>3. Use Environment Variables</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># Good - Use environment variables\ncomponents:\n  - id: api-client\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: ${env.API_ENDPOINT}\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.API_KEY}\n\n# Bad - Hardcoding\ncomponents:\n  - id: api-client\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.example.com\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer sk-hardcoded-key\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>Next Steps</h2>\n<p>Try it yourself:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Experiment with different component types</li>\n<li>Build a reusable component library</li>\n<li>Break down complex workflows into small components</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<p><strong>Next Chapter</strong>: <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/05-writing-workflows\">5. Writing Workflows</a></p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Chapter 4: Component Configuration"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "user-guide/05-writing-workflows",
