      "html": "<h1>Chapter 5: Writing Workflows</h1>\n<p>This chapter covers how to write workflows in model-compose. From single-job workflows to complex multi-step pipelines, you'll learn about data passing between jobs, conditional execution, streaming mode, and error handling.</p>\n<h2>5.1 What is a Workflow?</h2>\n<p>A <strong>Workflow</strong> is an execution unit that combines one or more jobs to form a complete execution pipeline. When writing a workflow, you need to define three core elements:</p>\n<h3>1. Job Definitions</h3>\n<p>Each job specifies the component to execute and the input to pass to that component.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: my-task\n    component: my-component\n    input:\n      field: ${input.value}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>2. Job Dependencies</h3>\n<p>Use the <code>depends_on</code> field to explicitly define the execution order between jobs. This allows you to create sequential execution, parallel execution, or complex execution graphs.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: task1\n    component: component1\n\n  - id: task2\n    component: component2\n    depends_on: [task1]  # Executes after task1 completes\n</code></pre>\n<h3>3. Input/Output Definitions</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>input</strong>: Maps workflow input or previous job outputs to the current job's input</li>\n<li><strong>output</strong>: Uses the job's result as workflow output or as input for subsequent jobs</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Each job's output is stored in <code>${jobs.job_id.output}</code> and can be referenced as input by subsequent jobs.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: task1\n    component: component1\n    input:\n      data: ${input.user_data}     # Use workflow input\n    output:\n      result: ${output.processed}\n    # Output is stored in jobs.task1.output\n\n  - id: task2\n    component: component2\n    input:\n      data: ${jobs.task1.output.result}  # Use task1's output as input\n    depends_on: [task1]\n</code></pre>\n<p>By combining these three elements, you can build workflows ranging from simple single jobs to complex multi-step pipelines.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>5.2 Single-Job Workflows</h2>\n<p>The simplest form of a workflow contains just one job.</p>\n<h3>Basic Structure</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: simple-workflow\n    jobs:\n      - id: task\n        component: my-component\n        input:\n          field: ${input.value}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Simplified Form</h3>\n<p>When there's only one job, you can omit <code>jobs</code> and the job <code>id</code>. If the <code>id</code> is omitted, it defaults to <code>__job__</code>.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: simple-workflow\n    component: my-component\n    input:\n      field: ${input.value}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Example: Text Generation</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: gpt4o\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n        Content-Type: application/json\n      body:\n        model: gpt-4o\n        messages:\n          - role: user\n            content: ${input.prompt}\n      output:\n        text: ${response.choices[0].message.content}\n\nworkflows:\n  - id: generate-text\n    jobs:\n      - id: generate\n        component: gpt4o\n        input:\n          prompt: ${input.prompt}\n        output:\n          result: ${output.text}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Execution:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose run generate-text --input '{&quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Hello, AI!&quot;}'\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>5.3 Multi-Step Workflows</h2>\n<p>Workflows that execute multiple jobs sequentially.</p>\n<h3>Job Dependencies (depends_on)</h3>\n<p>Use the <code>depends_on</code> field to explicitly define the execution order between jobs. This field specifies a list of job IDs that must complete before the current job starts.</p>\n<p><strong>Basic format:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">depends_on: [job-id-1, job-id-2]\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Key features:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Can specify dependencies on multiple jobs as an array</li>\n<li>Executes after all dependent jobs complete</li>\n<li>Jobs without dependencies can run in parallel</li>\n<li>Circular dependencies are not allowed</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Sequential Execution</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: multi-step\n    jobs:\n      - id: step1\n        component: component1\n        input: ${input}\n        output:\n          data1: ${output}\n\n      - id: step2\n        component: component2\n        input:\n          data: ${jobs.step1.output.data1}\n        output:\n          data2: ${output}\n        depends_on: [step1]  # Executes after step1 completes\n\n      - id: step3\n        component: component3\n        input:\n          data: ${jobs.step2.output.data2}\n        depends_on: [step2]  # Executes after step2 completes\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Parallel Execution</h3>\n<p>Jobs without dependencies run concurrently:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: parallel-workflow\n    jobs:\n      - id: task-a\n        component: component-a\n        input: ${input}\n        output:\n          result-a: ${output}\n\n      - id: task-b\n        component: component-b\n        input: ${input}\n        output:\n          result-b: ${output}\n      # task-a and task-b run in parallel\n\n      - id: combine\n        component: combiner\n        input:\n          data-a: ${jobs.task-a.output.result-a}\n          data-b: ${jobs.task-b.output.result-b}\n        depends_on: [task-a, task-b]  # Executes after both tasks complete\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Complex Dependency Graph</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: complex-workflow\n    jobs:\n      - id: fetch-data\n        component: data-fetcher\n        output:\n          raw: ${output}\n\n      - id: process-1\n        component: processor-1\n        input: ${jobs.fetch-data.output.raw}\n        depends_on: [fetch-data]\n        output:\n          processed-1: ${output}\n\n      - id: process-2\n        component: processor-2\n        input: ${jobs.fetch-data.output.raw}\n        depends_on: [fetch-data]\n        output:\n          processed-2: ${output}\n\n      - id: merge\n        component: merger\n        input:\n          data-1: ${jobs.process-1.output.processed-1}\n          data-2: ${jobs.process-2.output.processed-2}\n        depends_on: [process-1, process-2]\n        output:\n          merged: ${output}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Structure diagram:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-mermaid\">graph TB\n    fetch[&quot;Job: fetch-data&quot;]\n    proc1[&quot;Job: process-1&quot;]\n    proc2[&quot;Job: process-2&quot;]\n    merge[&quot;Job: merge&quot;]\n\n    fetch --&gt; proc1\n    fetch --&gt; proc2\n    proc1 --&gt; merge\n    proc2 --&gt; merge\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Example: Text Generation and Speech Synthesis</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: text-generator\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n        Content-Type: application/json\n      body:\n        model: gpt-4o\n        messages:\n          - role: user\n            content: ${input.prompt}\n      output:\n        text: ${response.choices[0].message.content}\n\n  - id: text-to-speech\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/${input.voice_id}\n      headers:\n        xi-api-key: ${env.ELEVENLABS_API_KEY}\n        Content-Type: application/json\n      body:\n        text: ${input.text}\n        model_id: eleven_multilingual_v2\n      output: ${response as base64}\n\nworkflows:\n  - id: text-to-voice\n    jobs:\n      - id: generate\n        component: text-generator\n        input:\n          prompt: ${input.prompt}\n        output:\n          text: ${output.text}\n\n      - id: synthesize\n        component: text-to-speech\n        input:\n          text: ${jobs.generate.output.text}\n          voice_id: ${input.voice_id}\n        output:\n          audio: ${output}\n        depends_on: [ generate ]\n</code></pre>\n<p>Structure diagram:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-mermaid\">graph LR\n    job1[&quot;Job: generate&quot;]\n    job2[&quot;Job: synthesize&quot;]\n\n    job1 --&gt;|text| job2\n\n    job1 -.-&gt; comp1[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;text-generator]]\n    job2 -.-&gt; comp2[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;text-to-speech]]\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>5.4 Data Passing Between Jobs</h2>\n<p>How to pass data between jobs in a workflow.</p>\n<h3>Variable Binding Syntax</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${input.field}              # Workflow input\n${output.field}             # Current job output\n${jobs.job-id.output.field} # Specific job output\n${env.VAR_NAME}             # Environment variable\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Example: Complex Data Passing</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: data-pipeline\n    jobs:\n      - id: fetch\n        component: data-fetcher\n        input:\n          url: ${input.source_url}\n        output:\n          raw_data: ${output.data}\n          metadata: ${output.meta}\n\n      - id: transform\n        component: data-transformer\n        input:\n          data: ${jobs.fetch.output.raw_data}\n          options:\n            format: json\n            encoding: utf-8\n        output:\n          transformed: ${output.result}\n        depends_on: [ fetch ]\n\n      - id: save\n        component: data-saver\n        input:\n          data: ${jobs.transform.output.transformed}\n          metadata: ${jobs.fetch.output.metadata}\n          destination: ${input.target_path}\n        depends_on: [ transform, fetch ]\n</code></pre>\n<p>Structure diagram:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-mermaid\">graph LR\n    fetch[&quot;Job: fetch&quot;]\n    transform[&quot;Job: transform&quot;]\n    save[&quot;Job: save&quot;]\n\n    fetch --&gt;|raw_data| transform\n    fetch --&gt;|metadata| save\n    transform --&gt;|transformed| save\n\n    fetch -.-&gt; comp1[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;data-fetcher]]\n    transform -.-&gt; comp2[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;data-transformer]]\n    save -.-&gt; comp3[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;data-saver]]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Type Conversion</h3>\n<p>You can apply type conversions during data passing:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: image-workflow\n    jobs:\n      - id: generate\n        component: image-generator\n        output:\n          image_base64: ${output as base64}\n\n      - id: process\n        component: image-processor\n        input:\n          image: ${jobs.generate.output.image_base64 as image/png;base64}\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>5.5 Job Types</h2>\n<p>model-compose provides various job types to support different task patterns.</p>\n<h3>Available Job Types</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Purpose</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>component</code></td>\n<td>Component execution</td>\n<td>Invoke a component to perform a task (default type)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>if</code></td>\n<td>Conditional branching</td>\n<td>Route to different jobs based on a condition</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>switch</code></td>\n<td>Multi-way branching</td>\n<td>Route to one of many paths based on a value</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>delay</code></td>\n<td>Wait</td>\n<td>Wait for a specified duration</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>filter</code></td>\n<td>Data restructuring</td>\n<td>Extract and restructure data into a new shape</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>random-router</code></td>\n<td>Random routing</td>\n<td>Randomly select one job</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note</strong>: If <code>type</code> is not specified, it defaults to <code>component</code>.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Component Job</h3>\n<p>The default job type that executes a component. If <code>type</code> is omitted, the job is treated as a component job.</p>\n<h4>Fields</h4>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>component</code></td>\n<td><code>string</code> or object</td>\n<td><code>&quot;__default__&quot;</code></td>\n<td>The component to run. Either a string ID referencing a defined component, or an inline component config object.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>action</code></td>\n<td><code>string</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;__default__&quot;</code></td>\n<td>The action to invoke on the component. For components with multiple actions, specify which one to call.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>input</code></td>\n<td>any</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Input data supplied to the component. Supports variable binding (<code>${input.field}</code>, <code>${jobs.*.output}</code>).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>output</code></td>\n<td>any</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Output mapping. Extracts and reshapes the component's output for use by subsequent jobs.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>repeat_count</code></td>\n<td><code>int</code> or <code>string</code></td>\n<td><code>1</code></td>\n<td>Number of times to repeat the component execution. Must be at least 1. Supports variable binding.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>interrupt</code></td>\n<td>object</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Human-in-the-loop interrupt configuration. See <a href=\"#interrupt-human-in-the-loop\">Interrupt</a> below.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>depends_on</code></td>\n<td><code>string[]</code></td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>List of job IDs that must complete before this job runs.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h4>Basic Structure</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: my-task\n    type: component  # Optional (default)\n    component: my-component\n    action: my-action  # For multi-action components\n    input: ${input}\n    output:\n      result: ${output}\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Inline Component</h4>\n<p>Instead of referencing a predefined component by ID, you can define the component inline:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: my-task\n    component:\n      type: http-client\n      action:\n        endpoint: https://api.example.com/run\n        body:\n          data: ${input.data}\n        output: ${response.result}\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Repeat Execution</h4>\n<p>Run a component multiple times with the same input. Results are collected into an array:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: generate-variants\n    component: text-generator\n    input:\n      prompt: ${input.prompt}\n    repeat_count: 3\n</code></pre>\n<p>The <code>repeat_count</code> also supports variable binding:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">repeat_count: ${input.count}\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Interrupt (Human-in-the-Loop)</h4>\n<p>Component jobs support an <code>interrupt</code> field that pauses workflow execution at defined points and waits for external input before continuing. This enables human-in-the-loop patterns such as approval gates, data review, or interactive editing.</p>\n<p><strong>Basic structure:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: my-task\n    component: my-component\n    input: ${input}\n    interrupt:\n      before: true   # Pause before component executes\n      after: true    # Pause after component executes\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Interrupt phases:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Phase</th>\n<th>Timing</th>\n<th>Resume data effect</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>before</code></td>\n<td>Before the component runs</td>\n<td>Replaces the job's input</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>after</code></td>\n<td>After the component runs</td>\n<td>Replaces the job's output</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Configuration options:</strong></p>\n<p>Each phase accepts either <code>true</code> (always interrupt) or a detailed configuration:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">interrupt:\n  before:\n    message: &quot;Review the input before processing&quot;\n    metadata:\n      preview: ${input.data}\n  after:\n    condition:\n      operator: gt\n      input: ${output.confidence}\n      value: 0.5\n    message: &quot;Low confidence result. Please review.&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li><strong><code>message</code></strong>: A message displayed to the user or client when the interrupt fires.</li>\n<li><strong><code>metadata</code></strong>: Structured data passed to the client (e.g., preview data, options).</li>\n<li><strong><code>condition</code></strong>: An optional condition that must evaluate to true for the interrupt to fire. Uses the same operators as <a href=\"#if-job\">If Job</a> (<code>eq</code>, <code>neq</code>, <code>gt</code>, <code>gte</code>, <code>lt</code>, <code>lte</code>, <code>in</code>, <code>not-in</code>, <code>match</code>). If omitted, the interrupt always fires.</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Task states:</strong></p>\n<p>When a workflow hits an interrupt, the task transitions through these states:</p>\n<pre><code>PENDING → PROCESSING → INTERRUPTED → PROCESSING → ... → COMPLETED / FAILED\n</code></pre>\n<p>The task remains in the <code>INTERRUPTED</code> state until it is resumed via the CLI, HTTP API, or MCP tool.</p>\n<p><strong>Resuming via HTTP API:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/tasks/{task_id}/resume \\\n  -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; \\\n  -d '{&quot;job_id&quot;: &quot;my-task&quot;, &quot;data&quot;: {&quot;revised&quot;: &quot;value&quot;}}'\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Resuming via CLI:</strong></p>\n<p>When using <code>model-compose run</code>, the CLI automatically prompts for input at interrupt points. Use <code>--auto-resume</code> to skip prompts. See <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/03-cli-usage#interrupt-handling\">Chapter 3: CLI Usage</a> for details.</p>\n<p><strong>Example: Shell command with human approval:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflow:\n  jobs:\n    - id: run-command\n      component: shell-executor\n      input:\n        command: ls -la\n      interrupt:\n        before:\n          message: &quot;About to execute: ls -la&quot;\n          metadata:\n            command: ls -la\n        after:\n          message: &quot;Command finished. Review the output above.&quot;\n      output:\n        result: ${output as text}\n\ncomponent:\n  id: shell-executor\n  type: shell\n  action:\n    command: [&quot;sh&quot;, &quot;-c&quot;, &quot;${input.command}&quot;]\n    output: ${result.stdout}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Structure diagram:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-mermaid\">graph LR\n    start([&quot;Start&quot;]) --&gt; before{&quot;Interrupt&lt;br/&gt;(before)&quot;}\n    before --&gt;|resumed| exec[&quot;Execute&lt;br/&gt;component&quot;]\n    exec --&gt; after{&quot;Interrupt&lt;br/&gt;(after)&quot;}\n    after --&gt;|resumed| done([&quot;Done&quot;])\n</code></pre>\n<h3>If Job</h3>\n<p>Branch to different jobs based on a condition. Conditions are evaluated in order; the first match determines the routing target.</p>\n<h4>Fields</h4>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>conditions</code></td>\n<td><code>IfCondition[]</code></td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>List of conditions to evaluate in order.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>otherwise</code></td>\n<td><code>string</code></td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Job ID to route to if no conditions matched.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>depends_on</code></td>\n<td><code>string[]</code></td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Jobs that must complete before this job runs.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>IfCondition fields:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>operator</code></td>\n<td><code>string</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;eq&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Comparison operator (see below).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>input</code></td>\n<td>any</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Value to evaluate. Supports variable binding.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>value</code></td>\n<td>any</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Value to compare against. Supports variable binding.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>if_true</code></td>\n<td><code>string</code></td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Job ID to route to when the condition is true.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>if_false</code></td>\n<td><code>string</code></td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Job ID to route to when the condition is false.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h4>Supported Operators</h4>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Operator</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>eq</code></td>\n<td>Equal</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>neq</code></td>\n<td>Not equal</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>gt</code></td>\n<td>Greater than</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>gte</code></td>\n<td>Greater than or equal</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>lt</code></td>\n<td>Less than</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>lte</code></td>\n<td>Less than or equal</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>in</code></td>\n<td>Contained in value</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>not-in</code></td>\n<td>Not contained in value</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>starts-with</code></td>\n<td>Starts with</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ends-with</code></td>\n<td>Ends with</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>match</code></td>\n<td>Regex match</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h4>Single Condition (Shorthand)</h4>\n<p>When there is only one condition, you can write the condition fields directly on the job without wrapping in <code>conditions</code>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: condition-check\n    type: if\n    operator: eq\n    input: ${input.value}\n    value: &quot;expected&quot;\n    if_true: job-when-true\n    if_false: job-when-false\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Multiple Conditions</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: multi-condition\n    type: if\n    conditions:\n      - operator: gt\n        input: ${input.score}\n        value: 80\n        if_true: excellent-handler\n      - operator: gt\n        input: ${input.score}\n        value: 60\n        if_true: good-handler\n    otherwise: need-improvement-handler\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Switch Job</h3>\n<p>Route to one of many paths based on exact value matching. Like a switch-case statement.</p>\n<h4>Fields</h4>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>input</code></td>\n<td>any</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Value to match against cases. Supports variable binding.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>cases</code></td>\n<td><code>SwitchCase[]</code></td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>List of cases to evaluate.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>otherwise</code></td>\n<td><code>string</code></td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Job ID to route to if no cases match.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>depends_on</code></td>\n<td><code>string[]</code></td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Jobs that must complete before this job runs.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>SwitchCase fields:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>value</code></td>\n<td><code>string</code></td>\n<td>Value to match against the input.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>then</code></td>\n<td><code>string</code></td>\n<td>Job ID to route to if the value matches.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h4>Single Case (Shorthand)</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: check-type\n    type: switch\n    input: ${input.type}\n    value: &quot;image&quot;\n    then: process-image\n    otherwise: process-other\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Multiple Cases</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: route-by-type\n    type: switch\n    input: ${input.type}\n    cases:\n      - value: &quot;image&quot;\n        then: process-image\n      - value: &quot;video&quot;\n        then: process-video\n      - value: &quot;audio&quot;\n        then: process-audio\n    otherwise: process-unknown\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Delay Job</h3>\n<p>Wait for a specified duration or until a specific time. Has two modes selected by the <code>mode</code> field.</p>\n<h4>Fields (time-interval)</h4>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mode</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;time-interval&quot;</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Wait for a duration.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>duration</code></td>\n<td><code>number</code> or <code>string</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Time to wait in milliseconds. Supports variable binding.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>output</code></td>\n<td>any</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Optional output mapping.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>depends_on</code></td>\n<td><code>string[]</code></td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Jobs that must complete before this job runs.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: wait\n    type: delay\n    mode: time-interval\n    duration: 5000  # 5 seconds\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Fields (specific-time)</h4>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mode</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;specific-time&quot;</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Wait until a specific date/time.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>time</code></td>\n<td><code>datetime</code> or <code>string</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Target date and time (ISO 8601 format). Supports variable binding.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>timezone</code></td>\n<td><code>string</code></td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Timezone identifier (e.g., <code>&quot;Asia/Seoul&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;UTC&quot;</code>).</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>output</code></td>\n<td>any</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Optional output mapping.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>depends_on</code></td>\n<td><code>string[]</code></td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Jobs that must complete before this job runs.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: wait-until\n    type: delay\n    mode: specific-time\n    time: &quot;2024-12-25T09:00:00&quot;\n    timezone: &quot;Asia/Seoul&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Filter Job</h3>\n<p>Extract parts of data and restructure into a new shape. Does not execute any component — it only transforms data using variable bindings.</p>\n<h4>Fields</h4>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>output</code></td>\n<td>any</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Output mapping that defines the new data shape. Uses variable binding to extract values from workflow input or previous job outputs.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>depends_on</code></td>\n<td><code>string[]</code></td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Jobs that must complete before this job runs.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: reshape-data\n    type: filter\n    output:\n      user_id: ${input.user.id}\n      user_name: ${input.user.profile.name}\n      score: ${input.metrics.score}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Random Router Job</h3>\n<p>Randomly select one of multiple jobs. Supports uniform (equal probability) and weighted (custom probability) modes.</p>\n<h4>Fields</h4>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mode</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;uniform&quot;</code> or <code>&quot;weighted&quot;</code></td>\n<td><code>&quot;uniform&quot;</code></td>\n<td>Routing mode. <code>uniform</code> gives equal probability; <code>weighted</code> uses the <code>weight</code> field of each route.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>routings</code></td>\n<td><code>Routing[]</code></td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>List of possible routing destinations.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>depends_on</code></td>\n<td><code>string[]</code></td>\n<td><code>[]</code></td>\n<td>Jobs that must complete before this job runs.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Routing fields:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>target</code></td>\n<td><code>string</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Destination job ID.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>weight</code></td>\n<td><code>number</code></td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Relative weight for weighted mode. Ignored in uniform mode.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h4>Uniform Distribution</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: ab-test\n    type: random-router\n    mode: uniform\n    routings:\n      - target: variant-a\n      - target: variant-b\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Weighted Distribution (70:20:10)</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: traffic-split\n    type: random-router\n    mode: weighted\n    routings:\n      - target: primary-model\n        weight: 70\n      - target: experimental-model\n        weight: 20\n      - target: fallback-model\n        weight: 10\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note</strong>: Weight values don't need to sum to 100. They work as relative ratios.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<hr />\n<h2>5.6 Conditional Execution</h2>\n<p>Using If and Switch jobs to control execution flow based on conditions.</p>\n<h3>Example 1: Content Filtering with If Job</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: content-moderator\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.openai.com/v1/moderations\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n        Content-Type: application/json\n      body:\n        input: ${input.text}\n      output:\n        flagged: ${response.results[0].flagged}\n\n  - id: text-processor\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n        Content-Type: application/json\n      body:\n        model: gpt-4o\n        messages:\n          - role: user\n            content: ${input.text}\n      output:\n        result: ${response.choices[0].message.content}\n\n  - id: rejection-handler\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.example.com/log-rejection\n      method: POST\n      body:\n        text: ${input.text}\n        reason: &quot;content_flagged&quot;\n      output: ${response}\n\nworkflows:\n  - id: safe-processing\n    jobs:\n      - id: moderate\n        component: content-moderator\n        input:\n          text: ${input.text}\n        output:\n          flagged: ${output.flagged}\n\n      - id: check-safety\n        type: if\n        operator: eq\n        input: ${jobs.moderate.output.flagged}\n        value: false\n        if_true: process\n        if_false: reject\n        depends_on: [ moderate ]\n\n      - id: process\n        component: text-processor\n        input:\n          text: ${input.text}\n        output:\n          result: ${output.result}\n\n      - id: reject\n        component: rejection-handler\n        input:\n          text: ${input.text}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Structure diagram:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-mermaid\">graph TB\n    moderate[&quot;Job: moderate&lt;br/&gt;(action)&quot;]\n    check[&quot;Job: check-safety&lt;br/&gt;(if)&quot;]\n    process[&quot;Job: process&lt;br/&gt;(action)&quot;]\n    reject[&quot;Job: reject&lt;br/&gt;(action)&quot;]\n\n    moderate --&gt; check\n    check --&gt;|flagged=false| process\n    check --&gt;|flagged=true| reject\n\n    moderate -.-&gt; comp1[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;content-moderator]]\n    process -.-&gt; comp2[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;text-processor]]\n    reject -.-&gt; comp3[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;rejection-handler]]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Example 2: Media Type Processing with Switch Job</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: image-processor\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.example.com/process-image\n      body:\n        image: ${input.data}\n      output: ${response}\n\n  - id: video-processor\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.example.com/process-video\n      body:\n        video: ${input.data}\n      output: ${response}\n\n  - id: audio-processor\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.example.com/process-audio\n      body:\n        audio: ${input.data}\n      output: ${response}\n\n  - id: default-processor\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.example.com/process-unknown\n      body:\n        data: ${input.data}\n      output: ${response}\n\nworkflows:\n  - id: media-processing\n    jobs:\n      - id: route-by-type\n        type: switch\n        input: ${input.media_type}\n        cases:\n          - value: &quot;image&quot;\n            then: process-image\n          - value: &quot;video&quot;\n            then: process-video\n          - value: &quot;audio&quot;\n            then: process-audio\n        otherwise: process-unknown\n\n      - id: process-image\n        component: image-processor\n        input:\n          data: ${input.data}\n        depends_on: [ route-by-type ]\n\n      - id: process-video\n        component: video-processor\n        input:\n          data: ${input.data}\n        depends_on: [ route-by-type ]\n\n      - id: process-audio\n        component: audio-processor\n        input:\n          data: ${input.data}\n        depends_on: [ route-by-type ]\n\n      - id: process-unknown\n        component: default-processor\n        input:\n          data: ${input.data}\n        depends_on: [ route-by-type ]\n</code></pre>\n<p>Structure diagram:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-mermaid\">graph TB\n    route[&quot;Job: route-by-type&lt;br/&gt;(switch)&quot;]\n    img[&quot;Job: process-image&quot;]\n    vid[&quot;Job: process-video&quot;]\n    aud[&quot;Job: process-audio&quot;]\n    unk[&quot;Job: process-unknown&quot;]\n\n    route --&gt;|&quot;image&quot;| img\n    route --&gt;|&quot;video&quot;| vid\n    route --&gt;|&quot;audio&quot;| aud\n    route --&gt;|&quot;otherwise&quot;| unk\n\n    img -.-&gt; comp1[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;image-processor]]\n    vid -.-&gt; comp2[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;video-processor]]\n    aud -.-&gt; comp3[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;audio-processor]]\n    unk -.-&gt; comp4[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;default-processor]]\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>5.7 Streaming Mode</h2>\n<p>When components support streaming, you can stream data in real-time.</p>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>For more details, see <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/13-streaming-mode\">Chapter 13: Streaming Mode</a>.</strong></p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Streaming Configuration in Components</h3>\n<h4>Model Components</h4>\n<p>Model components enable streaming by setting <code>streaming: true</code> at the component level:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: local-llm\n    type: model\n    task: text-generation\n    model:\n      provider: huggingface\n      repository: meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf\n      token: ${env.HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN}\n    streaming: true  # Enable streaming\n    action:\n      text: ${input.prompt}\n</code></pre>\n<h4>HTTP Components</h4>\n<p><code>http-client</code> and <code>http-server</code> components automatically switch to streaming mode when the API returns a stream response:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: gpt4o-stream\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n        Content-Type: application/json\n      body:\n        model: gpt-4o\n        messages: ${input.messages}\n        stream: true  # Request streaming from API\n      output: ${response}\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note</strong>: <code>http-client</code> and <code>http-server</code> automatically detect stream responses from APIs, so no explicit <code>streaming</code> setting is needed.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Using Streaming in Workflows</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: chat\n    jobs:\n      - id: respond\n        component: gpt4o-stream\n        input:\n          messages: ${input.messages}\n    output: ${output}\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note</strong>: If a component's output is a stream, the job's output is also a stream. If the last job's output is a stream, the workflow output is also returned as a stream.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>Requesting Streaming via HTTP API</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/workflows/runs \\\n  -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; \\\n  -d '{\n    &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;chat&quot;,\n    &quot;input&quot;: {\n      &quot;messages&quot;: [\n        {&quot;role&quot;: &quot;user&quot;, &quot;content&quot;: &quot;Tell me a story&quot;}\n      ]\n    }\n  }'\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note</strong>: Streaming responses are delivered in Server-Sent Events (SSE) format.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<hr />\n<h2>5.8 Error Handling</h2>\n<p>Handle errors that may occur during workflow execution.</p>\n<h3>Retry Configuration</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: resilient-workflow\n    jobs:\n      - id: api-call\n        component: external-api\n        retry:\n          max_retry_count: 3\n          delay: 1000  # milliseconds\n          backoff: exponential\n        input: ${input}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Fallback Handling</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: fallback-workflow\n    jobs:\n      - id: primary\n        component: primary-service\n        input: ${input}\n        on_error: continue\n\n      - id: fallback\n        component: fallback-service\n        condition: ${jobs.primary.error}\n        input: ${input}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Example: Multi-Model Fallback</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: gpt4o\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n        Content-Type: application/json\n      body:\n        model: gpt-4o\n        messages: ${input.messages}\n      output:\n        text: ${response.choices[0].message.content}\n\n  - id: claude\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages\n      headers:\n        x-api-key: ${env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}\n        anthropic-version: &quot;2023-06-01&quot;\n        Content-Type: application/json\n      body:\n        model: claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022\n        messages: ${input.messages}\n        max_tokens: 1024\n      output:\n        text: ${response.content[0].text}\n\nworkflows:\n  - id: robust-chat\n    jobs:\n      - id: try-gpt4o\n        component: gpt4o\n        retry:\n          max_retry_count: 2\n          delay: 500\n        input:\n          messages: ${input.messages}\n        output:\n          result: ${output.text}\n        on_error: continue\n\n      - id: fallback-claude\n        component: claude\n        condition: ${jobs.try-gpt4o.error}\n        input:\n          messages: ${input.messages}\n        output:\n          result: ${output.text}\n        depends_on: [ try-gpt4o ]\n</code></pre>\n<p>Structure diagram:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-mermaid\">graph TB\n    try[&quot;Job: try-gpt4o&lt;br/&gt;(retry: 2)&quot;]\n    fallback[&quot;Job: fallback-claude&quot;]\n\n    try --&gt;|success| output[Output]\n    try --&gt;|error| fallback\n    fallback --&gt; output\n\n    try -.-&gt; comp1[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;gpt4o]]\n    fallback -.-&gt; comp2[[Component:&lt;br/&gt;claude]]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Accessing Error Information</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: error-logging\n    jobs:\n      - id: risky-operation\n        component: risky-api\n        input: ${input}\n        on_error: continue\n\n      - id: log-error\n        component: error-logger\n        condition: ${jobs.risky-operation.error}\n        input:\n          error_message: ${jobs.risky-operation.error.message}\n          error_code: ${jobs.risky-operation.error.code}\n          timestamp: ${jobs.risky-operation.error.timestamp}\n        depends_on: [ risky-operation ]\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>5.9 Workflow Best Practices</h2>\n<h3>1. Clear Job Names</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># Good\nworkflows:\n  - id: user-onboarding\n    jobs:\n      - id: validate-email\n        component: email-validator\n      - id: create-account\n        component: account-creator\n      - id: send-welcome-email\n        component: email-sender\n\n# Bad\nworkflows:\n  - id: workflow1\n    jobs:\n      - id: step1\n        component: comp1\n      - id: step2\n        component: comp2\n</code></pre>\n<h3>2. Job Decomposition</h3>\n<p>Break complex logic into smaller jobs:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># Good - Clear step separation\nworkflows:\n  - id: content-pipeline\n    jobs:\n      - id: fetch-content\n        component: content-fetcher\n      - id: validate-content\n        component: content-validator\n      - id: transform-content\n        component: content-transformer\n      - id: publish-content\n        component: content-publisher\n\n# Bad - One monolithic job\nworkflows:\n  - id: content-pipeline\n    jobs:\n      - id: process-everything\n        component: monolithic-processor\n</code></pre>\n<h3>3. Reusable Workflows</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: preprocessing-workflow\n    type: workflow\n    workflow: preprocessing\n\nworkflows:\n  - id: preprocessing\n    jobs:\n      - id: clean\n        component: data-cleaner\n      - id: normalize\n        component: data-normalizer\n\n  - id: analysis\n    jobs:\n      - id: preprocess\n        component: preprocessing-workflow\n        input: ${input.raw_data}\n      - id: analyze\n        component: analyzer\n        input: ${jobs.preprocess.output}\n        depends_on: [ preprocess ]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>4. Document Inputs and Outputs</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: image-generation\n    # Input: { prompt: string, style: string, size: string }\n    # Output: { image_url: string, width: number, height: number }\n    jobs:\n      - id: generate\n        component: image-generator\n        input:\n          prompt: ${input.prompt}\n          style: ${input.style}\n          size: ${input.size}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>5. Consider Error Handling</h3>\n<p>Always add retry or fallback logic for critical jobs:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: critical-workflow\n    jobs:\n      - id: important-task\n        component: critical-service\n        retry:\n          max_retry_count: 3\n          delay: 1000\n        on_error: continue\n\n      - id: fallback-task\n        component: backup-service\n        condition: ${jobs.important-task.error}\n        depends_on: [ important-task ]\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>Next Steps</h2>\n<p>Try it out:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Start with simple single-job workflows</li>\n<li>Gradually expand to complex multi-step workflows</li>\n<li>Add error handling and retry logic</li>\n<li>Build reusable workflow components</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<p><strong>Next Chapter</strong>: <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/06-workflow-schema\">6. Workflow Schema</a></p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Chapter 5: Writing Workflows"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "user-guide/06-workflow-schema",
      "html": "<h1>Chapter 6: Workflow Schema</h1>\n<p>This chapter explains how model-compose automatically generates workflow schemas that describe the input and output variables of each workflow. You'll learn how to retrieve schemas via the API and how to leverage them for client integration, Web UI rendering, and MCP tool mapping.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>6.1 What is a Workflow Schema?</h2>\n<p>A <strong>Workflow Schema</strong> is a metadata structure that model-compose automatically infers from your workflow configuration. It describes:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Input Variables</strong>: What data the workflow expects when invoked</li>\n<li><strong>Output Variables</strong>: What data the workflow produces upon completion</li>\n</ul>\n<p>The schema is derived by analyzing the variable binding expressions (<code>${input.field as type}</code>) in your workflow's job definitions. You don't need to write the schema manually — model-compose generates it for you.</p>\n<h3>Why Schemas Matter</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Use Case</th>\n<th>How Schema is Used</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Web UI</td>\n<td>Automatically generates input forms (text fields, file uploads, dropdowns)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>MCP Server</td>\n<td>Maps workflow inputs to tool parameters</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>REST API Clients</td>\n<td>Provides type information for request/response validation</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Documentation</td>\n<td>Self-describing API contracts</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>6.2 Retrieving the Schema</h2>\n<h3>Single Workflow Schema</h3>\n<pre><code>GET /workflows/{workflow_id}/schema\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Example:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl http://localhost:8080/workflows/my-workflow/schema\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Response:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;my-workflow&quot;,\n  &quot;title&quot;: &quot;My Workflow&quot;,\n  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;A sample workflow&quot;,\n  &quot;input&quot;: [\n    {\n      &quot;name&quot;: &quot;prompt&quot;,\n      &quot;type&quot;: &quot;text&quot;\n    },\n    {\n      &quot;name&quot;: &quot;temperature&quot;,\n      &quot;type&quot;: &quot;number&quot;,\n      &quot;default&quot;: 0.7\n    }\n  ],\n  &quot;output&quot;: [\n    {\n      &quot;name&quot;: &quot;result&quot;,\n      &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot;\n    }\n  ],\n  &quot;default&quot;: true\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>All Workflow Schemas</h3>\n<pre><code>GET /workflows?include_schema=true\n</code></pre>\n<p>Returns an array of schema objects for all public workflows.</p>\n<h3>Workflow List (Without Schema)</h3>\n<pre><code>GET /workflows\n</code></pre>\n<p>Returns a simplified list with only <code>workflow_id</code>, <code>title</code>, and <code>default</code> fields.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>6.3 Input Schema</h2>\n<p>The input schema describes the variables that must be provided when executing a workflow.</p>\n<h3>Variable Structure</h3>\n<p>Each input variable has the following fields:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>name</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>Variable name (derived from <code>${input.name}</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>type</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>Data type of the variable</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>subtype</code></td>\n<td>string?</td>\n<td>Subtype qualifier (e.g., <code>pcm</code> for audio)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>format</code></td>\n<td>string?</td>\n<td>Transfer format (<code>base64</code>, <code>url</code>, <code>path</code>, <code>stream</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>default</code></td>\n<td>any?</td>\n<td>Default value if not provided</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Supported Types</h3>\n<p><strong>Primitive Types:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n<th>Example Use</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>string</code></td>\n<td>Short text string</td>\n<td>Names, IDs, labels</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>text</code></td>\n<td>Long text (multi-line)</td>\n<td>Prompts, documents</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>integer</code></td>\n<td>Whole number</td>\n<td>Counts, indices</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>number</code></td>\n<td>Floating-point number</td>\n<td>Temperature, scores</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>boolean</code></td>\n<td>True/false</td>\n<td>Feature flags</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>list</code></td>\n<td>Array of values</td>\n<td>Tags, keywords</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>json</code></td>\n<td>Arbitrary JSON object</td>\n<td>Complex structured data</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>object[]</code></td>\n<td>Array of objects with projected fields</td>\n<td>Table data</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Encoded Types:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>base64</code></td>\n<td>Base64-encoded binary data</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>markdown</code></td>\n<td>Markdown-formatted text</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Media Types:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>image</code></td>\n<td>Image file (PNG, JPEG, etc.)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>audio</code></td>\n<td>Audio file (WAV, MP3, etc.)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>video</code></td>\n<td>Video file (MP4, etc.)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>file</code></td>\n<td>Generic file</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Streaming Types:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>sse-text</code></td>\n<td>Server-Sent Events (text chunks)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>sse-json</code></td>\n<td>Server-Sent Events (JSON chunks)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>UI Types:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>select</code></td>\n<td>Dropdown selection (options defined via subtype)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Format Values</h3>\n<p>The <code>format</code> field specifies how data is transferred:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Format</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>base64</code></td>\n<td>Data is base64-encoded in the request body</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>url</code></td>\n<td>Data is referenced by URL</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>path</code></td>\n<td>Data is referenced by file path</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stream</code></td>\n<td>Data is delivered as a stream</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>How Input Schema is Inferred</h3>\n<p>model-compose analyzes variable binding expressions in job <code>input</code> fields:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: example\n    jobs:\n      - id: task\n        component: my-component\n        input:\n          prompt: ${input.prompt as text}\n          image: ${input.photo as image;base64}\n          count: ${input.count as integer | 5}\n</code></pre>\n<p>This produces the following input schema:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;input&quot;: [\n    { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;prompt&quot;, &quot;type&quot;: &quot;text&quot; },\n    { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;photo&quot;, &quot;type&quot;: &quot;image&quot;, &quot;format&quot;: &quot;base64&quot; },\n    { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;count&quot;, &quot;type&quot;: &quot;integer&quot;, &quot;default&quot;: 5 }\n  ]\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Inference rules:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>${input.name}</code> → type defaults to <code>string</code></li>\n<li><code>${input.name as type}</code> → uses the specified type</li>\n<li><code>${input.name as type;format}</code> → includes format</li>\n<li><code>${input.name as type | default}</code> → includes default value</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>6.4 Output Schema</h2>\n<p>The output schema describes the data returned when the workflow completes. It is inferred from the <strong>terminal jobs</strong> — jobs that no other job depends on.</p>\n<h3>Basic Output</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: summarize\n    jobs:\n      - id: generate\n        component: gpt4o\n        input:\n          prompt: ${input.text as text}\n        output:\n          summary: ${output as markdown}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Produces:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;output&quot;: [\n    { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;summary&quot;, &quot;type&quot;: &quot;markdown&quot; }\n  ]\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Multiple Output Variables</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">output:\n  text: ${output.content}\n  confidence: ${output.score as number}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Produces:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;output&quot;: [\n    { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;text&quot;, &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot; },\n    { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;confidence&quot;, &quot;type&quot;: &quot;number&quot; }\n  ]\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Grouped Output (repeat_count)</h3>\n<p>When a component job uses <code>repeat_count &gt; 1</code>, the output variables are wrapped in a group:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: generate\n    component: gpt4o\n    repeat_count: 3\n    input:\n      prompt: ${input.prompt}\n    output: ${output as text}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Produces:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;output&quot;: [\n    {\n      &quot;name&quot;: null,\n      &quot;variables&quot;: [\n        { &quot;name&quot;: null, &quot;type&quot;: &quot;text&quot; }\n      ],\n      &quot;repeat_count&quot;: 3\n    }\n  ]\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>This tells the client that the output will contain 3 iterations of the variable group.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>6.5 Schema in Practice</h2>\n<h3>Web UI Form Generation</h3>\n<p>When <code>webui</code> is enabled, model-compose uses the input schema to automatically generate form controls:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Variable Type</th>\n<th>UI Control</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>string</code></td>\n<td>Text input</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>text</code></td>\n<td>Textarea</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>integer</code> / <code>number</code></td>\n<td>Number input (with slider if annotated)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>boolean</code></td>\n<td>Checkbox</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>image</code></td>\n<td>File upload (image)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>audio</code></td>\n<td>File upload (audio)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>file</code></td>\n<td>File upload</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>select</code></td>\n<td>Dropdown</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>MCP Server Tool Mapping</h3>\n<p>When the controller type is <code>mcp-server</code>, workflow input variables become tool parameters:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: mcp-server\n\nworkflows:\n  - id: translate\n    jobs:\n      - id: task\n        component: translator\n        input:\n          text: ${input.text as text}\n          target_lang: ${input.target_lang as select/en,ko,ja,zh}\n</code></pre>\n<p>This registers an MCP tool <code>translate</code> with parameters:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>text</code> (string, required)</li>\n<li><code>target_lang</code> (enum: en, ko, ja, zh)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Client SDK Integration</h3>\n<p>Use the schema endpoint to dynamically build request payloads:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-python\">import requests\n\n# Get schema\nschema = requests.get(&quot;http://localhost:8080/workflows/my-workflow/schema&quot;).json()\n\n# Build input from schema\npayload = {}\nfor var in schema[&quot;input&quot;]:\n    if var.get(&quot;default&quot;) is not None:\n        payload[var[&quot;name&quot;]] = var[&quot;default&quot;]\n    else:\n        payload[var[&quot;name&quot;]] = get_user_input(var[&quot;name&quot;], var[&quot;type&quot;])\n\n# Execute workflow\nresult = requests.post(\n    &quot;http://localhost:8080/workflows/runs&quot;,\n    json={&quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;my-workflow&quot;, &quot;input&quot;: payload}\n).json()\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>6.6 Practical Examples</h2>\n<h3>Example 1: Text Chat Workflow</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">components:\n  - id: gpt4o\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      endpoint: https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n      body:\n        model: gpt-4o\n        messages:\n          - role: system\n            content: ${input.system_prompt}\n          - role: user\n            content: ${input.user_prompt}\n      output: ${response.choices[0].message.content}\n\nworkflows:\n  - id: chat\n    title: Chat with GPT-4o\n    jobs:\n      - id: generate\n        component: gpt4o\n        input:\n          system_prompt: ${input.system_prompt as text | You are a helpful assistant.}\n          user_prompt: ${input.user_prompt as text}\n        output: ${output as markdown}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Generated Schema:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;chat&quot;,\n  &quot;title&quot;: &quot;Chat with GPT-4o&quot;,\n  &quot;input&quot;: [\n    { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;system_prompt&quot;, &quot;type&quot;: &quot;text&quot;, &quot;default&quot;: &quot;You are a helpful assistant.&quot; },\n    { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;user_prompt&quot;, &quot;type&quot;: &quot;text&quot; }\n  ],\n  &quot;output&quot;: [\n    { &quot;name&quot;: null, &quot;type&quot;: &quot;markdown&quot; }\n  ]\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Example 2: Image Analysis Workflow</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: analyze-image\n    title: Analyze Image\n    jobs:\n      - id: analyze\n        component: vision-model\n        input:\n          image: ${input.image as image;base64}\n          question: ${input.question as text | Describe this image.}\n        output:\n          description: ${output as markdown}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Generated Schema:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;analyze-image&quot;,\n  &quot;title&quot;: &quot;Analyze Image&quot;,\n  &quot;input&quot;: [\n    { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;image&quot;, &quot;type&quot;: &quot;image&quot;, &quot;format&quot;: &quot;base64&quot; },\n    { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;question&quot;, &quot;type&quot;: &quot;text&quot;, &quot;default&quot;: &quot;Describe this image.&quot; }\n  ],\n  &quot;output&quot;: [\n    { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;description&quot;, &quot;type&quot;: &quot;markdown&quot; }\n  ]\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Example 3: Streaming Workflow</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: stream-chat\n    title: Streaming Chat\n    jobs:\n      - id: generate\n        component: gpt4o-stream\n        input:\n          prompt: ${input.prompt as text}\n        output: ${output as sse-text}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Generated Schema:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;stream-chat&quot;,\n  &quot;title&quot;: &quot;Streaming Chat&quot;,\n  &quot;input&quot;: [\n    { &quot;name&quot;: &quot;prompt&quot;, &quot;type&quot;: &quot;text&quot; }\n  ],\n  &quot;output&quot;: [\n    { &quot;name&quot;: null, &quot;type&quot;: &quot;sse-text&quot; }\n  ]\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>The <code>sse-text</code> output type indicates the client should expect a streaming response via Server-Sent Events.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>6.7 Workflow Metadata Fields</h2>\n<p>Beyond input/output variables, the schema includes workflow-level metadata:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>workflow_id</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>Unique identifier</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>title</code></td>\n<td>string?</td>\n<td>Human-readable title (displayed in Web UI)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>description</code></td>\n<td>string?</td>\n<td>Detailed description of the workflow</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>default</code></td>\n<td>boolean</td>\n<td>Whether this is the default workflow</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Private Workflows</h3>\n<p>Workflows marked with <code>private: true</code> are excluded from the schema API:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: internal-helper\n    private: true\n    jobs:\n      - id: task\n        component: helper\n</code></pre>\n<p>Private workflows cannot be accessed via <code>GET /workflows</code> or <code>GET /workflows/{id}/schema</code>.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>6.8 Best Practices</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Always specify types</strong> — Use <code>${input.field as type}</code> instead of bare <code>${input.field}</code> to generate accurate schemas.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Provide defaults</strong> — Use <code>${input.field as type | default}</code> for optional parameters so clients know what values to use.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Use descriptive titles</strong> — Set <code>title</code> on workflows so the Web UI and MCP tools have meaningful names.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Keep schemas stable</strong> — Changing input variable names or types is a breaking change for clients. Add new variables with defaults instead.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><strong>Use private for internal workflows</strong> — Mark helper/sub-workflows as <code>private: true</code> to keep the public schema clean.</p>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Next Chapter</strong>: <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/07-controller-configuration\">Chapter 7: Controller Configuration</a> — Learn how to configure HTTP servers, MCP servers, and other controller types.</p>\n</blockquote>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Chapter 6: Workflow Schema"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "user-guide/07-controller-configuration",
      "html": "<h1>Chapter 7: Controller Configuration</h1>\n<p>This chapter covers how to configure model-compose controllers, including HTTP server and MCP server settings, concurrency control, and port management.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>7.1 HTTP Server</h2>\n<p>The HTTP server controller exposes workflows as REST APIs.</p>\n<h3>Basic Structure</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /api\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Example: Simple Chatbot API</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /api\n\nworkflow:\n  title: Chat with AI\n  description: Generate text responses using AI\n  input: ${input}\n  output: ${output}\n\ncomponent:\n  type: http-client\n  base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n  path: /chat/completions\n  method: POST\n  headers:\n    Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n    Content-Type: application/json\n  body:\n    model: gpt-4o\n    messages:\n      - role: user\n        content: ${input.prompt}\n  output:\n    message: ${response.choices[0].message.content}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>API Endpoints</h3>\n<p>The HTTP server controller automatically generates the following endpoints:</p>\n<h4>List Workflows</h4>\n<pre><code>GET /api/workflows\nGET /api/workflows?include_schema=true\n</code></pre>\n<p>Retrieves the list of workflows. Adding the <code>include_schema=true</code> parameter also returns input/output schemas for each workflow.</p>\n<p>Request example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl http://localhost:8080/api/workflows\n</code></pre>\n<p>Response example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">[\n  {\n    &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;chat&quot;,\n    &quot;title&quot;: &quot;Chat with AI&quot;,\n    &quot;default&quot;: true\n  }\n]\n</code></pre>\n<p>With schema request:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl http://localhost:8080/api/workflows?include_schema=true\n</code></pre>\n<p>Response example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">[\n  {\n    &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;chat&quot;,\n    &quot;title&quot;: &quot;Chat with AI&quot;,\n    &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Generate text responses using AI&quot;,\n    &quot;input&quot;: [\n      {\n        &quot;name&quot;: &quot;prompt&quot;,\n        &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot;\n      }\n    ],\n    &quot;output&quot;: [\n      {\n        &quot;name&quot;: &quot;message&quot;,\n        &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot;\n      }\n    ],\n    &quot;default&quot;: true\n  }\n]\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Get Workflow Schema</h4>\n<pre><code>GET /api/workflows/{workflow_id}/schema\n</code></pre>\n<p>Retrieves the input/output schema for a specific workflow.</p>\n<p>Request example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl http://localhost:8080/api/workflows/chat/schema\n</code></pre>\n<p>Response example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;chat&quot;,\n  &quot;title&quot;: &quot;Chat with AI&quot;,\n  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Generate text responses using AI&quot;,\n  &quot;input&quot;: [\n    {\n      &quot;name&quot;: &quot;prompt&quot;,\n      &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot;\n    }\n  ],\n  &quot;output&quot;: [\n    {\n      &quot;name&quot;: &quot;message&quot;,\n      &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot;\n    }\n  ],\n  &quot;default&quot;: true\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Execute Workflow</h4>\n<pre><code>POST /api/workflows/runs\n</code></pre>\n<p>Executes a workflow. You can control sync/async execution with the <code>wait_for_completion</code> parameter.</p>\n<p>Request body parameters:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>workflow_id</code> (string, optional): Workflow ID to execute. If omitted, executes the default workflow</li>\n<li><code>input</code> (object, optional): Workflow input data</li>\n<li><code>wait_for_completion</code> (boolean, default: true): If true, waits until completion; if false, returns task_id immediately</li>\n<li><code>output_only</code> (boolean, default: false): If true, returns only output data (requires wait_for_completion=true)</li>\n</ul>\n<h5>Synchronous Execution (Default)</h5>\n<p>Waits until completion and returns the result.</p>\n<p>Request example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/workflows/runs \\\n  -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; \\\n  -d '{\n    &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;chat&quot;,\n    &quot;input&quot;: {\n      &quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Hello, AI!&quot;\n    },\n    &quot;wait_for_completion&quot;: true\n  }'\n</code></pre>\n<p>Response example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01JBQR5KSXM8HNXF7N9VYW3K2T&quot;,\n  &quot;status&quot;: &quot;completed&quot;,\n  &quot;output&quot;: {\n    &quot;message&quot;: &quot;Hello! How can I help you today?&quot;\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h5>output_only Mode</h5>\n<p>Setting <code>output_only: true</code> returns only the output data without task metadata.</p>\n<p>Request example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/workflows/runs \\\n  -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; \\\n  -d '{\n    &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;chat&quot;,\n    &quot;input&quot;: {\n      &quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Hello, AI!&quot;\n    },\n    &quot;wait_for_completion&quot;: true,\n    &quot;output_only&quot;: true\n  }'\n</code></pre>\n<p>Response example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;message&quot;: &quot;Hello! How can I help you today?&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h5>Asynchronous Execution</h5>\n<p>Setting <code>wait_for_completion: false</code> immediately returns task_id and executes in the background.</p>\n<p>Request example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/workflows/runs \\\n  -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; \\\n  -d '{\n    &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;chat&quot;,\n    &quot;input&quot;: {\n      &quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Hello, AI!&quot;\n    },\n    &quot;wait_for_completion&quot;: false\n  }'\n</code></pre>\n<p>Response example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01JBQR5KSXM8HNXF7N9VYW3K2T&quot;,\n  &quot;status&quot;: &quot;pending&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Get Task Status</h4>\n<pre><code>GET /api/tasks/{task_id}\nGET /api/tasks/{task_id}?output_only=true\n</code></pre>\n<p>Retrieves the status and result of an asynchronously executed workflow.</p>\n<p>Task states:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>pending</code>: Waiting (not yet started)</li>\n<li><code>processing</code>: Currently executing</li>\n<li><code>interrupted</code>: Waiting for user input (see <a href=\"#resume-task\">Resume Task</a>)</li>\n<li><code>completed</code>: Successfully completed</li>\n<li><code>failed</code>: Failed during execution</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Request example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl http://localhost:8080/api/tasks/01JBQR5KSXM8HNXF7N9VYW3K2T\n</code></pre>\n<p>Response when processing:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01JBQR5KSXM8HNXF7N9VYW3K2T&quot;,\n  &quot;status&quot;: &quot;processing&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Response when completed:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01JBQR5KSXM8HNXF7N9VYW3K2T&quot;,\n  &quot;status&quot;: &quot;completed&quot;,\n  &quot;output&quot;: {\n    &quot;message&quot;: &quot;Hello! How can I help you today?&quot;\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Response when interrupted:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01JBQR5KSXM8HNXF7N9VYW3K2T&quot;,\n  &quot;status&quot;: &quot;interrupted&quot;,\n  &quot;interrupt&quot;: {\n    &quot;job_id&quot;: &quot;review-step&quot;,\n    &quot;phase&quot;: &quot;before&quot;,\n    &quot;message&quot;: &quot;Please review the generated content before proceeding.&quot;,\n    &quot;metadata&quot;: { &quot;draft&quot;: &quot;...&quot; }\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Response when failed:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01JBQR5KSXM8HNXF7N9VYW3K2T&quot;,\n  &quot;status&quot;: &quot;failed&quot;,\n  &quot;error&quot;: &quot;Connection timeout&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>output_only mode:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl http://localhost:8080/api/tasks/01JBQR5KSXM8HNXF7N9VYW3K2T?output_only=true\n</code></pre>\n<p>Returns HTTP 202 if not completed:</p>\n<pre><code>HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted\n{&quot;detail&quot;: &quot;Task is still in progress.&quot;}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Returns output only when completed:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;message&quot;: &quot;Hello! How can I help you today?&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Returns HTTP 500 if failed:</p>\n<pre><code>HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error\n{&quot;detail&quot;: &quot;Connection timeout&quot;}\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Resume Task</h4>\n<pre><code>POST /api/tasks/{task_id}/resume\n</code></pre>\n<p>Resumes an interrupted workflow. When a task is in <code>interrupted</code> status, send this request to provide an answer and continue execution.</p>\n<p>Request body parameters:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>job_id</code> (string, required): The job ID from the interrupt response</li>\n<li><code>answer</code> (any, optional): Answer data to pass to the workflow (JSON or string)</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Request example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/tasks/01JBQR5KSXM8HNXF7N9VYW3K2T/resume \\\n  -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; \\\n  -d '{\n    &quot;job_id&quot;: &quot;review-step&quot;,\n    &quot;answer&quot;: &quot;approved&quot;\n  }'\n</code></pre>\n<p>Response example (completed):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01JBQR5KSXM8HNXF7N9VYW3K2T&quot;,\n  &quot;status&quot;: &quot;processing&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>After resuming, poll <code>GET /api/tasks/{task_id}</code> to check for completion, another interrupt, or failure.</p>\n<h4>Health Check</h4>\n<pre><code>GET /api/health\n</code></pre>\n<p>Checks server status.</p>\n<p>Response example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;status&quot;: &quot;ok&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Asynchronous Execution and Task Queue</h3>\n<h4>Task Creation and Tracking</h4>\n<p>When a workflow is executed, a Task is created internally:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Task Creation</strong>: A unique <code>task_id</code> based on ULID is generated when executing a workflow</li>\n<li><strong>Task State Tracking</strong>: Tasks have 5 states (<code>pending</code>, <code>processing</code>, <code>interrupted</code>, <code>completed</code>, <code>failed</code>)</li>\n<li><strong>Task Caching</strong>: Completed tasks are cached in memory for 1 hour and can be queried via the <code>/api/tasks/{task_id}</code> endpoint</li>\n</ol>\n<h4>Synchronous vs Asynchronous Execution</h4>\n<p><strong>Synchronous Execution</strong> (<code>wait_for_completion: true</code>, default):</p>\n<ul>\n<li>The HTTP request waits until the workflow completes</li>\n<li>Returns the result immediately upon completion</li>\n<li>Use for simple workflows or when immediate results are needed</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Asynchronous Execution</strong> (<code>wait_for_completion: false</code>):</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Immediately returns <code>task_id</code> and closes the connection</li>\n<li>The workflow executes in the background</li>\n<li>Query status and results via the <code>/api/tasks/{task_id}</code> endpoint</li>\n<li>Suitable for workflows with long execution times</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>CORS Configuration</h3>\n<p>Control HTTP server CORS with the <code>origins</code> field.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  origins: &quot;https://example.com,https://app.example.com&quot;  # Allow specific domains only\n  # origins: &quot;*&quot;  # Allow all domains (default, for development)\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>7.2 MCP Server</h2>\n<p>The MCP (Model Context Protocol) server controller integrates with Claude Desktop and other MCP clients using the Streamable HTTP protocol.</p>\n<h3>Basic Structure</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: mcp-server\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /mcp  # Streamable HTTP endpoint path\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Example: Content Moderation Tool</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: mcp-server\n  base_path: /mcp\n  port: 8080\n\nworkflows:\n  - id: moderate-text\n    title: Moderate Text Content\n    description: Check if text content violates content policies\n    action: text-moderation\n    input:\n      text: ${input.text}\n    output: ${output}\n\n  - id: moderate-image\n    title: Moderate Image Content\n    description: Check if image content is safe and appropriate\n    action: image-moderation\n    input:\n      image_url: ${input.image_url}\n    output: ${output}\n\ncomponents:\n  - id: openai-moderation\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n    headers:\n      Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n      Content-Type: application/json\n    actions:\n      - id: text-moderation\n        path: /moderations\n        method: POST\n        body:\n          input: ${input.text}\n        output:\n          flagged: ${response.results[0].flagged}\n          categories: ${response.results[0].categories}\n          scores: ${response.results[0].category_scores}\n\n      - id: image-moderation\n        path: /moderations\n        method: POST\n        body:\n          input: ${input.image_url}\n          model: omni-moderation-latest\n        output:\n          flagged: ${response.results[0].flagged}\n          categories: ${response.results[0].categories}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>MCP Workflow Features</h3>\n<p>MCP server workflows have the following characteristics:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>title</strong>: Tool name displayed in MCP client</li>\n<li><strong>description</strong>: Tool description (shown in MCP client)</li>\n<li><strong>action</strong>: Component action ID to connect to</li>\n<li><strong>input</strong>: Tool input parameter definition</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>MCP Client Integration</h3>\n<p>model-compose's MCP server uses the <strong>Streamable HTTP</strong> protocol (MCP spec 2025-03-26).</p>\n<p><strong>Streamable HTTP Features</strong>:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Single Endpoint</strong>: Handles all MCP communication through one HTTP endpoint</li>\n<li><strong>Bidirectional Communication</strong>: Server can send notifications and requests to client</li>\n<li><strong>SSE Support</strong>: Optionally uses Server-Sent Events for streaming responses</li>\n<li><strong>Session Management</strong>: Session tracking via <code>Mcp-Session-Id</code> header</li>\n</ul>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note</strong>: Streamable HTTP replaces the previous HTTP+SSE approach (2024-11-05 spec). It provides a single endpoint and enhanced bidirectional communication.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h4>Starting the Server</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">model-compose up -f model-compose.yml\n</code></pre>\n<p>Once the server starts, you can access the MCP server at:</p>\n<pre><code>http://localhost:8080/mcp\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Client Connection</h4>\n<p>MCP clients supporting Streamable HTTP can connect to the above URL.</p>\n<p><strong>Connection Information</strong>:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>URL: <code>http://localhost:8080/mcp</code> (or your configured host:port and base_path)</li>\n<li>Transport: Streamable HTTP</li>\n<li>Protocol Version: 2025-03-26</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Production Environment</strong>:</p>\n<p>For production, it's recommended to use HTTPS when exposing the MCP server externally. You can apply SSL/TLS through a reverse proxy like Nginx or Caddy.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># model-compose runs locally with HTTP\ncontroller:\n  type: mcp-server\n  host: 127.0.0.1\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /mcp\n</code></pre>\n<p>Nginx reverse proxy configuration example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-nginx\">server {\n    listen 443 ssl;\n    server_name mcp.example.com;\n\n    ssl_certificate /path/to/cert.pem;\n    ssl_certificate_key /path/to/key.pem;\n\n    location /mcp {\n        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp;\n        proxy_set_header Host $host;\n        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;\n        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;\n        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;\n\n        # SSE streaming support\n        proxy_buffering off;\n        proxy_cache off;\n        proxy_set_header Connection '';\n        proxy_http_version 1.1;\n        chunked_transfer_encoding off;\n    }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>MCP clients connect to:</p>\n<pre><code>https://mcp.example.com/mcp\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>7.3 Queue Subscriber</h2>\n<p>The queue subscriber controller consumes tasks from a message queue (e.g., Redis) and executes workflows.
