This enables distributed worker patterns where multiple model-compose instances process tasks from a shared queue.</p>\n<h3>Basic Structure</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: queue-subscriber\n  driver: redis\n  url: redis://localhost:6379\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Example: Distributed Image Processing Worker</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: queue-subscriber\n  driver: redis\n  url: redis://localhost:6379\n  workflow: image-processing\n  max_concurrent_count: 2\n\nworkflow:\n  title: Image Processing\n  input: ${input}\n  output: ${output}\n\ncomponent:\n  type: http-client\n  base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n  path: /images/generations\n  method: POST\n  headers:\n    Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n    Content-Type: application/json\n  body:\n    model: dall-e-3\n    prompt: ${input.prompt}\n  output:\n    image_url: ${response.data[0].url}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>How It Works</h3>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Producer</strong> pushes a task message to a Redis list using <code>LPUSH</code></li>\n<li><strong>Worker</strong> (queue-subscriber) pops the task using <code>BRPOP</code></li>\n<li><strong>Worker</strong> executes the corresponding workflow</li>\n<li><strong>Worker</strong> stores the result in Redis (<code>SET</code>) and broadcasts via pub/sub (<code>PUBLISH</code>)</li>\n<li><strong>Producer</strong> retrieves the result using <code>GET</code> or <code>SUBSCRIBE</code></li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Task Message Format</h3>\n<p>Producers push JSON messages to the queue:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;user-task-123&quot;,\n  &quot;run_id&quot;: &quot;01JXYZ...&quot;,\n  &quot;input&quot;: { &quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;A sunset over mountains&quot; }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li><code>task_id</code>: Logical task identifier (remains the same across retries)</li>\n<li><code>run_id</code>: Unique execution instance identifier</li>\n<li><code>input</code>: Workflow input data</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Result Format</h3>\n<p>After workflow execution, the worker stores and publishes the result:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;user-task-123&quot;,\n  &quot;run_id&quot;: &quot;01JXYZ...&quot;,\n  &quot;status&quot;: &quot;completed&quot;,\n  &quot;output&quot;: { &quot;image_url&quot;: &quot;https://...&quot; },\n  &quot;worker_id&quot;: &quot;01JXY...&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Result status values: <code>completed</code>, <code>failed</code>, <code>interrupted</code></p>\n<h3>Queue and Key Naming</h3>\n<p>Each workflow gets its own queue using the pattern <code>{name}:{workflow_id}</code>:</p>\n<pre><code>model-compose:tasks:image-processing              ← task queue (Redis List)\nmodel-compose:tasks:image-processing:01JXYZ...    ← result storage (Redis String, with TTL)\nmodel-compose:tasks:image-processing:01JXYZ...    ← result notification (Redis Pub/Sub channel)\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Configuration Options</h3>\n<h4>Common Settings</h4>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>driver</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Queue backend driver (<code>redis</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>name</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>model-compose:tasks</code></td>\n<td>Base name for task queues. Queue key: <code>{name}:{workflow_id}</code>. Result key: <code>{name}:{workflow_id}:{run_id}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>result_ttl</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>3600</code></td>\n<td>TTL in seconds for result entries. <code>0</code> = no expiry</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_concurrent</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>1</code></td>\n<td>Maximum concurrent task processing</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>worker_id</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>auto</td>\n<td>Unique worker identifier (auto-generated ULID)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>workflows</code></td>\n<td>list</td>\n<td><code>[&quot;__default__&quot;]</code></td>\n<td>Workflow IDs to handle</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h4>Redis Driver Settings</h4>\n<p>Connection can be configured using either <code>url</code> or <code>host</code>/<code>port</code>/<code>secure</code>. Both cannot be used together.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>url</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Redis connection URL (e.g., <code>redis://localhost:6379</code>, <code>rediss://...</code> for TLS)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>host</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>localhost</code></td>\n<td>Redis server hostname or IP address</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>port</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>6379</code></td>\n<td>Redis server port number</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>secure</code></td>\n<td>boolean</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Use TLS/SSL for connections</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>database</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>0</code></td>\n<td>Redis database number (0-15)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>password</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>null</code></td>\n<td>Redis password</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>pop_timeout</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>1</code></td>\n<td>BRPOP timeout in seconds</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Distributed Worker Scenarios</h3>\n<h4>Scenario 1: Single Workflow Worker</h4>\n<p>The simplest setup — one worker type processes one workflow:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: queue-subscriber\n  driver: redis\n  url: redis://localhost:6379\n  workflow: text-summary\n  max_concurrent_count: 3\n</code></pre>\n<p>Push tasks:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">redis-cli LPUSH model-compose:tasks:text-summary \\\n  '{&quot;task_id&quot;:&quot;t1&quot;,&quot;run_id&quot;:&quot;r1&quot;,&quot;input&quot;:{&quot;text&quot;:&quot;...&quot;}}'\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Scenario 2: Multi-Workflow Worker</h4>\n<p>A single worker handles multiple workflows:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: queue-subscriber\n  driver: redis\n  url: redis://localhost:6379\n  workflows:\n    - text-summary\n    - translation\n  max_concurrent_count: 5\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Scenario 3: Specialized Workers</h4>\n<p>Deploy different workers for different workloads:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># GPU server — image generation only\ncontroller:\n  type: queue-subscriber\n  driver: redis\n  url: redis://shared-redis:6379\n  workflow: image-generation\n  max_concurrent_count: 2\n\n# CPU server — text processing\ncontroller:\n  type: queue-subscriber\n  driver: redis\n  url: redis://shared-redis:6379\n  workflows:\n    - text-summary\n    - translation\n  max_concurrent_count: 10\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Consuming Results</h3>\n<h4>Using Pub/Sub (Real-time)</h4>\n<p>Subscribe to the result channel before pushing the task:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Terminal 1: Subscribe\nredis-cli SUBSCRIBE model-compose:tasks:my-workflow:run-001\n\n# Terminal 2: Push task\nredis-cli LPUSH model-compose:tasks:my-workflow \\\n  '{&quot;task_id&quot;:&quot;t1&quot;,&quot;run_id&quot;:&quot;run-001&quot;,&quot;input&quot;:{}}'\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Using GET (Polling)</h4>\n<p>Poll the result key after pushing:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">redis-cli GET model-compose:tasks:my-workflow:run-001\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Production Configuration</h3>\n<p>Using host/port:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: queue-subscriber\n  driver: redis\n  host: redis.internal\n  port: 6379\n  password: ${env.REDIS_PASSWORD}\n  database: 2\n  name: myapp:tasks\n  result_ttl: 7200\n  worker_id: gpu-worker-01\n  workflows:\n    - image-generation\n  max_concurrent_count: 2\n</code></pre>\n<p>Using URL (with TLS):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: queue-subscriber\n  driver: redis\n  url: rediss://:${env.REDIS_PASSWORD}@redis.internal:6380/2\n  workflows:\n    - image-generation\n  max_concurrent_count: 2\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note</strong>: The <code>redis</code> Python package (<code>redis&gt;=5.0.0</code>) must be installed. It is included as a dependency of model-compose.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<hr />\n<h2>7.4 Queue Dispatch (Distributed Deployment)</h2>\n<p>Queue dispatch enables a distributed deployment pattern where an HTTP/MCP entry point server delegates workflow execution to remote workers via a message queue, instead of running workflows locally.</p>\n<h3>Architecture</h3>\n<pre><code>Client → [HTTP Server] → Redis LPUSH → [Worker A or B] → Redis PUBLISH → [HTTP Server] → Client\n         (entry point)                   (queue-subscriber)                 (result)\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Basic Configuration</h3>\n<p><strong>Entry point server</strong> (receives requests, dispatches to queue):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  adapter:\n    type: http-server\n    port: 8080\n  queue:\n    driver: redis\n    url: redis://localhost:6379\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Worker server</strong> (consumes from queue, executes workflows):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  adapter:\n    type: queue-subscriber\n    driver: redis\n    url: redis://localhost:6379\n</code></pre>\n<h3>How It Works</h3>\n<ol>\n<li>Client sends an HTTP request to the entry point server</li>\n<li><code>ControllerService.run_workflow()</code> pushes a task to Redis queue via <code>LPUSH</code></li>\n<li>Entry point subscribes to the result channel via <code>SUBSCRIBE</code></li>\n<li>A queue-subscriber worker pops the task via <code>BRPOP</code> and executes the workflow</li>\n<li>Worker stores the result (<code>SET</code>) and publishes it (<code>PUBLISH</code>)</li>\n<li>Entry point receives the result and returns it to the client</li>\n</ol>\n<p>The queue dispatch is <strong>transparent</strong> to adapters — HTTP and MCP server adapters require no changes.</p>\n<h3>Configuration Options</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>driver</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><strong>required</strong></td>\n<td>Queue backend driver (<code>redis</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>name</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>model-compose:tasks</code></td>\n<td>Base name for task queues. Queue key: <code>{name}:{workflow_id}</code>. Result key: <code>{name}:{workflow_id}:{run_id}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>timeout</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>0</code></td>\n<td>Maximum time in seconds to wait for a result. <code>0</code> = no limit</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>Redis driver settings (<code>url</code> or <code>host</code>/<code>port</code>/<code>secure</code>) are the same as <a href=\"#73-queue-subscriber\">Queue Subscriber</a>.</p>\n<h3>Example: Distributed Deployment</h3>\n<p>Three servers: 1 entry point + 2 workers sharing a Redis instance.</p>\n<p><strong>Entry point</strong> (<code>server-a/model-compose.yml</code>):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  adapter:\n    type: http-server\n    port: 8080\n  queue:\n    driver: redis\n    url: redis://redis.internal:6379\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Worker 1</strong> (<code>server-b/model-compose.yml</code>):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  adapter:\n    type: queue-subscriber\n    driver: redis\n    url: redis://redis.internal:6379\n    workflow: image-generation\n    max_concurrent_count: 2\n\nworkflow:\n  id: image-generation\n  # ... workflow definition\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Worker 2</strong> (<code>server-c/model-compose.yml</code>):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  adapter:\n    type: queue-subscriber\n    driver: redis\n    url: redis://redis.internal:6379\n    workflow: image-generation\n    max_concurrent_count: 2\n\nworkflow:\n  id: image-generation\n  # ... workflow definition\n</code></pre>\n<p>Workers compete for tasks from the same queue — whichever pops first processes it.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>7.5 Queue Streaming</h2>\n<p>When a workflow produces streaming output (e.g., LLM token-by-token generation), the queue dispatch system automatically delivers chunks in real time from the worker to the dispatcher using Redis Streams. The client receives SSE events as if the workflow were running locally.</p>\n<h3>How It Works</h3>\n<pre><code>Client ← SSE ← [Dispatcher] ← XREAD ← Redis Stream ← XADD ← [Worker] ← LLM streaming\n</code></pre>\n<ol>\n<li>Worker executes a workflow that returns streaming output (AsyncIterator)</li>\n<li>Worker publishes a <code>status: &quot;streaming&quot;</code> message via Pub/Sub with a <code>stream_key</code></li>\n<li>Worker writes each chunk to a Redis Stream using <code>XADD</code></li>\n<li>Dispatcher receives the metadata, creates a <code>RedisStreamIterator</code>, and returns it as the workflow output</li>\n<li>HTTP server adapter detects the AsyncIterator and renders it as an SSE response</li>\n<li>Worker writes a <code>done</code> (or <code>error</code>) sentinel event to signal completion</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>No Configuration Required</h3>\n<p>Queue streaming works automatically — no additional configuration is needed. If the worker's workflow produces streaming output, chunks are delivered via Redis Streams. If the output is not streaming, the existing JSON result path is used.</p>\n<p>The same <code>name</code> field generates the stream key by appending <code>:stream</code>:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Key</th>\n<th>Pattern</th>\n<th>Redis Type</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Queue</td>\n<td><code>{name}:{workflow_id}</code></td>\n<td>LIST</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Result</td>\n<td><code>{name}:{workflow_id}:{run_id}</code></td>\n<td>STRING</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Result channel</td>\n<td><code>{name}:{workflow_id}:{run_id}</code></td>\n<td>Pub/Sub</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Stream</strong></td>\n<td><code>{name}:{workflow_id}:{run_id}:stream</code></td>\n<td><strong>STREAM</strong></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Example: Streaming Chat via Queue</h3>\n<p><strong>Dispatcher</strong> (<code>dispatcher/model-compose.yml</code>):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  adapter:\n    type: http-server\n    port: 8080\n    base_path: /api\n  queue:\n    driver: redis\n    host: localhost\n    port: 6379\n    name: my-queue\n  webui:\n    driver: gradio\n    port: 8081\n\nworkflow:\n  title: Chat with OpenAI GPT-4o (Streaming via Queue)\n  job:\n    type: component\n\ncomponent:\n  type: workflow\n  action:\n    workflow: chat\n    input:\n      prompt: ${input.prompt as text}\n    output: ${output as sse-text}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Worker</strong> (<code>subscriber/model-compose.yml</code>):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  adapter:\n    type: queue-subscriber\n    driver: redis\n    host: localhost\n    port: 6379\n    name: my-queue\n    workflows:\n      - chat\n\nworkflow:\n  id: chat\n  title: Chat with OpenAI GPT-4o (Streaming)\n  job:\n    component: openai\n    input:\n      prompt: ${input.prompt}\n    output: ${output as sse-text}\n\ncomponent:\n  id: openai\n  type: http-client\n  base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n  action:\n    path: /chat/completions\n    method: POST\n    headers:\n      Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n      Content-Type: application/json\n    body:\n      model: gpt-4o\n      messages:\n        - role: user\n          content: ${input.prompt as text}\n      stream: true\n    stream_format: json\n    output: ${response[].choices[0].delta.content}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Client request:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl -N -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/workflows/runs \\\n  -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; \\\n  -d '{\n    &quot;input&quot;: { &quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Write a short poem about the sea.&quot; },\n    &quot;output_only&quot;: true,\n    &quot;wait_for_completion&quot;: true\n  }'\n</code></pre>\n<p>The response streams as SSE:</p>\n<pre><code>data: The\ndata:  waves\ndata:  crash\ndata:  upon\ndata:  the\ndata:  shore\n...\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Stream Message Format</h3>\n<p>Each entry in the Redis Stream has an <code>event</code> field:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Event</th>\n<th>Fields</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>chunk</code></td>\n<td><code>event</code>, <code>data</code></td>\n<td>A streaming chunk (JSON or text)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>done</code></td>\n<td><code>event</code></td>\n<td>Stream completed successfully</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>error</code></td>\n<td><code>event</code>, <code>data</code></td>\n<td>Error occurred, <code>data</code> contains the error message</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Edge Cases</h3>\n<p><strong>Worker crash</strong>: If the worker terminates mid-stream without writing a sentinel event, the dispatcher's <code>RedisStreamIterator</code> times out based on the queue <code>timeout</code> setting. The stream key is cleaned up by Redis TTL (<code>result_ttl</code>).</p>\n<p><strong>Client disconnect</strong>: When the client closes the SSE connection, the HTTP server stops iterating the <code>RedisStreamIterator</code>. The worker continues writing to the Redis Stream (fire-and-forget) and the stream expires via TTL.</p>\n<p><strong>Non-streaming output</strong>: If the workflow returns a plain result (not an AsyncIterator), the existing JSON result path (<code>SETEX</code> + <code>PUBLISH</code>) is used. No streaming keys are created.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>7.6 Concurrency Control</h2>\n<p>The <code>max_concurrent_count</code> setting is available for both HTTP and MCP servers, limiting the number of workflows that can execute concurrently at the controller level.</p>\n<h3>Basic Configuration</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server  # or mcp-server\n  max_concurrent_count: 5  # Limit to maximum 5 concurrent executions\n</code></pre>\n<h3>How It Works</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><code>max_concurrent_count: 0</code> (default): Unlimited concurrent execution, task queue disabled</li>\n<li><code>max_concurrent_count: 1</code>: Execute one workflow at a time (sequential execution)</li>\n<li><code>max_concurrent_count: N</code> (N &gt; 1): Execute up to N workflows concurrently, queue when exceeded</li>\n</ul>\n<p>When task queue is activated (<code>max_concurrent_count &gt; 0</code>):</p>\n<ol>\n<li>New workflow execution requests are added to the queue</li>\n<li>Up to <code>max_concurrent_count</code> workers fetch tasks from the queue and execute them</li>\n<li>Even with <code>wait_for_completion: true</code>, tasks wait in the queue before execution</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>Use Cases</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># Default: Unlimited\ncontroller:\n  type: http-server\n  max_concurrent_count: 0\n\n# When GPU resources need to be limited\ncontroller:\n  type: http-server\n  max_concurrent_count: 3  # Limit total workflow execution to 3\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Controller vs Component Level Control</h3>\n<p>Concurrency control is possible at two levels:</p>\n<p><strong>Controller Level</strong> (<code>controller.max_concurrent_count</code>):</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Limits total workflow execution count</li>\n<li>Applied commonly to all workflows</li>\n<li>Use when protecting overall system resources (CPU, memory)</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Component Level</strong> (<code>component.max_concurrent_count</code>):</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Limits concurrent calls to a specific component</li>\n<li>Can be set independently for each component</li>\n<li>Use when protecting specific resources like GPU, external API rate limits</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  max_concurrent_count: 0  # Unlimited workflow execution\n\ncomponents:\n  - id: image-model\n    type: model\n    max_concurrent_count: 2  # Limit to 2 concurrent executions due to GPU memory\n    model: stabilityai/stable-diffusion-2-1\n    task: text-to-image\n\n  - id: openai-api\n    type: http-client\n    max_concurrent_count: 10  # Limit to 10 considering API rate limit\n    base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Recommendations</strong>:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Generally, component-level control provides finer resource management</li>\n<li>Use controller-level control only when preventing overall system overload</li>\n<li>If both levels are set, both limits apply</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>7.7 Port and Host Configuration</h2>\n<h3>Host</h3>\n<p>Specifies the network interface the controller binds to.</p>\n<h4>Allow Access from Localhost Only (Default)</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  host: 127.0.0.1  # Default\n  port: 8080       # Default\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li>Accessible only from the same machine</li>\n<li>Use when running behind a reverse proxy or when security is critical</li>\n</ul>\n<h4>Allow Access from All Interfaces</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8080\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li>Accessible from external sources</li>\n<li>Use for development environment or when exposing to network</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Port</h3>\n<p>Specifies the port the controller API server uses.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080  # Default\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Base Path</h3>\n<p>Sets a prefix for all API endpoints.</p>\n<h4>No Base Path (Default)</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  # No base_path\n</code></pre>\n<p>Endpoints:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>POST /workflows/runs</code></li>\n<li><code>GET /workflows</code></li>\n<li><code>GET /tasks/{task_id}</code></li>\n</ul>\n<h4>With Base Path</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /api\n</code></pre>\n<p>Endpoints:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>POST /api/workflows/runs</code></li>\n<li><code>GET /api/workflows</code></li>\n<li><code>GET /api/tasks/{task_id}</code></li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Reverse Proxy Configuration</h3>\n<p>When running behind a reverse proxy like Nginx or Caddy.</p>\n<h4>model-compose Configuration</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  host: 127.0.0.1  # Accessible from proxy only\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /ai   # Match proxy path\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Nginx Configuration Example</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-nginx\">server {\n    listen 80;\n    server_name example.com;\n\n    location /ai/ {\n        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080/ai/;\n        proxy_set_header Host $host;\n        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;\n        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;\n        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;\n    }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Now external access to <code>http://example.com/ai/workflows/runs</code> is forwarded by Nginx to internal <code>http://127.0.0.1:8080/ai/workflows/runs</code>.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>7.8 Controller Best Practices</h2>\n<h3>1. Port Configuration by Environment</h3>\n<p>Use different ports for development, staging, and production:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: ${env.PORT | 8080}  # Environment variable or default 8080\n  base_path: /api\n</code></pre>\n<h3>2. Proper CORS Configuration</h3>\n<p>In production, allow only specific domains:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># Development environment\ncontroller:\n  type: http-server\n  origins: &quot;*&quot;\n\n# Production environment\ncontroller:\n  type: http-server\n  origins: &quot;https://app.example.com,https://admin.example.com&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<h3>3. Concurrency Limit Configuration</h3>\n<p>Set appropriate <code>max_concurrent_count</code> based on resource usage:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># GPU-using workflows - Limited concurrency\ncontroller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  max_concurrent_count: 2  # Consider GPU memory limits\n\n# Lightweight API call workflows - High concurrency\ncontroller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  max_concurrent_count: 20\n</code></pre>\n<h3>4. Utilize Asynchronous Execution</h3>\n<p>Execute workflows with long execution times asynchronously:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">// Client code example\nasync function runLongWorkflow(input) {\n  // 1. Start workflow asynchronously\n  const response = await fetch('/api/workflows/runs', {\n    method: 'POST',\n    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n    body: JSON.stringify({\n      workflow_id: 'long-task',\n      input: input,\n      wait_for_completion: false\n    })\n  });\n\n  const { task_id } = await response.json();\n\n  // 2. Poll for status\n  while (true) {\n    const taskResponse = await fetch(`/api/tasks/${task_id}`);\n    const task = await taskResponse.json();\n\n    if (task.status === 'completed') {\n      return task.output;\n    } else if (task.status === 'failed') {\n      throw new Error(task.error);\n    }\n\n    await new Promise(resolve =&gt; setTimeout(resolve, 2000)); // Wait 2 seconds\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>5. Proper base_path Usage</h3>\n<p>Set base_path consistently when running behind a reverse proxy:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  host: 127.0.0.1\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /ai-service  # Exactly match proxy path\n</code></pre>\n<h3>6. Utilize output_only</h3>\n<p>Use <code>output_only</code> when you want to reduce API response size:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># When task_id is not needed on the client\nPOST /api/workflows/runs\n{\n  &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;simple-chat&quot;,\n  &quot;input&quot;: { &quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Hello&quot; },\n  &quot;wait_for_completion&quot;: true,\n  &quot;output_only&quot;: true\n}\n\n# Response: Returns only output without task_id and status\n{ &quot;message&quot;: &quot;Hello! How can I help?&quot; }\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>Next Steps</h2>\n<p>Try these:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Build REST APIs with HTTP server</li>\n<li>Build Streamable HTTP server with MCP server</li>\n<li>Utilize asynchronous execution and task status querying</li>\n<li>Run behind a reverse proxy</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<p><strong>Next Chapter</strong>: <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/08-websocket-interface\">8. WebSocket Interface</a></p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Chapter 7: Controller Configuration"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "user-guide/08-websocket-interface",
      "html": "<h1>Chapter 8: WebSocket Interface</h1>\n<p>This chapter explains how to use model-compose's WebSocket interface for real-time task monitoring, workflow execution, and bidirectional control over a persistent connection.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>8.1 WebSocket Overview</h2>\n<h3>8.1.1 What is the WebSocket Interface?</h3>\n<p>The WebSocket interface adds a <code>/ws</code> endpoint to the HTTP server controller, enabling real-time bidirectional communication between clients and the server. Instead of polling <code>GET /tasks/{task_id}</code> repeatedly, clients receive instant status updates as tasks progress.</p>\n<p><strong>Benefits:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Real-time task status updates (no polling)</li>\n<li>Bidirectional communication (server push + client commands)</li>\n<li>Lower latency for status changes and interrupt handling</li>\n<li>Efficient resource usage with a single persistent connection</li>\n<li>Monitor multiple tasks simultaneously over one connection</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Use Cases:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Real-time dashboards monitoring workflow execution</li>\n<li>Interactive applications with interrupt/resume flows</li>\n<li>Chat applications requiring immediate feedback</li>\n<li>Multi-task monitoring from a single client</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>8.1.2 WebSocket vs REST API</h3>\n<p>Both interfaces support workflow execution. Choose based on your needs:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Scenario</th>\n<th>Recommended</th>\n<th>Reason</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Simple batch jobs</td>\n<td>REST API</td>\n<td>No WebSocket connection needed</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Real-time UI (chat, generation)</td>\n<td>WebSocket</td>\n<td>Single connection handles everything</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>External system integration</td>\n<td>REST API + WebSocket</td>\n<td>Standard HTTP to start, monitor via WebSocket</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Multi-task monitoring</td>\n<td>WebSocket</td>\n<td>One connection for all tasks</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>curl/Postman testing</td>\n<td>REST API</td>\n<td>Simple request/response</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>8.1.3 Delivery Behavior</h3>\n<p>Subscribed clients receive task state changes and per-job lifecycle events in real time:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong><code>task_state</code></strong> — pushed whenever the task's status changes (<code>pending → processing → completed</code>, etc.). On subscription, the current state is delivered once in the <code>task_subscribed</code> response so the client can catch up immediately.</li>\n<li><strong><code>job_event</code></strong> — pushed for each <code>started</code> / <code>completed</code> / <code>failed</code> / <code>routed</code> transition of every job inside the workflow. If the client stays connected for the duration of the run, all events are delivered in the order they occur.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Both message types are sent at emission time and, under normal operation, arrive without loss. Messages are not buffered after they're emitted, so <strong>events that happened before you subscribed are not replayed</strong> — subscribe at workflow start (<code>run_workflow</code> with <code>subscribe_task: true</code>) to ensure full coverage.</p>\n<h3>8.1.4 How It Works</h3>\n<pre><code>Client                          Server\n  │                               │\n  │──── WebSocket Connect ───────&gt;│  ws://localhost:8080/ws\n  │&lt;─── Connection Accepted ──────│\n  │                               │\n  │──── run_workflow ────────────&gt;│  Execute workflow\n  │&lt;─── workflow_started ─────────│  Returns task_id\n  │                               │\n  │&lt;─── task_state (processing) ──│  Real-time updates\n  │&lt;─── task_state (interrupted) ─│  Interrupt notification\n  │                               │\n  │──── resume_task ─────────────&gt;│  Resume workflow\n  │&lt;─── task_resumed ─────────────│\n  │&lt;─── task_state (completed) ───│  Final result\n  │                               │\n  │──── close ───────────────────&gt;│\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>8.2 Configuration</h2>\n<h3>8.2.1 Enabling WebSocket</h3>\n<p>WebSocket is enabled by default when using the HTTP server controller. No additional configuration is required for basic usage.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n</code></pre>\n<p>The WebSocket endpoint is available at <code>ws://localhost:8080/ws</code>.</p>\n<h3>8.2.2 WebSocket Configuration Options</h3>\n<p>The <code>websocket</code> field accepts either a boolean or a configuration object:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>websocket: true</code> (default) — enable with default settings</li>\n<li><code>websocket: false</code> — disable WebSocket support</li>\n<li><code>websocket: { ... }</code> — enable with custom settings</li>\n</ul>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  origins: &quot;*&quot;\n  websocket:\n    path: /ws\n    max_connection_count: 100\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Configuration Fields:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>path</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>/ws</code></td>\n<td>WebSocket endpoint path</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_connection_count</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td>unlimited</td>\n<td>Maximum concurrent WebSocket connections (best-effort; a small overrun is possible between the connection count check and accept)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ping_interval</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>30</code></td>\n<td>Server-side ping interval in seconds (<code>0</code> to disable)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>ping_timeout</code></td>\n<td>integer</td>\n<td><code>10</code></td>\n<td>Ping timeout in seconds</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>8.2.3 Configuration Examples</h3>\n<h4>Development Environment</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8080\n  origins: &quot;*&quot;\n  # WebSocket enabled by default, no extra config needed\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Production Environment</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  host: 127.0.0.1\n  port: 8080\n  origins: &quot;https://app.example.com&quot;\n  websocket:\n    path: /ws\n    max_connection_count: 100\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Disable WebSocket</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  websocket: false\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>8.3 Connecting to WebSocket</h2>\n<h3>8.3.1 Basic Connection</h3>\n<p>Connect to the WebSocket endpoint:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">const ws = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:8080/ws');\n\nws.onopen = () =&gt; {\n  console.log('Connected');\n};\n\nws.onmessage = (event) =&gt; {\n  const message = JSON.parse(event.data);\n  console.log('Received:', message);\n};\n\nws.onclose = () =&gt; {\n  console.log('Disconnected');\n};\n</code></pre>\n<pre><code class=\"language-python\">import asyncio\nimport websockets\nimport json\n\nasync def connect():\n    async with websockets.connect('ws://localhost:8080/ws') as ws:\n        print('Connected')\n        async for message in ws:\n            data = json.loads(message)\n            print('Received:', data)\n\nasyncio.run(connect())\n</code></pre>\n<h3>8.3.2 Session ID</h3>\n<p>You can specify a session ID via query parameter to identify your connection:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">const sessionId = crypto.randomUUID();\nconst ws = new WebSocket(`ws://localhost:8080/ws?session=${sessionId}`);\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li>If not specified, the server generates a UUID automatically.</li>\n<li>A session ID can only have one active connection. Duplicate connections with the same session ID are rejected (close code <code>4409</code>).</li>\n<li>Session IDs enable REST API integration (see <a href=\"#85-rest-api-integration\">Section 8.5</a>).</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>8.3.3 Auto-Subscribe on Connect</h3>\n<p>Subscribe to a task immediately on connection using the <code>task</code> query parameter:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">const ws = new WebSocket(`ws://localhost:8080/ws?task=${taskId}`);\n</code></pre>\n<p>This is equivalent to connecting and then sending a <code>subscribe_task</code> message.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>8.4 WebSocket Messages</h2>\n<h3>8.4.1 Message Format</h3>\n<p>All messages use a common JSON envelope:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;type&quot;: &quot;message_type&quot;,\n  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;optional_message_id&quot;,\n  &quot;data&quot;: { }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li><code>type</code> (string, required): Message type identifier</li>\n<li><code>id</code> (string, optional): Unique message ID for request-response correlation</li>\n<li><code>data</code> (object, optional per type): Message-specific payload. May be omitted for messages with no payload (e.g., <code>ping</code>); the server treats a missing <code>data</code> as <code>{}</code>.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>8.4.2 Client → Server Messages</h3>\n<h4><code>run_workflow</code> — Execute a Workflow</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;type&quot;: &quot;run_workflow&quot;,\n  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;msg-001&quot;,\n  &quot;data&quot;: {\n    &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;chat-completion&quot;,\n    &quot;input&quot;: {\n      &quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Hello, AI!&quot;\n    },\n    &quot;subscribe_task&quot;: true\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Fields:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>workflow_id</code> (string, optional): Workflow to execute (default: <code>__default__</code>)</li>\n<li><code>input</code> (object, optional): Workflow input parameters</li>\n<li><code>subscribe_task</code> (boolean, default: <code>true</code>): Automatically subscribe to task status updates</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Response:</strong> <code>workflow_started</code> message. If <code>subscribe_task</code> is <code>true</code>, you'll also receive <code>task_state</code> updates.</p>\n<h4><code>subscribe_task</code> — Subscribe to Task Updates</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;type&quot;: &quot;subscribe_task&quot;,\n  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;msg-002&quot;,\n  &quot;data&quot;: {\n    &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01HXYZ...&quot;\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Fields:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>task_id</code> (string, required): Task ID to monitor (ULID format)</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Response:</strong> <code>task_subscribed</code> message with current state, followed by <code>task_state</code> updates on changes.</p>\n<h4><code>unsubscribe_task</code> — Stop Monitoring a Task</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;type&quot;: &quot;unsubscribe_task&quot;,\n  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;msg-003&quot;,\n  &quot;data&quot;: {\n    &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01HXYZ...&quot;\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Response:</strong> <code>task_unsubscribed</code> message.</p>\n<h4><code>resume_task</code> — Resume an Interrupted Task</h4>\n<p>This is the WebSocket equivalent of <code>POST /tasks/{task_id}/resume</code>.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;type&quot;: &quot;resume_task&quot;,\n  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;msg-004&quot;,\n  &quot;data&quot;: {\n    &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01HXYZ...&quot;,\n    &quot;job_id&quot;: &quot;review-step&quot;,\n    &quot;answer&quot;: {\n      &quot;approved&quot;: true\n    }\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Fields:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>task_id</code> (string, required): Task to resume</li>\n<li><code>job_id</code> (string, required): Interrupted job ID (from <code>interrupt.job_id</code>)</li>\n<li><code>answer</code> (any, optional): Response value to pass to the workflow</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Response:</strong> <code>task_resumed</code> or <code>error</code> message.</p>\n<h4><code>get_task</code> — Query Task State (One-time)</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;type&quot;: &quot;get_task&quot;,\n  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;msg-005&quot;,\n  &quot;data&quot;: {\n    &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01HXYZ...&quot;\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Response:</strong> <code>task_state</code> message with current state. Does not create a subscription.</p>\n<h4><code>ping</code> — Connection Health Check</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;type&quot;: &quot;ping&quot;,\n  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;msg-006&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Response:</strong> <code>pong</code> message.</p>\n<h3>8.4.3 Server → Client Messages</h3>\n<h4><code>workflow_started</code> — Workflow Execution Started</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;type&quot;: &quot;workflow_started&quot;,\n  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;msg-001&quot;,\n  &quot;data&quot;: {\n    &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01HXYZ...&quot;,\n    &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;chat-completion&quot;,\n    &quot;status&quot;: &quot;pending&quot;\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Sent in response to <code>run_workflow</code>.</p>\n<h4><code>task_subscribed</code> — Subscription Confirmed</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;type&quot;: &quot;task_subscribed&quot;,\n  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;msg-002&quot;,\n  &quot;data&quot;: {\n    &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01HXYZ...&quot;,\n    &quot;state&quot;: {\n      &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01HXYZ...&quot;,\n      &quot;status&quot;: &quot;processing&quot;,\n      &quot;output&quot;: null,\n      &quot;error&quot;: null,\n      &quot;interrupt&quot;: null\n    }\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Sent in response to <code>subscribe_task</code>. Includes the current task state at the time of subscription.</p>\n<h4><code>task_unsubscribed</code> — Subscription Removed</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;type&quot;: &quot;task_unsubscribed&quot;,\n  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;msg-003&quot;,\n  &quot;data&quot;: {\n    &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01HXYZ...&quot;\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h4><code>task_state</code> — Task Status Update</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;type&quot;: &quot;task_state&quot;,\n  &quot;data&quot;: {\n    &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01HXYZ...&quot;,\n    &quot;status&quot;: &quot;interrupted&quot;,\n    &quot;output&quot;: null,\n    &quot;error&quot;: null,\n    &quot;interrupt&quot;: {\n      &quot;job_id&quot;: &quot;review-step&quot;,\n      &quot;phase&quot;: &quot;before&quot;,\n      &quot;message&quot;: &quot;Approval required&quot;,\n      &quot;metadata&quot;: { &quot;cost&quot;: 0.5 }\n    },\n    &quot;timestamp&quot;: &quot;2026-02-06T12:34:56.789Z&quot;\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Fields:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>status</code>: <code>&quot;pending&quot;</code> | <code>&quot;processing&quot;</code> | <code>&quot;interrupted&quot;</code> | <code>&quot;completed&quot;</code> | <code>&quot;failed&quot;</code></li>\n<li><code>output</code>: Result data on completion (JSON-serializable values only; non-serializable outputs like images return <code>null</code>)</li>\n<li><code>error</code>: Error message on failure</li>\n<li><code>interrupt</code>: Interrupt details when status is <code>&quot;interrupted&quot;</code> (<code>job_id</code>, <code>phase</code>, <code>message</code>, <code>metadata</code>)</li>\n<li><code>timestamp</code>: State change time (ISO 8601)</li>\n</ul>\n<h4><code>job_event</code> — Per-Job Lifecycle Event</h4>\n<p>Pushed for each job inside a workflow as it transitions through its lifecycle. Unlike <code>task_state</code> (which reflects the <em>workflow as a whole</em>), <code>job_event</code> provides fine-grained visibility into individual jobs.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;type&quot;: &quot;job_event&quot;,\n  &quot;data&quot;: {\n    &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01HXYZ...&quot;,\n    &quot;run_id&quot;: &quot;01HRUN...&quot;,\n    &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;chat-completion&quot;,\n    &quot;job_id&quot;: &quot;job-quote&quot;,\n    &quot;event&quot;: &quot;completed&quot;,\n    &quot;elapsed&quot;: 1.78,\n    &quot;output&quot;: { &quot;quote&quot;: &quot;...&quot; },\n    &quot;error&quot;: null,\n    &quot;next_job_id&quot;: null,\n    &quot;timestamp&quot;: &quot;2026-02-06T12:34:56.789Z&quot;\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Fields:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>task_id</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>Task this job belongs to</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>run_id</code></td>\n<td>string | string[] | null</td>\n<td>Component action run id(s). A string for a single run, an array when <code>repeat_count</code> produces multiple runs, <code>null</code> for non-component jobs or when not yet issued (e.g. some <code>started</code> events)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>workflow_id</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>Workflow id</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>job_id</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>Job id from the workflow config</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>event</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td><code>&quot;started&quot;</code> | <code>&quot;completed&quot;</code> | <code>&quot;failed&quot;</code> | <code>&quot;routed&quot;</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>elapsed</code></td>\n<td>number</td>\n<td>Seconds elapsed since job start (present on <code>completed</code> / <code>failed</code> / <code>routed</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>output</code></td>\n<td>any</td>\n<td>Job output on <code>completed</code> (only when JSON-serializable; non-serializable values become <code>null</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>error</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>Error message on <code>failed</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>next_job_id</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>Target job id on <code>routed</code> (emitted by routing jobs like <code>switch</code> / <code>if</code> / <code>random_router</code>)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>timestamp</code></td>\n<td>string</td>\n<td>Emission time (ISO 8601, UTC)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Event ordering for a typical job:</strong></p>\n<pre><code>started → completed\nstarted → failed\nstarted → routed → started(next_job) → ...\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Notes:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>job_event</code> is delivered to all clients subscribed to the parent <code>task_id</code> (no separate subscription needed).</li>\n<li>The <code>started</code> event may arrive before <code>run_id</code> is available — <code>run_id</code> is generated when a <code>ComponentJob</code> actually invokes its action, which happens after the job task is scheduled. The <code>completed</code> / <code>failed</code> event always carries <code>run_id</code>.</li>\n<li>For jobs that aren't backed by a component (e.g. <code>delay</code>, <code>filter</code>, <code>switch</code>), <code>run_id</code> stays <code>null</code>.</li>\n</ul>\n<h4><code>task_resumed</code> — Task Resumed</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;type&quot;: &quot;task_resumed&quot;,\n  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;msg-004&quot;,\n  &quot;data&quot;: {\n    &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;01HXYZ...&quot;,\n    &quot;status&quot;: &quot;processing&quot;\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Sent in response to <code>resume_task</code> on success.</p>\n<h4><code>error</code> — Error Message</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;type&quot;: &quot;error&quot;,\n  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;msg-001&quot;,\n  &quot;data&quot;: {\n    &quot;code&quot;: &quot;WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND&quot;,\n    &quot;message&quot;: &quot;Workflow 'invalid-workflow' not found&quot;,\n    &quot;details&quot;: {\n      &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;invalid-workflow&quot;\n    }\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Error Codes:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Code</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND</code></td>\n<td>Specified workflow does not exist</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TASK_NOT_FOUND</code></td>\n<td>Specified task does not exist</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>INVALID_REQUEST</code></td>\n<td>Invalid message format or missing required fields</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>TASK_NOT_INTERRUPTED</code></td>\n<td>Task is not in interrupted state</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>JOB_ID_MISMATCH</code></td>\n<td>Job ID doesn't match current interrupt point</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>INTERNAL_ERROR</code></td>\n<td>Unexpected server error</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h4><code>pong</code> — Ping Response</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;type&quot;: &quot;pong&quot;,\n  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;msg-006&quot;,\n  &quot;data&quot;: {\n    &quot;timestamp&quot;: &quot;2026-02-06T12:34:56.789Z&quot;\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>8.5 REST API Integration</h2>\n<p>WebSocket and REST API can be used together. This is useful when you want to start workflows via REST but monitor them in real time via WebSocket.</p>\n<h3>8.5.1 <code>subscribe_task</code> Parameter</h3>\n<p>The <code>POST /workflows/runs</code> endpoint supports a <code>subscribe_task</code> parameter:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl -X POST &quot;http://localhost:8080/workflows/runs?session_id=my-session-id&quot; \\\n  -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; \\\n  -d '{\n    &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;chat-completion&quot;,\n    &quot;input&quot;: { &quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Hello&quot; },\n    &quot;wait_for_completion&quot;: false,\n    &quot;subscribe_task&quot;: true\n  }'\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Requirements:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>session_id</code> query parameter is required when <code>subscribe_task: true</code></li>\n<li>An active WebSocket connection with the matching session ID must exist</li>\n<li><code>wait_for_completion</code> must be <code>false</code> (combining both is not allowed, returns 400)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>8.5.2 <code>wait_for_completion</code> and <code>subscribe_task</code> Combinations</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>wait_for_completion</th>\n<th>subscribe_task</th>\n<th>Behavior</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>true</code> (default)</td>\n<td><code>false</code> (default)</td>\n<td>HTTP waits until completion. No subscription. (Existing behavior)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Returns PENDING immediately. No subscription.</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Returns PENDING immediately + auto-subscribes via WebSocket. <strong>Recommended pattern.</strong></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td><strong>Not allowed.</strong> Returns 400 Bad Request.</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>8.5.3 Pattern: WebSocket First + REST Execution</h3>\n<p>The recommended pattern for REST + WebSocket integration:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">// 1. Generate session ID and connect WebSocket\nconst sessionId = crypto.randomUUID();\nconst ws = new WebSocket(`ws://localhost:8080/ws?session=${sessionId}`);\n\nws.onmessage = (event) =&gt; {\n  const msg = JSON.parse(event.data);\n  if (msg.type === 'task_state') {\n    console.log('Status:', msg.data.status);\n    if (msg.data.status === 'completed') {\n      console.log('Result:', msg.data.output);\n    }\n  }\n};\n\n// 2. Execute workflow via REST API (same session ID)\nws.onopen = async () =&gt; {\n  const response = await fetch(`/workflows/runs?session_id=${sessionId}`, {\n    method: 'POST',\n    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n    body: JSON.stringify({\n      workflow_id: 'chat-completion',\n      input: { prompt: 'Hello' },\n      wait_for_completion: false,\n      subscribe_task: true\n    })\n  });\n\n  const { task_id } = await response.json();\n  console.log('Workflow started:', task_id);\n  // Updates will arrive automatically via WebSocket\n};\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>8.6 Usage Patterns</h2>\n<h3>8.6.1 Pattern 1: Execute and Monitor via WebSocket</h3>\n<p>The simplest pattern — execute a workflow and receive updates over a single WebSocket connection.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">const ws = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:8080/ws');\n\nws.onopen = () =&gt; {\n  ws.send(JSON.stringify({\n    type: 'run_workflow',\n    id: 'msg-001',\n    data: {\n      workflow_id: 'chat-completion',\n      input: { prompt: 'Hello, AI!' },\n      subscribe_task: true\n    }\n  }));\n};\n\nws.onmessage = (event) =&gt; {\n  const msg = JSON.parse(event.data);\n\n  switch (msg.type) {\n    case 'workflow_started':\n      console.log('Started:', msg.data.task_id);\n      break;\n\n    case 'task_state':\n      console.log('Status:', msg.data.status);\n      if (msg.data.status === 'completed') {\n        console.log('Output:', msg.data.output);\n        ws.close();\n      }\n      break;\n\n    case 'error':\n      console.error('Error:', msg.data.message);\n      break;\n  }\n};\n</code></pre>\n<pre><code class=\"language-python\">import asyncio\nimport websockets\nimport json\n\nasync def run_and_monitor():\n    async with websockets.connect('ws://localhost:8080/ws') as ws:\n        # Execute workflow\n        await ws.send(json.dumps({\n            'type': 'run_workflow',\n            'id': 'msg-001',\n            'data': {\n                'workflow_id': 'chat-completion',\n                'input': {'prompt': 'Hello, AI!'},\n                'subscribe_task': True\n            }\n        }))\n\n        # Receive updates\n        async for message in ws:\n            msg = json.loads(message)\n\n            if msg['type'] == 'workflow_started':\n                print(f&quot;Started: {msg['data']['task_id']}&quot;)\n\n            elif msg['type'] == 'task_state':\n                status = msg['data']['status']\n                print(f&quot;Status: {status}&quot;)\n                if status == 'completed':\n                    print(f&quot;Output: {msg['data']['output']}&quot;)\n                    break\n                elif status == 'failed':\n                    print(f&quot;Error: {msg['data']['error']}&quot;)\n                    break\n\nasyncio.run(run_and_monitor())\n</code></pre>\n<h3>8.6.2 Pattern 2: Interactive Interrupt/Resume</h3>\n<p>Handle workflows with human-in-the-loop interrupt points.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">const ws = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:8080/ws');\n\nws.onopen = () =&gt; {\n  ws.send(JSON.stringify({\n    type: 'run_workflow',\n    id: 'msg-001',\n    data: {\n      workflow_id: 'content-review',\n      input: { text: 'Generate a blog post about AI' },\n      subscribe_task: true\n    }\n  }));\n};\n\nws.onmessage = (event) =&gt; {\n  const msg = JSON.parse(event.data);\n\n  if (msg.type === 'task_state' &amp;&amp; msg.data.status === 'interrupted') {\n    const interrupt = msg.data.interrupt;\n    console.log(`Interrupt at job '${interrupt.job_id}': ${interrupt.message}`);\n\n    // Respond to the interrupt\n    ws.send(JSON.stringify({\n      type: 'resume_task',\n      id: 'msg-002',\n      data: {\n        task_id: msg.data.task_id,\n        job_id: interrupt.job_id,\n        answer: { approved: true }\n      }\n    }));\n  }\n\n  if (msg.type === 'task_state' &amp;&amp; msg.data.status === 'completed') {\n    console.log('Final output:', msg.data.output);\n    ws.close();\n  }\n};\n</code></pre>\n<h3>8.6.3 Pattern 3: Subscribe to Existing Task</h3>\n<p>Monitor a task that was started via REST API or another client.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">// 1. Start workflow via REST API\nconst response = await fetch('/workflows/runs', {\n  method: 'POST',\n  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n  body: JSON.stringify({\n    workflow_id: 'batch-processing',\n    input: { data: '...' },\n    wait_for_completion: false\n  })\n});\n\nconst { task_id } = await response.json();\n\n// 2. Later, connect WebSocket and subscribe\nconst ws = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:8080/ws');\nws.onopen = () =&gt; {\n  ws.send(JSON.stringify({\n    type: 'subscribe_task',\n    id: 'msg-001',\n    data: { task_id }\n  }));\n};\n\nws.onmessage = (event) =&gt; {\n  const msg = JSON.parse(event.data);\n  if (msg.type === 'task_subscribed') {\n    console.log('Current state:', msg.data.state.status);\n  }\n  if (msg.type === 'task_state') {\n    console.log('Updated:', msg.data.status);\n  }\n};\n</code></pre>\n<h3>8.6.4 Pattern 4: Per-Job Progress Visualization</h3>\n<p>Render a progress timeline by listening to <code>job_event</code> messages alongside <code>task_state</code>. Useful when you need to show users <em>which job is running right now</em> instead of just an overall spinner.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">const ws = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:8080/ws');\n\nws.onopen = () =&gt; {\n  ws.send(JSON.stringify({\n    type: 'run_workflow',\n    id: 'msg-001',\n    data: {\n      workflow_id: 'inspire-with-voice',\n      input: {},\n      subscribe_task: true\n    }\n  }));\n};\n\nws.onmessage = (event) =&gt; {\n  const msg = JSON.parse(event.data);\n\n  if (msg.type === 'job_event') {\n    const { job_id, event: phase, elapsed, run_id } = msg.data;\n    if (phase === 'started') {\n      console.log(`▶ ${job_id} started`);\n    } else if (phase === 'completed') {\n      console.log(`✓ ${job_id} completed in ${elapsed.toFixed(2)}s (run_id=${run_id})`);\n    } else if (phase === 'failed') {\n      console.log(`✗ ${job_id} failed: ${msg.data.error}`);\n    } else if (phase === 'routed') {\n      console.log(`→ ${job_id} routed to ${msg.data.next_job_id}`);\n    }\n  }\n\n  if (msg.type === 'task_state' &amp;&amp; msg.data.status === 'completed') {\n    console.log('Workflow done.');\n    ws.close();\n  }\n};\n</code></pre>\n<h3>8.6.5 Pattern 5: Multi-Task Dashboard</h3>\n<p>Monitor multiple tasks over a single WebSocket connection.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">const ws = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:8080/ws');\nconst tasks = {};\n\nws.onopen = async () =&gt; {\n  // Start multiple workflows\n  for (const workflow of ['translate', 'summarize', 'classify']) {\n    ws.send(JSON.stringify({\n      type: 'run_workflow',\n      id: `run-${workflow}`,\n      data: {\n        workflow_id: workflow,\n        input: { text: 'Some input text' },\n        subscribe_task: true\n      }\n    }));\n  }\n};\n\nws.onmessage = (event) =&gt; {\n  const msg = JSON.parse(event.data);\n\n  if (msg.type === 'workflow_started') {\n    tasks[msg.data.task_id] = { workflow: msg.data.workflow_id, status: 'pending' };\n    console.log(`[${msg.data.workflow_id}] Started: ${msg.data.task_id}`);\n  }\n\n  if (msg.type === 'task_state') {\n    const task = tasks[msg.data.task_id];\n    if (task) {\n      task.status = msg.data.status;\n      console.log(`[${task.workflow}] ${msg.data.status}`);\n\n      if (msg.data.status === 'completed') {\n        task.output = msg.data.output;\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Check if all tasks are done\n    const allDone = Object.values(tasks).every(\n      t =&gt; t.status === 'completed' || t.status === 'failed'\n    );\n    if (allDone) {\n      console.log('All tasks completed:', tasks);\n      ws.close();\n    }\n  }\n};\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>8.7 Connection Management</h2>\n<h3>8.7.1 Session and Reconnection</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Each WebSocket connection is identified by a session ID (auto-generated or specified via <code>?session=</code>).</li>\n<li>If a connection drops, you can reconnect with the same session ID (after the previous connection is fully closed).</li>\n<li>To create a new session, simply omit the <code>?session=</code> parameter or use a new UUID.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>8.7.2 Connection Lifecycle</h3>\n<p>When a WebSocket connection closes:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>All task subscriptions for that client are automatically removed.</li>\n<li>Running workflows are <strong>not</strong> affected — WebSocket is a monitoring/control channel, not tied to workflow execution.</li>\n<li>The client can reconnect and re-subscribe to continue monitoring.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>8.7.3 Connection Limits</h3>\n<p>When <code>max_connection_count</code> is configured and the limit is reached, new connections are rejected with close code <code>4429</code> (Too Many Connections).</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  websocket:\n    max_connection_count: 50  # Reject connections beyond 50\n</code></pre>\n<h3>8.7.4 Keep-Alive with Ping</h3>\n<p>Use the <code>ping</code> message to verify the connection is alive:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">// Send ping every 30 seconds\nsetInterval(() =&gt; {\n  if (ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {\n    ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'ping', id: 'heartbeat' }));\n  }\n}, 30000);\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>8.8 Security Considerations</h2>\n<h3>8.8.1 Session ID Security</h3>\n<p>Session IDs (<code>?session=</code> and <code>?session_id=</code>) are not authentication mechanisms:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Anyone who knows a session ID can link REST subscriptions to that session's WebSocket.</li>\n<li>In untrusted network environments, consider adding token-based authentication at the application level.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>8.8.2 CORS and Origins</h3>\n<p>The <code>origins</code> setting in controller configuration applies to WebSocket connections from browsers:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  origins: &quot;https://app.example.com&quot;  # Restrict browser origins\n</code></pre>\n<p>Note: This only applies to browser-initiated connections. Server-to-server WebSocket connections are not restricted by CORS.</p>\n<h3>8.8.3 Production Recommendations</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Use WSS (WebSocket over TLS) via a reverse proxy</li>\n<li>Restrict origins to trusted domains</li>\n<li>Set <code>max_connection_count</code> to prevent resource exhaustion</li>\n<li>Consider adding application-level authentication</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Nginx reverse proxy for WebSocket:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-nginx\">server {\n    listen 443 ssl;\n    server_name app.example.com;\n\n    ssl_certificate /path/to/cert.pem;\n    ssl_certificate_key /path/to/key.pem;\n\n    location /ws {\n        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080/ws;\n        proxy_http_version 1.1;\n        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;\n        proxy_set_header Connection &quot;upgrade&quot;;\n        proxy_set_header Host $host;\n        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;\n        proxy_read_timeout 3600s;  # Keep connection alive\n    }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>8.9 Best Practices</h2>\n<h3>1. Use <code>subscribe_task: true</code> for Real-Time Monitoring</h3>\n<p>When executing workflows via WebSocket, always set <code>subscribe_task: true</code> to receive automatic updates:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;type&quot;: &quot;run_workflow&quot;,\n  &quot;data&quot;: {\n    &quot;workflow_id&quot;: &quot;my-workflow&quot;,\n    &quot;subscribe_task&quot;: true\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>2. Handle All Message Types</h3>\n<p>Always include handlers for <code>error</code> messages and unexpected states:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">ws.onmessage = (event) =&gt; {\n  const msg = JSON.parse(event.data);\n\n  switch (msg.type) {\n    case 'workflow_started':\n    case 'task_state':\n    case 'job_event':\n    case 'task_subscribed':\n    case 'task_resumed':\n      // Handle normally\n      break;\n    case 'error':\n      console.error(`[${msg.data.code}] ${msg.data.message}`);\n      break;\n    default:\n      console.warn('Unknown message type:', msg.type);\n  }\n};\n</code></pre>\n<h3>3. Implement Reconnection Logic</h3>\n<p>WebSocket connections can drop. Implement exponential backoff reconnection:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">function connectWithRetry(url, maxRetries = 5) {\n  let retries = 0;\n\n  function connect() {\n    const ws = new WebSocket(url);\n\n    ws.onopen = () =&gt; {\n      retries = 0; // Reset on successful connection\n      // Re-subscribe to tasks if needed\n    };\n\n    ws.onclose = () =&gt; {\n      if (retries &lt; maxRetries) {\n        const delay = Math.min(1000 * Math.pow(2, retries), 30000);\n        retries++;\n        console.log(`Reconnecting in ${delay}ms...`);\n        setTimeout(connect, delay);\n      }\n    };\n\n    return ws;\n  }\n\n  return connect();\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>4. Use Message IDs for Correlation</h3>\n<p>Include <code>id</code> in request messages to correlate responses:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">const msgId = `msg-${Date.now()}`;\nws.send(JSON.stringify({\n  type: 'run_workflow',\n  id: msgId,\n  data: { workflow_id: 'my-workflow' }\n}));\n\n// Response will include the same id\nws.onmessage = (event) =&gt; {\n  const msg = JSON.parse(event.data);\n  if (msg.id === msgId &amp;&amp; msg.type === 'workflow_started') {\n    // This is the response to our specific request\n  }\n};\n</code></pre>\n<h3>5. Unsubscribe When Done</h3>\n<p>Unsubscribe from completed tasks to keep the connection clean:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">if (msg.data.status === 'completed' || msg.data.status === 'failed') {\n  ws.send(JSON.stringify({\n    type: 'unsubscribe_task',\n    data: { task_id: msg.data.task_id }\n  }));\n}\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>Next Steps</h2>\n<p>Try these:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Connect to a WebSocket endpoint and execute a workflow</li>\n<li>Build a real-time monitoring dashboard</li>\n<li>Handle interrupt/resume flows interactively</li>\n<li>Combine REST API and WebSocket for hybrid architectures</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<p><strong>Previous Chapter</strong>: <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/07-controller-configuration\">7. Controller Configuration</a> | <strong>Next Chapter</strong>: <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/09-webui-configuration\">9. Web UI Configuration</a></p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Chapter 8: WebSocket Interface"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "user-guide/09-webui-configuration",
      "html": "<h1>Chapter 9: Web UI Configuration</h1>\n<p>This chapter covers how to configure model-compose's Web UI. Learn how to set up a web interface for testing and running workflows using Gradio and static file drivers.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>9.1 Web UI Overview</h2>\n<p>model-compose optionally provides a web interface for testing and running workflows. The Web UI works identically regardless of controller type (<code>http-server</code> or <code>mcp-server</code>) and automatically executes workflows according to the configured controller.</p>\n<h3>Controller Only</h3>\n<p>Running only the controller without Web UI. Suitable for production environments where only API endpoints are needed.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /api\n  # No webui configuration\n</code></pre>\n<p>In this case, workflows can only be executed via the HTTP API (<code>/api/workflows/runs</code>).</p>\n<h3>Controller + Web UI</h3>\n<p>Run Web UI together to test and execute workflows from a browser.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080       # Controller API port\n  base_path: /api\n  webui:\n    driver: gradio # or static\n    port: 8081     # Web UI port (must differ from controller)\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Important</strong>: Web UI must always run on a different port from the controller.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<p>With this configuration, the controller API runs at <code>http://localhost:8080/api</code> and the Web UI at <code>http://localhost:8081</code>. The Web UI internally calls the controller API to execute workflows.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>9.2 Gradio Driver</h2>\n<p>Gradio is an interactive web UI automatically generated based on workflow schemas.</p>\n<h3>Configuration</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /api\n  webui:\n    driver: gradio  # Default (can be omitted)\n    host: 127.0.0.1 # Default\n    port: 8081      # Default\n</code></pre>\n<p>Configuration options:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>driver</code>: Web UI driver (default: <code>gradio</code>)</li>\n<li><code>host</code>: Host address the Web UI server binds to (default: <code>127.0.0.1</code>)</li>\n<li><code>port</code>: Web UI server port (default: <code>8081</code>, must differ from controller port)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Automatic UI Generation</h3>\n<p>Gradio automatically generates UI based on workflow <code>input</code> and <code>output</code> definitions:</p>\n<p><strong>Input Component Mapping</strong>:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>string</code>: Text input (Textbox)</li>\n<li><code>text</code>: Multi-line text input (Textbox, 5-15 lines)</li>\n<li><code>integer</code>: Integer input (Textbox)</li>\n<li><code>number</code>: Number input (Number)</li>\n<li><code>boolean</code>: Checkbox (Checkbox)</li>\n<li><code>list</code>: Comma-separated list (Textbox)</li>\n<li><code>image</code>: Image upload (Image)</li>\n<li><code>audio</code>: Audio upload (Audio)</li>\n<li><code>video</code>: Video upload (Video)</li>\n<li><code>file</code>: File upload (File)</li>\n<li><code>select</code>: Dropdown (Dropdown)</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Output Component Mapping</strong>:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>string</code>, <code>text</code>: Text display (Textbox, read-only)</li>\n<li><code>markdown</code>: Markdown rendering (Markdown)</li>\n<li><code>json</code>, <code>objects</code>: JSON viewer (JSON)</li>\n<li><code>image</code>: Image display (Image)</li>\n<li><code>audio</code>: Audio player (Audio)</li>\n<li><code>video</code>: Video player (Video)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Streaming Output Support</h3>\n<p>When workflow output is specified as <code>as sse-text</code> or <code>as sse-json</code>, it's displayed in real-time streaming.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflow:\n  title: Summarize Text\n  input: ${input}\n  output: ${output as sse-text}  # Streaming output\n\ncomponent:\n  type: model\n  task: text-generation\n  model: facebook/bart-large-cnn\n  text: ${input.text}\n  streaming: true  # Enable streaming in component\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Text Streaming</strong> (<code>sse-text</code>): Accumulates and displays chunks as they arrive (e.g., AI text generation)</li>\n<li><strong>JSON Streaming</strong> (<code>sse-json</code>): Adds each chunk to a list and displays (e.g., sequential generation of multiple results)</li>\n</ul>\n<p>In Gradio UI, output updates in real-time so you can see the generation process.</p>\n<h3>Multiple Workflows</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>When multiple workflows are defined, they're displayed in separate tabs</li>\n<li>Each tab displays the workflow's <code>title</code> or <code>id</code></li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Accessing Gradio UI</h3>\n<pre><code>http://localhost:8081\n</code></pre>\n<p>Each workflow is displayed with the following structure:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Workflow title and description</li>\n<li>Input parameter section</li>\n<li>&quot;Run Workflow&quot; button</li>\n<li>Output value section</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>9.3 Static File Driver</h2>\n<p>Serves custom HTML/CSS/JavaScript files. Uses FastAPI's <code>StaticFiles</code> to serve static files and automatically serves <code>index.html</code> with the <code>html=True</code> option.</p>\n<h3>Configuration</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /api\n  webui:\n    driver: static     # Required\n    host: 127.0.0.1    # Default\n    port: 8081         # Default\n    static_dir: webui  # Default\n</code></pre>\n<p>Configuration options:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>driver</code>: <code>static</code> (required, must be specified since gradio is the default)</li>\n<li><code>host</code>: Host address the Web UI server binds to (default: <code>127.0.0.1</code>)</li>\n<li><code>port</code>: Web UI server port (default: <code>8081</code>)</li>\n<li><code>static_dir</code>: Directory path containing static files (default: <code>webui</code>)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>How It Works</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>All files in the <code>static_dir</code> path are mounted to the <code>/</code> path</li>\n<li>Accessing <code>http://localhost:8081/</code> automatically serves <code>index.html</code></li>\n<li>All static files (CSS, JS, images, etc.) can be referenced with relative paths</li>\n<li>The controller API runs on a separate port (e.g., 8080), so CORS configuration may be needed</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Directory Structure Example</h3>\n<pre><code>webui/\n├── index.html\n├── css/\n│   └── style.css\n├── js/\n│   └── app.js\n└── assets/\n    └── logo.png\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Simple Example</h3>\n<p><strong>index.html</strong>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-html\">&lt;!DOCTYPE html&gt;\n&lt;html&gt;\n&lt;head&gt;\n    &lt;title&gt;AI Workflow UI&lt;/title&gt;\n    &lt;link rel=&quot;stylesheet&quot; href=&quot;/css/style.css&quot;&gt;\n&lt;/head&gt;\n&lt;body&gt;\n    &lt;h1&gt;Workflow Runner&lt;/h1&gt;\n    &lt;div id=&quot;workflow-container&quot;&gt;\n        &lt;input id=&quot;input&quot; type=&quot;text&quot; placeholder=&quot;Enter input...&quot;&gt;\n        &lt;button onclick=&quot;runWorkflow()&quot;&gt;Run&lt;/button&gt;\n        &lt;pre id=&quot;output&quot;&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;\n    &lt;/div&gt;\n    &lt;script src=&quot;/js/app.js&quot;&gt;&lt;/script&gt;\n&lt;/body&gt;\n&lt;/html&gt;\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>js/app.js</strong>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">async function runWorkflow() {\n    const input = document.getElementById('input').value;\n    const output = document.getElementById('output');\n\n    try {\n        const response = await fetch('http://localhost:8080/api/workflows/runs', {\n            method: 'POST',\n            headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n            body: JSON.stringify({\n                workflow_id: 'my-workflow',\n                input: { text: input },\n                wait_for_completion: true,\n                output_only: true\n            })\n        });\n\n        const data = await response.json();\n        output.textContent = JSON.stringify(data, null, 2);\n    } catch (error) {\n        output.textContent = `Error: ${error.message}`;\n    }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note</strong>: The static file driver simply serves files; actual workflow execution must be called directly from JavaScript via the controller API.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<hr />\n<h2>9.4 Web UI Deployment via Reverse Proxy</h2>\n<p>In production environments, you can deploy both the controller API and Web UI together through a reverse proxy like Nginx.</p>\n<h3>model-compose Configuration</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  host: 127.0.0.1  # Accessible from proxy only\n  port: 8080\n  base_path: /api\n  webui:\n    driver: gradio\n    host: 127.0.0.1\n    port: 8081\n</code></pre>\n<h3>Nginx Configuration Example</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-nginx\">server {\n    listen 80;\n    server_name example.com;\n\n    # API proxy\n    location /api/ {\n        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/;\n        proxy_set_header Host $host;\n        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;\n        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;\n        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;\n    }\n\n    # Web UI proxy\n    location / {\n        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8081/;\n        proxy_set_header Host $host;\n        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;\n        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;\n        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;\n    }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>External access:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>API</strong>: <code>http://example.com/api/</code> → <code>http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/</code></li>\n<li><strong>Web UI</strong>: <code>http://example.com/</code> → <code>http://127.0.0.1:8081/</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p>Since the Web UI is served from the same domain as the controller, no separate CORS configuration is needed.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>Next Steps</h2>\n<p>Try these:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Test auto-generated UI with Gradio</li>\n<li>Build custom UI with static file driver</li>\n<li>Display real-time responses with streaming output</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<p><strong>Previous Chapter</strong>: <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/08-websocket-interface\">8. WebSocket Interface</a> | <strong>Next Chapter</strong>: <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/10-local-ai-models\">10. Working with Local AI Models</a></p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "Chapter 9: Web UI Configuration"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "user-guide/10-local-ai-models",
      "html": "<h1>Chapter 10: Working with Local AI Models</h1>\n<p>This chapter covers how to use local AI models with model-compose.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>10.1 Local Model Overview</h2>\n<h3>What are Local Models?</h3>\n<p>Local models are AI models that run directly on your system without external APIs. model-compose supports various drivers and model formats, providing a flexible model execution environment.</p>\n<h3>Supported Model Drivers</h3>\n<p>model-compose supports the following model drivers:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Driver</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n<th>Primary Use Cases</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>huggingface</code></td>\n<td>HuggingFace transformers</td>\n<td>General-purpose inference, widest model support</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>unsloth</code></td>\n<td>Unsloth optimized models</td>\n<td>Fast fine-tuning, memory-efficient training</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>vllm</code></td>\n<td>vLLM inference engine</td>\n<td>High-performance LLM serving, production deployment</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>llamacpp</code></td>\n<td>llama.cpp engine</td>\n<td>CPU inference, GGUF format, low-resource environments</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>custom</code></td>\n<td>Custom implementation</td>\n<td>Special models, custom logic</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Supported Model Formats</h3>\n<p>Various model formats are supported:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Format</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n<th>Compatible Drivers</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>pytorch</code></td>\n<td>PyTorch default format (.bin, .pt)</td>\n<td>huggingface, unsloth</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>safetensors</code></td>\n<td>Safe tensor storage format</td>\n<td>huggingface, unsloth</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>onnx</code></td>\n<td>Optimized cross-platform format</td>\n<td>custom</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>gguf</code></td>\n<td>llama.cpp quantized format</td>\n<td>llamacpp</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>tensorrt</code></td>\n<td>NVIDIA TensorRT optimized</td>\n<td>custom</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Pros and Cons of Local Models</h3>\n<p><strong>Pros:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Cost savings</strong>: No API call costs</li>\n<li><strong>Privacy</strong>: Data never leaves your system</li>\n<li><strong>Offline execution</strong>: No internet connection required</li>\n<li><strong>Customization</strong>: Apply fine-tuning, LoRA adapters</li>\n<li><strong>Low latency</strong>: No network delays (depending on local hardware)</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Cons:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Hardware requirements</strong>: GPU memory and compute power needed</li>\n<li><strong>Model size</strong>: Large model files to download and store</li>\n<li><strong>Configuration complexity</strong>: Environment setup, dependency management</li>\n<li><strong>Performance constraints</strong>: Large models require high-end GPUs</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Basic Usage</h3>\n<p><strong>Simple model loading (HuggingFace)</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">component:\n  type: model\n  task: text-generation\n  model: meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf\n  # Default driver is huggingface\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Specifying driver</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">component:\n  type: model\n  task: text-generation\n  driver: unsloth  # Use Unsloth driver\n  model: unsloth/llama-2-7b-bnb-4bit\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Loading local files</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">component:\n  type: model\n  task: text-generation\n  model:\n    provider: local\n    path: /path/to/model\n    format: pytorch\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>GGUF format</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">component:\n  type: model\n  task: text-generation\n  driver: llamacpp\n  model:\n    provider: local\n    path: /models/llama-2-7b-chat.Q4_K_M.gguf\n    format: gguf\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>10.2 Model Installation and Setup</h2>\n<h3>Specifying Model Sources</h3>\n<p>model-compose can load models through two providers:</p>\n<h4>1.
