generation (faster)\n      num_beams: 1                   # Disable beam search\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Output References:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Streaming: <code>${result[]}</code> (per chunk)</li>\n<li>Non-streaming: <code>${result}</code> (after full completion)</li>\n</ul>\n<h4>Chat Completion Streaming</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">component:\n  type: model\n  task: chat-completion\n  model: microsoft/DialoGPT-medium\n  streaming: true\n  action:\n    messages:\n      - role: user\n        content: ${input.message as text}\n    params:\n      max_output_length: 100\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Features:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Chat template automatically applied</li>\n<li>Same streaming mechanism as text generation</li>\n<li>Per-chunk processing with <code>${result[]}</code></li>\n</ul>\n<h3>13.2.2 HTTP Components</h3>\n<h4>HTTP Client Streaming</h4>\n<p><strong>OpenAI API Streaming:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">component:\n  type: http-client\n  base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n  action:\n    path: /chat/completions\n    method: POST\n    headers:\n      Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n    body:\n      model: gpt-4o\n      messages:\n        - role: user\n          content: ${input.prompt as text}\n      stream: true                   # API parameter\n    stream_format: json              # Parse chunks as JSON\n    output: ${response[].choices[0].delta.content}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>stream_format Options:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>\n<p><code>json</code>: Parse each chunk as JSON</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">stream_format: json\noutput: ${response[].choices[0].delta.content}\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><code>text</code>: Decode each chunk as UTF-8 text</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">stream_format: text\noutput: ${response[]}\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Not specified: Pass raw bytes</p>\n</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Output References:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Streaming: <code>${response[]}</code> (per chunk)</li>\n<li>Non-streaming: <code>${response}</code> (after full completion)</li>\n</ul>\n<h4>HTTP Server (Managed Service) Streaming</h4>\n<p><strong>vLLM Server Streaming:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">component:\n  type: http-server\n  start:\n    - vllm\n    - serve\n    - Qwen/Qwen2-7B-Instruct\n    - --port\n    - &quot;8000&quot;\n  port: 8000\n  healthcheck:\n    path: /health\n  action:\n    method: POST\n    path: /v1/chat/completions\n    body:\n      model: qwen2-7b-instruct\n      messages:\n        - role: user\n          content: ${input.prompt as text}\n      stream: true\n    stream_format: json\n    output: ${response[].choices[0].delta.content}\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>13.3 Using Streaming in Workflows</h2>\n<h3>13.3.1 Basic Streaming Workflow</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n\nworkflow:\n  title: Streaming Chat\n  output: ${output as sse-text}    # Output as SSE text format\n\ncomponent:\n  type: http-client\n  base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n  action:\n    path: /chat/completions\n    method: POST\n    headers:\n      Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n    body:\n      model: gpt-4o\n      messages:\n        - role: user\n          content: ${input.prompt as text}\n      stream: true\n    stream_format: json\n    output: ${response[].choices[0].delta.content}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Workflow Output Formats:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>\n<p><code>as sse-text</code>: SSE text stream</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">output: ${output as sse-text}\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p><code>as sse-json</code>: SSE JSON stream</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">output: ${output as sse-json}\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>13.3.2 Multi-Step Workflow Streaming</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: translate-and-summarize\n    title: Translate and Summarize\n    output: ${output as sse-text}\n    jobs:\n      - id: translate\n        component: translator\n        input:\n          text: ${input.text}\n          target_lang: en\n        # Translation without streaming (waits for full completion)\n\n      - id: summarize\n        component: summarizer\n        input:\n          text: ${jobs.translate.output}\n        # Summary with streaming output\n        depends_on: [translate]\n\ncomponents:\n  - id: translator\n    type: model\n    task: translation\n    model: Helsinki-NLP/opus-mt-ko-en\n    streaming: false\n    action:\n      text: ${input.text as text}\n\n  - id: summarizer\n    type: model\n    task: text-generation\n    model: facebook/bart-large-cnn\n    streaming: true                    # Only last job streams\n    action:\n      text: ${input.text as text}\n      params:\n        max_output_length: 150\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Important:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Only the <strong>last job</strong> in a workflow can stream</li>\n<li>Intermediate jobs must wait for completion</li>\n<li>Only final output streams with <code>${result[]}</code></li>\n</ul>\n<h3>13.3.3 Conditional Streaming</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflow:\n  title: Conditional Streaming\n  output: ${output as sse-text}\n\ncomponent:\n  type: model\n  task: text-generation\n  model: gpt2\n  streaming: ${input.stream | false}   # Streaming determined by input\n  action:\n    text: ${input.prompt as text}\n    params:\n      max_output_length: 100\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>API Call Examples:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\"># Enable streaming\ncurl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/workflows/runs \\\n  -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; \\\n  -d '{\n    &quot;input&quot;: {&quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Hello&quot;, &quot;stream&quot;: true},\n    &quot;output_only&quot;: true,\n    &quot;wait_for_completion&quot;: true\n  }'\n\n# Disable streaming\ncurl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/workflows/runs \\\n  -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; \\\n  -d '{\n    &quot;input&quot;: {&quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Hello&quot;, &quot;stream&quot;: false},\n    &quot;wait_for_completion&quot;: true\n  }'\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>13.4 Processing Streaming Responses</h2>\n<h3>13.4.1 API Endpoints</h3>\n<p><strong>Streaming Request Requirements:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/workflows/runs \\\n  -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; \\\n  -d '{\n    &quot;input&quot;: {&quot;prompt&quot;: &quot;Write a story&quot;},\n    &quot;output_only&quot;: true,              # Required: return output only\n    &quot;wait_for_completion&quot;: true       # Required: wait until completion\n  }'\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Response Headers:</strong></p>\n<pre><code>Content-Type: text/event-stream\nCache-Control: no-cache\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Response Body (SSE):</strong></p>\n<pre><code>data: Once\n\ndata:  upon\n\ndata:  a\n\ndata:  time\n\n</code></pre>\n<h3>13.4.2 Client Implementation (JavaScript)</h3>\n<p><strong>Using EventSource API:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">const eventSource = new EventSource(\n  'http://localhost:8080/api/workflows/runs',\n  {\n    method: 'POST',\n    headers: {\n      'Content-Type': 'application/json'\n    },\n    body: JSON.stringify({\n      input: { prompt: 'Hello' },\n      output_only: true,\n      wait_for_completion: true\n    })\n  }\n);\n\neventSource.onmessage = (event) =&gt; {\n  const chunk = event.data;\n  console.log('Received:', chunk);\n  // Update UI\n  document.getElementById('output').textContent += chunk;\n};\n\neventSource.onerror = (error) =&gt; {\n  console.error('Error:', error);\n  eventSource.close();\n};\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Using Fetch API:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">const response = await fetch('http://localhost:8080/api/workflows/runs', {\n  method: 'POST',\n  headers: {\n    'Content-Type': 'application/json'\n  },\n  body: JSON.stringify({\n    input: { prompt: 'Hello' },\n    output_only: true,\n    wait_for_completion: true\n  })\n});\n\nconst reader = response.body.getReader();\nconst decoder = new TextDecoder();\n\nwhile (true) {\n  const { done, value } = await reader.read();\n  if (done) break;\n\n  const chunk = decoder.decode(value);\n  const lines = chunk.split('\\n');\n\n  for (const line of lines) {\n    if (line.startsWith('data: ')) {\n      const content = line.substring(6);\n      console.log('Chunk:', content);\n      // Update UI\n      document.getElementById('output').textContent += content;\n    }\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>13.4.3 Client Implementation (Python)</h3>\n<p><strong>Using requests library:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-python\">import requests\nimport json\n\nurl = 'http://localhost:8080/api/workflows/runs'\npayload = {\n    'input': {'prompt': 'Hello'},\n    'output_only': True,\n    'wait_for_completion': True\n}\n\nresponse = requests.post(url, json=payload, stream=True)\n\nfor line in response.iter_lines():\n    if line:\n        line = line.decode('utf-8')\n        if line.startswith('data: '):\n            chunk = line[6:]\n            print(chunk, end='', flush=True)\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Using aiohttp library (async):</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-python\">import aiohttp\nimport asyncio\n\nasync def stream_workflow():\n    url = 'http://localhost:8080/api/workflows/runs'\n    payload = {\n        'input': {'prompt': 'Hello'},\n        'output_only': True,\n        'wait_for_completion': True\n    }\n\n    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:\n        async with session.post(url, json=payload) as response:\n            async for line in response.content:\n                line = line.decode('utf-8').strip()\n                if line.startswith('data: '):\n                    chunk = line[6:]\n                    print(chunk, end='', flush=True)\n\nasyncio.run(stream_workflow())\n</code></pre>\n<h3>13.4.4 Web UI Integration</h3>\n<p><strong>Gradio Auto-Streaming:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  webui:\n    driver: gradio\n    port: 8081\n\nworkflow:\n  title: Streaming Chat\n  output: ${output as sse-text}\n\ncomponent:\n  type: model\n  task: chat-completion\n  model: gpt2\n  streaming: true\n  action:\n    messages:\n      - role: user\n        content: ${input.prompt as text}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Gradio Web UI automatically:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Detects <code>sse-text</code> format</li>\n<li>Displays real-time text accumulation</li>\n<li>Shows typing animation effect</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>13.5 Performance and Optimization</h2>\n<h3>13.5.1 Model Streaming Optimization</h3>\n<p><strong>Settings for Fast Token Generation:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">component:\n  type: model\n  task: text-generation\n  model: gpt2\n  streaming: true\n  action:\n    text: ${input.prompt as text}\n    params:\n      # Performance optimization\n      do_sample: false               # Deterministic generation (no beam search)\n      num_beams: 1                   # Single beam\n      max_output_length: 100         # Appropriate length limit\n\n      # Quality vs Speed balance\n      # top_p: 0.9                   # Use with sampling\n      # temperature: 0.8             # Use with sampling\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Impact by Setting:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Parameter</th>\n<th>Value</th>\n<th>Effect</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>do_sample</code></td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n<td>Fastest, deterministic</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>do_sample</code></td>\n<td><code>true</code></td>\n<td>Slower, diverse outputs</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>num_beams</code></td>\n<td><code>1</code></td>\n<td>Fast</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>num_beams</code></td>\n<td><code>&gt;1</code></td>\n<td>Slower, better quality</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_output_length</code></td>\n<td>Small</td>\n<td>Quick completion</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>max_output_length</code></td>\n<td>Large</td>\n<td>Longer wait time</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>13.5.2 HTTP Streaming Optimization</h3>\n<p><strong>Chunk Size Adjustment:</strong></p>\n<p>Default chunk size is 65536 bytes. Can be adjusted with aiohttp settings:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-python\"># Custom HTTP client settings (code level)\nimport aiohttp\n\nasync with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:\n    async with session.get(url, chunk_size=8192) as response:\n        async for chunk in response.content.iter_chunked(8192):\n            # Process\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Timeout Settings:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">component:\n  type: http-client\n  base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n  timeout: 60                      # 60 second timeout\n  action:\n    path: /chat/completions\n    body:\n      stream: true\n    stream_format: json\n</code></pre>\n<h3>13.5.3 Memory Management</h3>\n<p><strong>Memory Usage During Streaming:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Model streaming: Thread-based, uses queues (minimal memory)</li>\n<li>HTTP streaming: Chunk-based processing (no full response buffering)</li>\n<li>Workflow: Per-chunk rendering (no accumulation)</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Recommendations:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>GPU memory: Determined by model size</li>\n<li>CPU memory: Only chunk size needed during streaming</li>\n<li>Long responses are memory efficient</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>13.5.4 Network Optimization</h3>\n<p><strong>Minimize Latency:</strong></p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Server Location</strong>: Close to users</li>\n<li><strong>Use HTTP/2</strong>: Keep-alive connections</li>\n<li><strong>CDN</strong>: Cache static assets</li>\n<li><strong>Compression</strong>: gzip compression (SSE is automatic)</li>\n</ol>\n<p><strong>Bandwidth Optimization:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>\n<p>Extract only necessary fields</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">output: ${response[].choices[0].delta.content}\n# Only content, not full response\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Minimize JSON format</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">stream_format: text              # Lighter than JSON\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>13.5.5 Error Handling</h3>\n<p><strong>Retry Logic:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">component:\n  type: http-client\n  base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n  max_retries: 3                   # Max 3 retries\n  retry_delay: 1                   # 1 second wait\n  action:\n    path: /chat/completions\n    body:\n      stream: true\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Timeout Handling:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">component:\n  type: http-client\n  base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n  timeout: 30                      # 30 second timeout\n  action:\n    path: /chat/completions\n    body:\n      stream: true\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Stream Interruption Handling:</strong></p>\n<p>On client side:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-javascript\">const controller = new AbortController();\n\n// Auto-abort after 5 seconds\nsetTimeout(() =&gt; controller.abort(), 5000);\n\nfetch(url, {\n  signal: controller.signal,\n  // ...\n});\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>13.6 Real-World Examples</h2>\n<h3>13.6.1 Real-time Translation Streaming</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n  webui:\n    driver: gradio\n    port: 8081\n\nworkflow:\n  title: Real-time Translation\n  output: ${output as sse-text}\n\ncomponent:\n  type: model\n  task: translation\n  model: Helsinki-NLP/opus-mt-ko-en\n  streaming: true\n  action:\n    text: ${input.text as text}\n    params:\n      max_output_length: 512\n</code></pre>\n<h3>13.6.2 OpenAI + Claude Combination</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflows:\n  - id: multi-model-chat\n    title: Multi-Model Chat\n    output: ${output as sse-text}\n    jobs:\n      - id: openai-response\n        component: openai-client\n        input:\n          prompt: ${input.prompt}\n        condition: ${input.model == 'openai'}\n\n      - id: claude-response\n        component: claude-client\n        input:\n          prompt: ${input.prompt}\n        condition: ${input.model == 'claude'}\n\ncomponents:\n  - id: openai-client\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1\n    action:\n      path: /chat/completions\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}\n      body:\n        model: gpt-4o\n        messages:\n          - role: user\n            content: ${input.prompt as text}\n        stream: true\n      stream_format: json\n      output: ${response[].choices[0].delta.content}\n\n  - id: claude-client\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.anthropic.com/v1\n    action:\n      path: /messages\n      headers:\n        x-api-key: ${env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}\n        anthropic-version: &quot;2023-06-01&quot;\n      body:\n        model: claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022\n        messages:\n          - role: user\n            content: ${input.prompt as text}\n        stream: true\n      stream_format: json\n      output: ${response[].delta.text}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>13.6.3 Local Model Streaming Server</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">controller:\n  type: http-server\n  port: 8080\n\nworkflow:\n  title: Local Model Streaming\n  output: ${output as sse-text}\n\ncomponent:\n  type: http-server\n  start:\n    - vllm\n    - serve\n    - meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-chat-hf\n    - --port\n    - &quot;8000&quot;\n    - --gpu-memory-utilization\n    - &quot;0.9&quot;\n  port: 8000\n  healthcheck:\n    path: /health\n    interval: 5s\n  action:\n    method: POST\n    path: /v1/chat/completions\n    body:\n      model: llama-2-7b-chat\n      messages:\n        - role: user\n          content: ${input.prompt as text}\n      stream: true\n      max_tokens: 256\n    stream_format: json\n    output: ${response[].choices[0].delta.content}\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>13.7 Distributed Streaming (Queue Streaming)</h2>\n<p>Streaming also works in distributed deployments where workflow execution is delegated to remote workers via Redis queue dispatch.</p>\n<p>When a worker executes a streaming workflow, chunks are written to a Redis Stream (<code>XADD</code>), and the dispatcher reads them (<code>XREAD</code>) and delivers them to the client as SSE — just like local streaming. No additional configuration is required.</p>\n<pre><code>Client ← SSE ← [Dispatcher] ← XREAD ← Redis Stream ← XADD ← [Worker] ← LLM streaming\n</code></pre>\n<p>For full details on queue streaming configuration, architecture, and edge cases, see <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/07-controller-configuration#75-queue-streaming\">Section 7.5: Queue Streaming</a>.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>13.8 Streaming Best Practices</h2>\n<h3>Streaming Usage Recommendations</h3>\n<p><strong>When Should You Use Streaming?</strong></p>\n<p>✅ <strong>Recommended:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Long responses (100+ tokens)</li>\n<li>Real-time user experience needed</li>\n<li>Chatbot and conversation systems</li>\n<li>Progressive result display</li>\n</ul>\n<p>❌ <strong>Not Recommended:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Short responses (&lt; 50 tokens)</li>\n<li>Batch processing</li>\n<li>Background tasks</li>\n<li>Complete response needed (analysis, storage, etc.)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Performance Optimization Checklist</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> Set <code>num_beams: 1</code> (model streaming)</li>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> Set <code>do_sample: false</code> (fast generation)</li>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> Set appropriate <code>max_output_length</code></li>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> Configure timeout</li>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> Implement error handling</li>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> Client-side abort logic</li>\n<li><input disabled=\"\" type=\"checkbox\"> Use GPU (when available)</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Security Considerations</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Manage API keys via environment variables</li>\n<li>Use HTTPS (production)</li>\n<li>Set rate limiting</li>\n<li>Input validation</li>\n<li>Output filtering (harmful content)</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>Next Steps</h2>\n<p>Practice:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Test local model streaming</li>\n<li>Integrate external API streaming</li>\n<li>Check real-time responses in Web UI</li>\n<li>Experiment with various output formats</li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<p><strong>Next Chapter</strong>: <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/14-variable-binding\">14. Variable Binding</a></p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "13. Streaming Mode"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "user-guide/14-variable-binding",
      "html": "<h1>14. Variable Binding</h1>\n<p>This chapter provides a detailed explanation of model-compose's variable binding syntax. Variable binding is a core feature that uses the <code>${...}</code> syntax to reference and transform data.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>14.1 Syntax Overview</h2>\n<p>Variable binding specifies a <strong>data source</strong> (<code>key.path</code>), and optionally adds <strong>type conversion</strong> (<code>as type/subtype[attrs];format</code>), <strong>default value</strong> (<code>| default</code>), and <strong>metadata</strong> (<code>@(annotation)</code>).</p>\n<p><strong>Full Syntax</strong>:</p>\n<pre><code>${key.path as type/subtype[attrs];format | default @(annotation)}\n</code></pre>\n<p>All elements except the data source (<code>key.path</code>) are optional.</p>\n<p><strong>Progressive Examples</strong>:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${input.name}                              # Data source only\n${input.avatar as image/png}               # With type and subtype\n${input.photo as image;base64}             # With format\n${input.count | 0}                         # With default value\n${input.email @(description &quot;Email&quot;)}      # With metadata\n${input.profile as image/jpeg;url | ${env.DEFAULT_AVATAR} @(description &quot;Profile Picture&quot;)}  # All combined\n</code></pre>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Element</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n<th>Examples</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>key</strong></td>\n<td>Data source</td>\n<td><code>input</code>, <code>response</code>, <code>result</code>, <code>env</code>, <code>jobs</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>path</strong></td>\n<td>Nested field access with dot notation and array indexing</td>\n<td><code>.user.name</code>, <code>.data[0].id</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>type</strong></td>\n<td>Data type (<a href=\"#144-type-conversion\">14.4</a>)</td>\n<td><code>image</code>, <code>audio</code>, <code>text</code>, <code>json</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>subtype</strong></td>\n<td>Detailed format of the type</td>\n<td><code>jpeg</code>, <code>png</code>, <code>mp3</code>, <code>pcm</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>attrs</strong></td>\n<td>Additional parameters in brackets</td>\n<td><code>sample_rate=24000,channels=1</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>format</strong></td>\n<td>Encoding state of the data (<a href=\"#145-format-and-context-semantics\">14.5</a>)</td>\n<td><code>base64</code>, <code>url</code>, <code>path</code>, <code>sse-json</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>default</strong></td>\n<td>Fallback value when value is missing (<a href=\"#146-default-values\">14.6</a>)</td>\n<td><code>0</code>, <code>&quot;gpt-4o&quot;</code>, <code>${env.FALLBACK}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>annotation</strong></td>\n<td>Metadata for MCP/UI (<a href=\"#147-metadata-and-ui-hints\">14.7</a>)</td>\n<td><code>@(description &quot;Username&quot;)</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>14.2 Variable Sources</h2>\n<h3>14.2.1 Workflow Input</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${input}                    # Entire input object\n${input.field}              # field property of input\n${input.user.email}         # Nested path\n</code></pre>\n<h3>14.2.2 Component Response Variables</h3>\n<p>Different component types use different variable names to reference response data.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Component Type</th>\n<th>Variable Source</th>\n<th>Streaming Variable</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>http-client</code></td>\n<td><code>${response}</code></td>\n<td><code>${response[]}</code></td>\n<td>HTTP response data</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>http-server</code></td>\n<td><code>${response}</code></td>\n<td><code>${response[]}</code></td>\n<td>Managed HTTP server response</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>websocket-client</code></td>\n<td><code>${response}</code></td>\n<td><code>${response[]}</code></td>\n<td>WebSocket received data</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>websocket-server</code></td>\n<td><code>${response}</code></td>\n<td><code>${response[]}</code></td>\n<td>Managed WebSocket server data</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mcp-client</code></td>\n<td><code>${response}</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>MCP response data</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>mcp-server</code></td>\n<td><code>${response}</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Managed MCP server response</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>model</code></td>\n<td><code>${result}</code></td>\n<td><code>${result[]}</code></td>\n<td>Model inference result</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>model-trainer</code></td>\n<td><code>${result}</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Training result metrics</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>vector-store</code></td>\n<td><code>${response}</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Vector search/insert result</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>datasets</code></td>\n<td><code>${result}</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Dataset samples</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>text-splitter</code></td>\n<td><code>${result}</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Split text chunks</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>image-processor</code></td>\n<td><code>${result}</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Processed image</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>workflow</code></td>\n<td><code>${output}</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Sub-workflow output</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>shell</code></td>\n<td><code>${stdout}</code>, <code>${stderr}</code></td>\n<td>-</td>\n<td>Command execution result</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>Key Rules</strong>:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>HTTP-based components (<code>http-client</code>, <code>http-server</code>, <code>vector-store</code>, <code>mcp-client</code>) → <code>${response}</code></li>\n<li>Local execution components (<code>model</code>, <code>datasets</code>, <code>text-splitter</code>, <code>image-processor</code>) → <code>${result}</code></li>\n<li>Shell commands → <code>${stdout}</code> or <code>${stderr}</code></li>\n<li>Workflow invocation → <code>${output}</code></li>\n</ul>\n<h3>14.2.3 Previous Job Outputs</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${jobs.job-id.output}           # Specific job output\n${jobs.job-id.output.field}     # Specific field of job output\n</code></pre>\n<h3>14.2.4 Environment Variables</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}       # Environment variable\n${env.PORT | 8080}          # With default value\n</code></pre>\n<h3>14.2.5 Streaming Chunk References</h3>\n<p>Append <code>[]</code> to the variable name to receive data as a stream of chunks instead of a single value.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${response[]}               # HTTP streaming chunks\n${result[]}                 # Model streaming chunks\n</code></pre>\n<p>Components that support streaming:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>http-client</code> / <code>http-server</code> → <code>${response[]}</code></li>\n<li><code>websocket-client</code> / <code>websocket-server</code> → <code>${response[]}</code></li>\n<li><code>model</code> (with streaming: true) → <code>${result[]}</code></li>\n</ul>\n<hr />\n<h2>14.3 Path Access</h2>\n<p>Variable paths support dot notation for nested objects and bracket notation for array indexing.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${response.choices[0].message.content}     # Nested object + array index\n${response.data[-1].id}                    # Negative index (last element)\n${input.users[0].name}                     # First element's name field\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>14.4 Type Conversion</h2>\n<p>Type conversion transforms variable values into specific data types using the <code>as</code> keyword.</p>\n<h3>14.4.1 Primitive Types</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n<th>Example</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>text</code></td>\n<td>Convert to string</td>\n<td><code>${input.message as text}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>number</code></td>\n<td>Convert to float</td>\n<td><code>${input.price as number}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>integer</code></td>\n<td>Convert to integer</td>\n<td><code>${input.count as integer}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>boolean</code></td>\n<td>Convert to boolean (<code>&quot;true&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;1&quot;</code> → true)</td>\n<td><code>${input.enabled as boolean}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>json</code></td>\n<td>Parse JSON string to object</td>\n<td><code>${input.data as json}</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>14.4.2 Object Array Projection</h3>\n<p>Extract specific fields from an array of objects using <code>subtype</code> as comma-separated field paths.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># Extract specific fields from object array\n${response.users as object[]/id,name}\n# Result: [{&quot;id&quot;: 1, &quot;name&quot;: &quot;John&quot;}, {&quot;id&quot;: 2, &quot;name&quot;: &quot;Jane&quot;}]\n\n# Nested path support (last segment becomes the key name)\n${response.data as object[]/user.id,user.email,status}\n# Result: [{&quot;id&quot;: 1, &quot;email&quot;: &quot;john@example.com&quot;, &quot;status&quot;: &quot;active&quot;}, ...]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>14.4.3 Media Types</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Subtype</th>\n<th>Format</th>\n<th>Example</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>image</code></td>\n<td><code>png</code>, <code>jpg</code>, <code>webp</code></td>\n<td><code>base64</code>, <code>url</code>, <code>path</code></td>\n<td><code>${input.photo as image/jpg}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>audio</code></td>\n<td><code>mp3</code>, <code>wav</code>, <code>ogg</code>, <code>pcm</code></td>\n<td><code>base64</code>, <code>url</code>, <code>path</code></td>\n<td><code>${output as audio/mp3;base64}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>video</code></td>\n<td><code>mp4</code>, <code>webm</code></td>\n<td><code>base64</code>, <code>url</code>, <code>path</code></td>\n<td><code>${result as video/mp4}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>file</code></td>\n<td>any</td>\n<td><code>base64</code>, <code>url</code>, <code>path</code></td>\n<td><code>${input.document as file}</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>14.4.4 Attributes</h3>\n<p>Attributes provide additional key-value parameters using bracket syntax: <code>type/subtype[key=value,...]</code>. They are passed as a dictionary alongside type and subtype, allowing extra context for type conversion and downstream processing.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># PCM audio with encoding parameters\n${response[] as audio/pcm[sample_rate=24000,channels=1,bit_depth=16]}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>14.4.5 Base64 Type vs Base64 Format</h3>\n<p>These are different concepts:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong><code>base64</code> type</strong> (<code>${value as base64}</code>) — <strong>Encodes</strong> the value to a base64 string. Always performed regardless of context.</li>\n<li><strong><code>base64</code> format</strong> (<code>${value as image;base64}</code>) — Indicates the value <strong>is already</strong> base64 encoded. In input context, the system decodes it; in output context, it is preserved as metadata.</li>\n</ul>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># Encode binary data TO base64 (type)\n${output as base64}\n\n# Tell the system this data IS base64-encoded (format) — decoded in input context\n${input.photo as image;base64}\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>14.5 Format and Context Semantics</h2>\n<p>Format specifiers describe the <strong>encoding state</strong> of the data. The same <code>as type;format</code> syntax behaves differently depending on where it is used.</p>\n<h3>14.5.1 Format Values</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Format</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n<th>Example</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>base64</code></td>\n<td>Data is base64 encoded</td>\n<td><code>${input.photo as image;base64}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>url</code></td>\n<td>Data is a URL to be fetched</td>\n<td><code>${input.avatar as image;url}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>path</code></td>\n<td>Data is a file path</td>\n<td><code>${output.path as audio;path}</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>stream</code></td>\n<td>Data is a stream</td>\n<td><code>${output as audio;stream}</code></td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Note:</strong> <code>sse-text</code> and <code>sse-json</code> are <strong>types</strong>, not formats. Use <code>${output as sse-text}</code> or <code>${output as sse-json}</code> to convert a value to an SSE stream.</p>\n</blockquote>\n<h3>14.5.2 Input Context</h3>\n<p>In component action <code>input</code>, format tells the system <strong>how the incoming data is currently encoded</strong>. The system converts it to the form the component expects.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Format</th>\n<th>Input Value</th>\n<th>What Happens</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>image</code></td>\n<td><code>base64</code></td>\n<td>base64 string</td>\n<td>Decoded and saved as a temporary file</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>image</code></td>\n<td><code>url</code></td>\n<td>URL string</td>\n<td>Downloaded and saved as a temporary file</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>image</code></td>\n<td><code>path</code></td>\n<td>file path</td>\n<td>Used directly as a file reference</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>image</code></td>\n<td>(none)</td>\n<td>bytes / stream</td>\n<td>Saved as a temporary file</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>audio</code></td>\n<td><code>base64</code></td>\n<td>base64 string</td>\n<td>Decoded and saved as a temporary file</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>audio</code></td>\n<td><code>url</code></td>\n<td>URL string</td>\n<td>Downloaded and saved as a temporary file</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># &quot;the data is a base64-encoded image&quot; → system decodes it to a file\ninput:\n  image: ${input.photo as image;base64}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>14.5.3 Component/Job Output Context</h3>\n<p>In component/job action <code>output</code>, media file conversion is <strong>not performed</strong>. The value is passed through with only basic type conversion (e.g., <code>integer</code>, <code>json</code>, <code>base64</code> encoding). The format is preserved as metadata for downstream consumers.</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Format</th>\n<th>What Happens</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>image</code></td>\n<td><code>base64</code></td>\n<td>Value passed through as-is (no decoding)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>audio</code></td>\n<td><code>path</code></td>\n<td>File object rendered to its file path</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>sse-text</code></td>\n<td>(none)</td>\n<td>Wraps value as SSE text stream</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>sse-json</code></td>\n<td>(none)</td>\n<td>Wraps value as SSE JSON stream</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>base64</code></td>\n<td>(any)</td>\n<td>Value encoded to base64 string (always performed)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># &quot;tell consumers this is a base64-encoded image&quot;\noutput: ${result as image;base64}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>14.5.4 Workflow Output Context</h3>\n<p>Workflow output variables define <code>type</code> and <code>format</code> in the workflow schema. These are consumed by <strong>controller adapters</strong> to determine how to display and transmit the data:</p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Consumer</th>\n<th>Format</th>\n<th>Behavior</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Web UI</strong></td>\n<td><code>sse-text</code></td>\n<td>Accumulate text chunks incrementally</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Web UI</strong></td>\n<td><code>sse-json</code></td>\n<td>Parse each chunk as JSON, extract field via <code>subtype</code> path</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Web UI</strong></td>\n<td><code>base64</code></td>\n<td>Decode base64 to display image/audio</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Web UI</strong></td>\n<td><code>url</code></td>\n<td>Fetch URL to display image/audio</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Web UI</strong></td>\n<td><code>path</code></td>\n<td>Use file path directly</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>HTTP API</strong></td>\n<td>(any)</td>\n<td>Format is not used; transmission is determined by the output data type</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\"># Web UI accumulates text chunks; HTTP API sends as SSE\nworkflow:\n  output: ${output as sse-text}\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>14.6 Default Values</h2>\n<p>Default values provide fallback data when a variable is missing or null. Using the pipe (<code>|</code>) operator, you can specify literal values or reference environment variables.</p>\n<h3>14.6.1 Literal Default Values</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${input.temperature | 0.7}             # Number\n${input.model | &quot;gpt-4o&quot;}              # String\n${input.enabled | true}                # Boolean\n</code></pre>\n<h3>14.6.2 Environment Variable Default Values</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${input.channel | ${env.DEFAULT_CHANNEL}}     # Use environment variable as default\n${input.api_key | ${env.API_KEY}}             # Use environment variable as default\n</code></pre>\n<h3>14.6.3 Nested Default Values (Environment Variable + Literal)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${input.api_key | ${env.API_KEY | &quot;default-key&quot;}}\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>14.7 Metadata and UI Hints</h2>\n<h3>14.7.1 Annotations</h3>\n<p>Used to provide parameter descriptions for MCP servers.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${input.channel @(description Slack channel ID)}\n${input.limit as integer | 10 @(description Maximum number of results)}\n</code></pre>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">input:\n  prompt: ${input.prompt as text @(description The text prompt for generation)}\n  temperature: ${input.temperature as number | 0.7 @(description Controls randomness (0-2))}\n  max_tokens: ${input.max_tokens as integer | 100 @(description Maximum tokens to generate)}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>14.7.2 Select (Dropdown)</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${input.voice as select/alloy,echo,fable,onyx,nova,shimmer}\n${input.model as select/gpt-4o,gpt-4o-mini,o1-mini}\n${input.size as select/256x256,512x512,1024x1024 | 1024x1024}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>14.7.3 Slider</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${input.temperature as slider/0,2,0.1 | 0.7}\n# Format: slider/min,max,step | default\n</code></pre>\n<h3>14.7.4 Textarea</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">${input.prompt as text}\n# Web UI renders text type as a textarea widget\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>14.8 Practical Examples</h2>\n<h3>14.8.1 OpenAI API Call</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">body:\n  model: ${input.model as select/gpt-4o,gpt-4o-mini,o1-mini | gpt-4o}\n  messages:\n    - role: user\n      content: ${input.prompt as text}\n  temperature: ${input.temperature as slider/0,2,0.1 | 0.7}\n  max_tokens: ${input.max_tokens as integer | 1000}\noutput:\n  message: ${response.choices[0].message.content}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>14.8.2 Image Processing Pipeline</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">jobs:\n  - id: analyze\n    component: vision-model\n    input:\n      image: ${input.image as image/jpg}\n    output: ${output}\n\n  - id: enhance\n    component: image-editor\n    input:\n      image: ${input.image as image/jpg}\n      prompt: ${jobs.analyze.output.description}\n    output: ${output as image/png;base64}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>14.8.3 Streaming Response</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">workflow:\n  output: ${output as sse-text}\n\ncomponent:\n  type: http-client\n  action:\n    body:\n      stream: true\n    stream_format: json\n    output: ${response[].choices[0].delta.content}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>14.8.4 Vector Search Result Format</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">component:\n  type: vector-store\n  action: search\n  output: ${response as object[]/id,score,metadata.text}\n# Result: [{&quot;id&quot;: &quot;1&quot;, &quot;score&quot;: 0.95, &quot;text&quot;: &quot;...&quot;}, ...]\n</code></pre>\n<h3>14.8.5 Conditional Default Values</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">component:\n  type: http-client\n  action:\n    headers:\n      Authorization: Bearer ${input.api_key | ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}}\n    body:\n      model: ${input.model | ${env.DEFAULT_MODEL | &quot;gpt-4o&quot;}}\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<p><strong>Next Chapter</strong>: <a href=\"/model-compose/user-guide/15-system-integration\">15. System Integration</a></p>\n",
      "data": {
        "title": "14. Variable Binding"
      }
    },
    {
      "slug": "user-guide/15-system-integration",
      "html": "<h1>15. System Integration</h1>\n<p>This chapter covers listeners and gateways for integrating with external systems.</p>\n<hr />\n<h2>15.1 Listener Overview</h2>\n<p>Listeners are HTTP servers for communicating with external systems. There are two types:</p>\n<h3>Listener Types</h3>\n<p><strong>1. HTTP Callback (http-callback)</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Receives <strong>asynchronous callbacks</strong> from external services and delivers results to <strong>waiting workflows</strong></li>\n<li>Use cases: Async API integration (image generation, video processing, payment processing, etc.)</li>\n<li>Behavior: Workflow pauses while waiting for callback</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>2. HTTP Trigger (http-trigger)</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Receives HTTP requests from external sources and <strong>immediately starts workflows</strong></li>\n<li>Use cases: Webhook reception, REST API endpoint provision</li>\n<li>Behavior: Each request starts a new workflow instance</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Comparison</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Feature</th>\n<th>HTTP Callback</th>\n<th>HTTP Trigger</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Purpose</strong></td>\n<td>Receive async task results</td>\n<td>Start workflows</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Workflow</strong></td>\n<td>Already running (waiting state)</td>\n<td>Newly started</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Response</strong></td>\n<td>Delivered to waiting workflow</td>\n<td>Immediately start workflow</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Examples</strong></td>\n<td>External API callbacks, payment completion</td>\n<td>Webhook reception, REST API</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>Identifier</strong></td>\n<td>Match waiting workflow via <code>identify_by</code></td>\n<td>Always start new workflow</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<hr />\n<h2>15.2 HTTP Callback Listener</h2>\n<p>HTTP Callback listeners receive asynchronous callbacks from external services. Useful when integrating with services that send results to a callback URL after task completion.</p>\n<h3>15.2.1 HTTP Callback Overview</h3>\n<p>Many external services don't return results immediately, but queue tasks and send results to a callback URL later:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Client sends task request to external service (including callback URL)</li>\n<li>External service returns task ID immediately</li>\n<li>External service processes task in background</li>\n<li>After completion, sends results to callback URL</li>\n<li>Listener receives callback and delivers results to waiting workflow</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>15.2.2 Basic HTTP Callback Configuration</h3>\n<p><strong>Simple callback listener:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-callback\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8090\n  path: /callback\n  method: POST\n</code></pre>\n<p>This creates an endpoint at <code>http://0.0.0.0:8090/callback</code> that accepts POST requests.</p>\n<h3>15.2.3 Callback Endpoint Configuration</h3>\n<p><strong>Single callback endpoint:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-callback\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8090\n  path: /webhook/completed           # Callback path\n  method: POST                        # HTTP method\n  identify_by: ${body.task_id}       # Task identifier\n  status: ${body.status}              # Status field\n  success_when:                       # Success status values\n    - &quot;completed&quot;\n    - &quot;success&quot;\n  fail_when:                          # Failure status values\n    - &quot;failed&quot;\n    - &quot;error&quot;\n  result: ${body.result}              # Result extraction path\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Multiple callback endpoints:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-callback\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8090\n  base_path: /webhooks                # Common base path\n  callbacks:\n    # Image generation completion callback\n    - path: /image/completed\n      method: POST\n      identify_by: ${body.request_id}\n      status: ${body.status}\n      success_when: [&quot;completed&quot;]\n      fail_when: [&quot;failed&quot;]\n      result: ${body.image_url}\n\n    # Video processing completion callback\n    - path: /video/completed\n      method: POST\n      identify_by: ${body.task_id}\n      status: ${body.state}\n      success_when: [&quot;done&quot;]\n      fail_when: [&quot;error&quot;, &quot;timeout&quot;]\n      result: ${body.output}\n\n    # General task completion callback\n    - path: /task/callback\n      method: POST\n      identify_by: ${body.id}\n      result: ${body.data}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>15.2.4 Callback Field Descriptions</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n<th>Required</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>path</code></td>\n<td>Callback endpoint path</td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>-</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>method</code></td>\n<td>HTTP method</td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td><code>POST</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>identify_by</code></td>\n<td>Task identification field path</td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td><code>__callback__</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>status</code></td>\n<td>Status check field path</td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>-</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>success_when</code></td>\n<td>Success status value list</td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>-</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>fail_when</code></td>\n<td>Failure status value list</td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>-</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>result</code></td>\n<td>Result extraction field path</td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Entire body</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>bulk</code></td>\n<td>Handle multiple items in single request</td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>item</code></td>\n<td>Item extraction path in bulk mode</td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>-</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>15.2.5 Bulk Callback Processing</h3>\n<p>When receiving results for multiple tasks in a single callback request:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-callback\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8090\n  path: /batch/completed\n  method: POST\n  bulk: true                          # Enable bulk mode\n  item: ${body.results}               # Results array path\n  identify_by: ${item.task_id}        # Identifier for each item\n  status: ${item.status}\n  success_when: [&quot;completed&quot;]\n  result: ${item.data}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Callback request example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;results&quot;: [\n    {\n      &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;task-1&quot;,\n      &quot;status&quot;: &quot;completed&quot;,\n      &quot;data&quot;: {&quot;url&quot;: &quot;https://example.com/result1.png&quot;}\n    },\n    {\n      &quot;task_id&quot;: &quot;task-2&quot;,\n      &quot;status&quot;: &quot;completed&quot;,\n      &quot;data&quot;: {&quot;url&quot;: &quot;https://example.com/result2.png&quot;}\n    }\n  ]\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>15.2.6 Advanced HTTP Callback Configuration</h3>\n<p><strong>Concurrency control:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-callback\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8090\n  max_concurrent_count: 10            # Maximum concurrent callback processing\n  path: /callback\n  method: POST\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Runtime configuration:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-callback\n  runtime: native                     # or docker\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8090\n  path: /callback\n</code></pre>\n<h3>15.2.7 How HTTP Callback Works</h3>\n<p>Listeners receive callbacks from external services and deliver results to waiting workflows.</p>\n<p><strong>Basic structure:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-callback\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8090\n  path: /callback\n  identify_by: ${body.task_id}        # Identify which workflow\n  result: ${body.result}              # Extract result\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Workflow execution flow:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-mermaid\">sequenceDiagram\n    participant W as Workflow\n    participant L as Listener&lt;br/&gt;(Port 8090)\n    participant E as External Service\n\n    Note over W,E: 1. Task Request\n    W-&gt;&gt;E: POST /api/process&lt;br/&gt;{data, callback_url: &quot;http://localhost:8090/callback&quot;}\n    E--&gt;&gt;W: 202 Accepted&lt;br/&gt;{task_id: &quot;task-123&quot;}\n\n    Note over W: 2. Waiting for Callback&lt;br/&gt;(Workflow paused)\n\n    Note over E: 3. Background Processing&lt;br/&gt;(Async task execution)\n\n    Note over E,L: 4. Callback After Completion\n    E-&gt;&gt;L: POST http://localhost:8090/callback&lt;br/&gt;{task_id: &quot;task-123&quot;, status: &quot;completed&quot;, result: {...}}\n\n    Note over L: 5. Callback Processing\n    L-&gt;&gt;L: Search waiting workflow&lt;br/&gt;by identify_by&lt;br/&gt;(task_id: &quot;task-123&quot;)\n\n    Note over L,W: 6. Result Delivery\n    L-&gt;&gt;W: Deliver result\n\n    Note over W: 7. Workflow Resumes&lt;br/&gt;(Execute next step)\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Step-by-step explanation:</strong></p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Workflow start</strong>: Send request to external service (including callback URL)</li>\n<li><strong>Immediate response</strong>: External service returns task ID</li>\n<li><strong>Waiting state</strong>: Workflow pauses waiting for callback</li>\n<li><strong>Background processing</strong>: External service performs async task</li>\n<li><strong>Callback sent</strong>: After completion, sends result to callback URL</li>\n<li><strong>Listener receives</strong>: Listener receives callback and finds workflow using <code>identify_by</code></li>\n<li><strong>Workflow resumes</strong>: Delivers result to workflow and executes next step</li>\n</ol>\n<p><strong>Important</strong>: Listeners only run on local ports. To access from external sources, you need a <strong>gateway</strong> (Section 15.4). Complete examples using gateways are covered in <strong>Section 15.5</strong>.</p>\n<h3>15.2.8 Callback Data Mapping</h3>\n<p>Listeners can extract and map various fields from callback requests.</p>\n<p><strong>Single field extraction:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  path: /webhook\n  identify_by: ${body.task_id}\n  result: ${body.output.url}          # Nested field access\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Multiple field extraction:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  path: /webhook\n  identify_by: ${body.task_id}\n  result:\n    url: ${body.output.url}\n    width: ${body.output.width}\n    height: ${body.output.height}\n    size: ${body.output.file_size}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Using query parameters:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  path: /webhook\n  identify_by: ${query.task_id}       # Extract from URL query\n  result: ${body}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Callback request example:</p>\n<pre><code>POST http://localhost:8090/webhook?task_id=task-123\nContent-Type: application/json\n\n{\n  &quot;status&quot;: &quot;completed&quot;,\n  &quot;output&quot;: {\n    &quot;url&quot;: &quot;https://example.com/result.png&quot;\n  }\n}\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>15.3 HTTP Trigger Listener</h2>\n<p>HTTP Trigger listeners receive HTTP requests from external sources and immediately start workflows. Can be used as REST API endpoints or webhook receivers.</p>\n<h3>15.3.1 HTTP Trigger Overview</h3>\n<p>HTTP Triggers are useful in these situations:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Receiving webhooks from external systems (GitHub, Slack, Discord, etc.)</li>\n<li>Providing REST API endpoints</li>\n<li>Manually triggering workflows</li>\n<li>Event-driven automation needs</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Difference from HTTP Callback:</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>HTTP Callback: Deliver results to already running workflows</li>\n<li>HTTP Trigger: Start new workflow instances</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>15.3.2 Basic HTTP Trigger Configuration</h3>\n<p><strong>Simple trigger listener:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-trigger\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8091\n  path: /trigger/my-workflow\n  method: POST\n  workflow: my-workflow\n  input:\n    data: ${body.data}\n</code></pre>\n<p>This creates an endpoint at <code>http://0.0.0.0:8091/trigger/my-workflow</code> that starts <code>my-workflow</code> when receiving a POST request.</p>\n<h3>15.3.3 Trigger Endpoint Configuration</h3>\n<p><strong>Single trigger endpoint:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-trigger\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8091\n  path: /webhooks/deploy\n  method: POST\n  workflow: deployment-workflow\n  input:\n    repo: ${body.repository.name}\n    branch: ${body.ref}\n    commit: ${body.head_commit.id}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Multiple trigger endpoints:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-trigger\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8091\n  base_path: /api\n  triggers:\n    # GitHub push event\n    - path: /github/push\n      method: POST\n      workflow: ci-build\n      input:\n        repository: ${body.repository.name}\n        branch: ${body.ref}\n        pusher: ${body.pusher.name}\n\n    # Slack slash command\n    - path: /slack/command\n      method: POST\n      workflow: slack-handler\n      input:\n        command: ${body.command}\n        text: ${body.text}\n        user: ${body.user_name}\n        channel: ${body.channel_id}\n\n    # Manual trigger\n    - path: /manual/process\n      method: POST\n      workflow: data-processing\n      input:\n        file_url: ${body.file_url}\n        options: ${body.options}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>15.3.4 Trigger Field Descriptions</h3>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Field</th>\n<th>Description</th>\n<th>Required</th>\n<th>Default</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code>path</code></td>\n<td>Trigger endpoint path</td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>-</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>method</code></td>\n<td>HTTP method</td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td><code>POST</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>workflow</code></td>\n<td>Workflow ID to execute</td>\n<td>Yes</td>\n<td>-</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>input</code></td>\n<td>Workflow input mapping</td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>Entire body</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>bulk</code></td>\n<td>Execute multiple workflows in single request</td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td><code>false</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><code>item</code></td>\n<td>Item extraction path in bulk mode</td>\n<td>No</td>\n<td>-</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>15.3.5 Bulk Trigger Processing</h3>\n<p>When processing multiple items at once, executing a workflow for each:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-trigger\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8091\n  path: /batch/process\n  method: POST\n  bulk: true\n  item: ${body.items}\n  workflow: item-processor\n  input:\n    item_id: ${item.id}\n    data: ${item.data}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Request example:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n  &quot;items&quot;: [\n    {&quot;id&quot;: &quot;item-1&quot;, &quot;data&quot;: {&quot;name&quot;: &quot;Product A&quot;}},\n    {&quot;id&quot;: &quot;item-2&quot;, &quot;data&quot;: {&quot;name&quot;: &quot;Product B&quot;}},\n    {&quot;id&quot;: &quot;item-3&quot;, &quot;data&quot;: {&quot;name&quot;: &quot;Product C&quot;}}\n  ]\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p>This request starts 3 separate workflow instances.</p>\n<h3>15.3.6 How HTTP Trigger Works</h3>\n<p><strong>Basic structure:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-trigger\n  port: 8091\n  path: /webhook\n  workflow: my-workflow\n  input:\n    data: ${body.data}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Execution flow:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-mermaid\">sequenceDiagram\n    participant E as External System\n    participant T as HTTP Trigger&lt;br/&gt;(Port 8091)\n    participant W as Workflow Engine\n\n    Note over E,W: 1. Receive HTTP request\n    E-&gt;&gt;T: POST http://localhost:8091/webhook&lt;br/&gt;{data: &quot;example&quot;}\n\n    Note over T: 2. Input mapping\n    T-&gt;&gt;T: input.data = body.data\n\n    Note over T,W: 3. Start workflow\n    T-&gt;&gt;W: run_workflow(&quot;my-workflow&quot;, {data: &quot;example&quot;})\n\n    Note over W: 4. Execute workflow&lt;br/&gt;(async, background)\n\n    Note over T,E: 5. Immediate response\n    T--&gt;&gt;E: 200 OK&lt;br/&gt;{status: &quot;triggered&quot;}\n\n    Note over W: 6. Workflow completes&lt;br/&gt;(runs independently of trigger)\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Step-by-step explanation:</strong></p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Receive request</strong>: External system sends HTTP request to trigger endpoint</li>\n<li><strong>Input mapping</strong>: Convert request data to workflow input according to <code>input</code> configuration</li>\n<li><strong>Start workflow</strong>: Start new workflow instance asynchronously</li>\n<li><strong>Immediate response</strong>: Return response immediately without waiting for workflow completion</li>\n<li><strong>Background execution</strong>: Workflow runs independently to completion</li>\n</ol>\n<p><strong>Important</strong>: HTTP Trigger only starts workflows and returns immediately. To receive workflow results, you need separate mechanisms (HTTP Callback, database queries, etc.).</p>\n<h3>15.3.7 Input Data Mapping</h3>\n<p>You can map various fields from HTTP requests to workflow inputs.</p>\n<p><strong>Body field extraction:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-trigger\n  path: /webhook\n  workflow: my-workflow\n  input:\n    name: ${body.user.name}\n    email: ${body.user.email}\n    action: ${body.action}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Using query parameters:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-trigger\n  path: /webhook\n  workflow: my-workflow\n  input:\n    token: ${query.token}\n    mode: ${query.mode}\n    data: ${body}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Request example:</p>\n<pre><code>POST http://localhost:8091/webhook?token=abc123&amp;mode=test\nContent-Type: application/json\n\n{\n  &quot;user&quot;: &quot;john&quot;,\n  &quot;action&quot;: &quot;process&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Complex mapping:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-trigger\n  path: /webhook\n  workflow: my-workflow\n  input:\n    auth:\n      token: ${query.token}\n      user: ${body.user}\n    payload:\n      data: ${body.data}\n      timestamp: ${body.timestamp}\n</code></pre>\n<h3>15.3.8 Practical Examples</h3>\n<p><strong>GitHub Webhook handling:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-trigger\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8091\n  path: /github/webhook\n  method: POST\n  workflow: github-ci\n  input:\n    event: ${body.action}\n    repository: ${body.repository.full_name}\n    branch: ${body.pull_request.head.ref}\n    author: ${body.pull_request.user.login}\n\nworkflow:\n  id: github-ci\n  title: GitHub CI Pipeline\n  jobs:\n    - id: checkout\n      component: git-clone\n      input:\n        repo: ${input.repository}\n        branch: ${input.branch}\n\n    - id: test\n      component: run-tests\n      depends_on: [checkout]\n\n    - id: notify\n      component: github-status\n      depends_on: [test]\n      input:\n        status: ${jobs.test.output.success}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Slack Webhook handling:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">listener:\n  type: http-trigger\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8091\n  path: /slack/events\n  method: POST\n  workflow: slack-bot\n  input:\n    event_type: ${body.event.type}\n    user: ${body.event.user}\n    channel: ${body.event.channel}\n    text: ${body.event.text}\n\nworkflow:\n  id: slack-bot\n  title: Slack Bot Handler\n  jobs:\n    - id: process-message\n      component: nlp-analyzer\n      input:\n        text: ${input.text}\n\n    - id: reply\n      component: slack-client\n      depends_on: [process-message]\n      input:\n        channel: ${input.channel}\n        text: &quot;Processing complete: ${jobs.process-message.output.result}&quot;\n</code></pre>\n<hr />\n<h2>15.4 Gateways - HTTP Tunneling</h2>\n<p>Gateways are tunneling services for exposing locally running services to the internet. Useful for testing webhooks in development or when external access to local services is needed.</p>\n<h3>15.4.1 Gateway Overview</h3>\n<p>Gateways are needed in these scenarios:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Testing external webhooks in local development</li>\n<li>Exposing services behind firewalls</li>\n<li>Temporary public URLs needed</li>\n<li>External services require callback URLs</li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Supported gateways:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Type</th>\n<th>Features</th>\n<th>Use Cases</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>HTTP Tunnel (ngrok)</strong></td>\n<td>Easy setup, temporary URLs</td>\n<td>Local development, quick testing</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>HTTP Tunnel (Cloudflare)</strong></td>\n<td>Free unlimited, high reliability</td>\n<td>Local development, continuous testing</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td><strong>SSH Tunnel</strong></td>\n<td>Own server, fixed addresses</td>\n<td>Enterprise environments, production-ready</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>15.4.2 HTTP Tunnel - ngrok</h3>\n<p>ngrok is a tunneling service that exposes local servers with public URLs.</p>\n<p><strong>Basic configuration (single port):</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: ngrok\n  port: 8080  # Local port to tunnel\n</code></pre>\n<p>This exposes local port 8080 through ngrok public URL.</p>\n<p><strong>Multiple ports configuration:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: ngrok\n  port:\n    - 8080  # First local port\n    - 8090  # Second local port\n    - 3000  # Third local port\n</code></pre>\n<p>Each port gets its own unique public URL (e.g., <code>https://abc123.ngrok.io</code>, <code>https://def456.ngrok.io</code>, <code>https://ghi789.ngrok.io</code>).</p>\n<p><strong>Complete example with single port:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: ngrok\n  port: 8090  # Same as listener port\n\nlistener:\n  type: http-callback\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8090\n  path: /callback\n  identify_by: ${body.task_id}\n  result: ${body.result}\n\ncomponents:\n  external-service:\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.external-service.com\n    action:\n      path: /process\n      method: POST\n      body:\n        data: ${input.data}\n        # Use gateway:8090.public_url to access public URL\n        callback_url: ${gateway:8090.public_url}/callback\n        callback_id: ${context.run_id}\n      output: ${response}\n\nworkflow:\n  title: External Service with Gateway\n  jobs:\n    - id: process\n      component: external-service\n      input: ${input}\n      output: ${output}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Example with multiple ports:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: ngrok\n  port:\n    - 8090  # Callback listener\n    - 8091  # Status webhook\n    - 8092  # Admin interface\n\ncomponents:\n  external-service:\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.external-service.com\n    action:\n      path: /process\n      method: POST\n      body:\n        data: ${input.data}\n        callback_url: ${gateway:8090.public_url}/callback\n        status_url: ${gateway:8091.public_url}/status\n        admin_url: ${gateway:8092.public_url}/admin\n      output: ${response}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Accessing gateway URLs:</strong></p>\n<p>The format <code>${gateway:PORT.public_url}</code> provides the public URL for each exposed port:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>${gateway:8090.public_url}</code> → <code>https://abc123.ngrok.io</code></li>\n<li><code>${gateway:8091.public_url}</code> → <code>https://def456.ngrok.io</code></li>\n<li><code>${gateway:8092.public_url}</code> → <code>https://ghi789.ngrok.io</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>Execution flow:</strong></p>\n<ol>\n<li>Gateway starts: ngrok exposes local port(s) with public URL(s)</li>\n<li>Listener starts: Waiting for callbacks on configured port(s)</li>\n<li>Workflow executes: <code>${gateway:PORT.public_url}</code> is replaced with actual public URL</li>\n<li>Callback URL sent to external service</li>\n<li>External service sends callback to public URL after completion</li>\n<li>ngrok forwards request to corresponding local port</li>\n<li>Listener receives callback and delivers result to workflow</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>15.4.3 HTTP Tunnel - Cloudflare</h3>\n<p>Cloudflare Tunnel (formerly Argo Tunnel) is a stable tunneling service available for free with unlimited bandwidth.</p>\n<p><strong>Basic configuration (single port):</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: cloudflare\n  port: 8080  # Local port to tunnel\n</code></pre>\n<p>This exposes local port 8080 through Cloudflare Tunnel public URL.</p>\n<p><strong>Multiple ports configuration:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: cloudflare\n  port:\n    - 8080  # First local port\n    - 8090  # Second local port\n    - 3000  # Third local port\n</code></pre>\n<p>Each port gets its own unique public URL (e.g., <code>https://abc-def.trycloudflare.com</code>, <code>https://ghi-jkl.trycloudflare.com</code>, <code>https://mno-pqr.trycloudflare.com</code>).</p>\n<p><strong>Complete example with callback:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: cloudflare\n  port: 8090\n\nlistener:\n  type: http-callback\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8090\n  path: /callback\n  identify_by: ${body.task_id}\n  result: ${body.result}\n\ncomponents:\n  external-service:\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.external-service.com\n    action:\n      path: /process\n      method: POST\n      body:\n        data: ${input.data}\n        # Use gateway:8090.public_url to access public URL\n        callback_url: ${gateway:8090.public_url}/callback\n        callback_id: ${context.run_id}\n      output: ${response}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Example with multiple ports:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: cloudflare\n  port:\n    - 8090  # Callback listener\n    - 8091  # Status webhook\n    - 3000  # Frontend application\n\ncomponents:\n  external-service:\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.external-service.com\n    action:\n      path: /process\n      method: POST\n      body:\n        data: ${input.data}\n        callback_url: ${gateway:8090.public_url}/callback\n        status_url: ${gateway:8091.public_url}/status\n        app_url: ${gateway:3000.public_url}\n      output: ${response}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Accessing gateway URLs:</strong></p>\n<p>The format <code>${gateway:PORT.public_url}</code> provides the public URL for each exposed port:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>${gateway:8090.public_url}</code> → <code>https://abc-def.trycloudflare.com</code></li>\n<li><code>${gateway:8091.public_url}</code> → <code>https://ghi-jkl.trycloudflare.com</code></li>\n<li><code>${gateway:3000.public_url}</code> → <code>https://mno-pqr.trycloudflare.com</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p><strong>ngrok vs Cloudflare comparison:</strong></p>\n<table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Feature</th>\n<th>ngrok</th>\n<th>Cloudflare</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td>Free plan</td>\n<td>Limited (request limit per hour)</td>\n<td>Unlimited</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Setup difficulty</td>\n<td>Easy</td>\n<td>Medium (account required)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>URL format</td>\n<td><code>https://random.ngrok.io</code></td>\n<td><code>https://random.trycloudflare.com</code></td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Stability</td>\n<td>High</td>\n<td>Very high</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>Speed</td>\n<td>Fast</td>\n<td>Very fast</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td>URL lifetime</td>\n<td>Session-based</td>\n<td>Session-based</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>15.4.4 SSH Tunnel</h3>\n<p>Use SSH reverse tunnels to expose local services through remote servers.</p>\n<p><strong>SSH key authentication:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: ssh-tunnel\n  port:\n    - &quot;9834:8090&quot;  # Remote port 9834 -&gt; Local port 8090\n  connection:\n    host: remote-server.com\n    port: 22\n    auth:\n      type: keyfile\n      username: user\n      keyfile: ~/.ssh/id_rsa\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>SSH password authentication:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: ssh-tunnel\n  port:\n    - &quot;9834:8090&quot;  # Remote port 9834 -&gt; Local port 8090\n  connection:\n    host: remote-server.com\n    port: 22\n    auth:\n      type: password\n      username: user\n      password: ${env.SSH_PASSWORD}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Port forwarding formats:</strong></p>\n<p>The <code>port</code> field supports multiple flexible formats:</p>\n<ol>\n<li><strong>Integer</strong>: <code>8090</code> → Forwards remote port 8090 to localhost:8090</li>\n<li><strong>Port:Port</strong>: <code>&quot;9834:8090&quot;</code> → Forwards remote port 9834 to localhost:8090</li>\n<li><strong>Port:Host</strong>: <code>&quot;8090:192.168.1.107&quot;</code> → Forwards remote port 8090 to 192.168.1.107:8090</li>\n<li><strong>Port:Host:Port</strong>: <code>&quot;9834:192.168.1.107:3000&quot;</code> → Forwards remote port 9834 to 192.168.1.107:3000</li>\n</ol>\n<p><strong>Multiple port forwarding:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: ssh-tunnel\n  port:\n    - &quot;9834:8090&quot;  # Remote 9834 -&gt; localhost:8090\n    - &quot;9835:8091&quot;  # Remote 9835 -&gt; localhost:8091\n    - &quot;9836:8092&quot;  # Remote 9836 -&gt; localhost:8092\n  connection:\n    host: remote-server.com\n    port: 22\n    auth:\n      type: keyfile\n      username: user\n      keyfile: ~/.ssh/id_rsa\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Forwarding to other hosts in local network:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: ssh-tunnel\n  port:\n    - &quot;8080:192.168.1.107&quot;       # Remote 8080 -&gt; 192.168.1.107:8080\n    - &quot;9834:192.168.1.107:3000&quot;  # Remote 9834 -&gt; 192.168.1.107:3000\n    - &quot;9835:example.local:8090&quot;  # Remote 9835 -&gt; example.local:8090\n  connection:\n    host: remote-server.com\n    port: 22\n    auth:\n      type: keyfile\n      username: user\n      keyfile: ~/.ssh/id_rsa\n</code></pre>\n<p>This is useful for exposing services running on other machines in your local network.</p>\n<p><strong>Simple port setup (same local and remote port):</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: ssh-tunnel\n  port: 8090  # Remote port 8090 -&gt; localhost:8090\n  connection:\n    host: remote-server.com\n    port: 22\n    auth:\n      type: keyfile\n      username: user\n      keyfile: ~/.ssh/id_rsa\n</code></pre>\n<p>SSH tunnels are useful when:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Using custom domains</li>\n<li>Firewalls block ngrok/Cloudflare</li>\n<li>Corporate environments require approved servers only</li>\n<li>Fixed IP addresses or ports are needed</li>\n<li>Exposing services on other machines in local network</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>15.4.5 Advanced Gateway Configuration</h3>\n<p><strong>Runtime configuration:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: ngrok\n  runtime: native  # or docker\n  port: 8080\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Using gateway variables:</strong></p>\n<p>When gateway is configured, these variables are available:</p>\n<p><strong>HTTP Tunnel (ngrok, Cloudflare):</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: ngrok\n  port: 8080\n\ncomponents:\n  service:\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      body:\n        # Use public URL (gateway:port.public_url format)\n        webhook_url: ${gateway:8080.public_url}/webhook\n        # Example: https://abc123.ngrok.io/webhook\n\n        # Port information\n        local_port: ${gateway:8080.port}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>SSH Tunnel:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: ssh-tunnel\n  port:\n    - &quot;9834:8090&quot;\n  connection:\n    host: remote-server.com\n    port: 22\n    auth:\n      type: keyfile\n      username: user\n      keyfile: ~/.ssh/id_rsa\n\ncomponents:\n  service:\n    type: http-client\n    action:\n      body:\n        # Use public address (gateway:local_port.public_address format)\n        webhook_url: http://${gateway:8090.public_address}/webhook\n        # Example: http://remote-server.com:9834/webhook\n</code></pre>\n<h3>15.4.6 Real-world Example: SSH Tunnel</h3>\n<p><strong>Callback reception via SSH tunnel:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: ssh-tunnel\n  port:\n    - &quot;9834:8090&quot;  # Remote port 9834 -&gt; Local port 8090\n  connection:\n    host: ${env.SSH_TUNNEL_HOST}\n    port: ${env.SSH_TUNNEL_PORT | 22}\n    auth:\n      type: keyfile\n      username: ${env.SSH_USERNAME}\n      keyfile: ${env.SSH_KEYFILE | ~/.ssh/id_rsa}\n\nlistener:\n  type: http-callback\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8090\n  path: /callback\n  identify_by: ${body.task_id}\n  result: ${body.result}\n\ncomponent:\n  type: http-client\n  base_url: https://api.external-service.com\n  action:\n    path: /process\n    method: POST\n    headers:\n      Content-Type: application/json\n    body:\n      data: ${input.data}\n      # Use SSH tunnel's public address\n      callback_url: http://${gateway:8090.public_address}/callback\n      task_id: ${context.run_id}\n    output:\n      task_id: ${response.task_id}\n      result: ${result as json}\n  completion:\n    type: callback\n    wait_for: ${context.run_id}\n\nworkflow:\n  title: SSH Tunnel Gateway Example\n  description: Expose local callback listener to external services using SSH tunnel\n  input: ${input}\n  output: ${output}\n</code></pre>\n<p><strong>Environment variable setup:</strong></p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">export SSH_TUNNEL_HOST=&quot;remote-server.com&quot;\nexport SSH_TUNNEL_PORT=22\nexport SSH_USERNAME=&quot;user&quot;\nexport SSH_KEYFILE=&quot;~/.ssh/id_rsa&quot;\n\nmodel-compose up\n</code></pre>\n<p>This setup works as follows:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Listener runs on local port 8090</li>\n<li>SSH tunnel forwards remote server's port 9834 to local port 8090</li>\n<li>External service sends callback to <code>http://remote-server.com:9834/callback</code></li>\n<li>SSH tunnel forwards the request to local port 8090</li>\n<li>Listener receives callback and delivers result to workflow</li>\n</ol>\n<h3>15.4.7 Real-world Example: Slack Bot Webhook</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: cloudflare\n  port: 8090  # Same as listener port\n\nlistener:\n  type: http-callback\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8090\n  base_path: /slack\n  callbacks:\n    - path: /events\n      method: POST\n      identify_by: ${body.event.client_msg_id}\n      result: ${body.event}\n\ncomponents:\n  slack-responder:\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://slack.com/api\n    action:\n      path: /chat.postMessage\n      method: POST\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}\n        Content-Type: application/json\n      body:\n        channel: ${input.channel}\n        text: ${input.text}\n      output: ${response}\n\nworkflow:\n  title: Slack Event Handler\n  jobs:\n    - id: respond\n      component: slack-responder\n      input:\n        channel: ${input.event.channel}\n        text: &quot;Processing complete: ${input.event.text}&quot;\n      output: ${output}\n</code></pre>\n<p>Slack app setup:</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Create Slack app (<a href=\"https://api.slack.com/apps\">https://api.slack.com/apps</a>)</li>\n<li>Run <code>model-compose up</code> and check gateway logs for public URL</li>\n<li>Enable Event Subscriptions</li>\n<li>Enter gateway public URL + listener path in Request URL (e.g., <code>https://abc123.trycloudflare.com/slack/events</code>)</li>\n<li>Issue bot token and set <code>SLACK_BOT_TOKEN</code> environment variable</li>\n</ol>\n<hr />\n<h2>15.5 Using Listeners and Gateways Together</h2>\n<p>Using listeners and gateways together allows safe testing of external webhooks in local environments.</p>\n<h3>15.5.1 Integration Example: Async Image Processing</h3>\n<pre><code class=\"language-yaml\">gateway:\n  type: http-tunnel\n  driver: ngrok\n  port: 8090  # Same as listener port\n\nlistener:\n  type: http-callback\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8090\n  base_path: /webhooks\n  max_concurrent_count: 5\n  callbacks:\n    - path: /image/completed\n      method: POST\n      identify_by: ${body.task_id}\n      status: ${body.status}\n      success_when: [&quot;completed&quot;, &quot;success&quot;]\n      fail_when: [&quot;failed&quot;, &quot;error&quot;]\n      result:\n        url: ${body.output.url}\n        width: ${body.output.width}\n        height: ${body.output.height}\n\ncomponents:\n  image-generator:\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.image-ai.com/v1\n    action:\n      path: /generate\n      method: POST\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.IMAGE_AI_KEY}\n      body:\n        prompt: ${input.prompt}\n        size: ${input.size | &quot;1024x1024&quot;}\n        # Gateway public URL + listener path\n        callback_url: ${gateway:8090.public_url}/webhooks/image/completed\n        task_id: ${context.run_id}\n      output:\n        task_id: ${response.task_id}\n        status: ${response.status}\n\n  image-optimizer:\n    type: http-client\n    base_url: https://api.imageoptim.com\n    action:\n      path: /optimize\n      method: POST\n      headers:\n        Authorization: Bearer ${env.IMAGEOPTIM_KEY}\n      body:\n        url: ${input.url}\n        quality: 85\n      output:\n        optimized_url: ${response.url}\n        original_size: ${response.original_size}\n        compressed_size: ${response.compressed_size}\n\nworkflow:\n  title: Image Generation and Optimization\n  description: Generate image with AI and optimize it\n  jobs:\n    # Step 1: AI image generation (async)\n    - id: generate\n      component: image-generator\n      input:\n        prompt: ${input.prompt}\n        size: ${input.size}\n      output:\n        task_id: ${output.task_id}\n        image_url: ${output.url}  #
